builds.title: Every UI element is a named asset
builds.detail:
Apply the rule across schemas/asset-types.json, the web and Android ports, the 39 starter assets and the conformance fixtures.

- Two tiers: element assets (button, slider, toggle, input, icon, label...) and parent assets (toolbar, menu, nav, app menu, dialog, container, window). A standalone element in a layout is its own named asset; groups only exist inside a parent asset.
- Namespaced ids for every asset (e.g. axf.button.save, axf.toolbar.editor); layouts and parents reference ids.
- Split instance (label, icon, action, state) from skin (style asset + theme tokens).
- Slots with type contracts in layout regions and parents; hot-swap and drag-and-drop = rebinding a slot to a compatible asset id.
- Kernel unchanged (open type registry).

notes.text: Overlaps settings-asset (new `settings` asset type, branch claude/project-thread-55oakl); build with settings-asset-fable.
Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Design note first: write `_claude/memory/docs/named-assets.md` — the two tiers (element assets: button, slider, toggle, input, icon, label; parent assets: toolbar, menu, nav, app-menu, dialog, container, window), the id namespace rule (`<ns>.<type>.<name>`, e.g. `axf.button.save`), instance vs skin split, and which existing starter ids change. List every file the rule touches. No code.

BRETT: review the design note. Decide (a) whether existing starter ids are renamed in place or aliased (old id keeps resolving), (b) whether element assets are required for every control or opt-in per app. Record both answers in the note and in `_claude/memory/decisions.md`.

Schema: in `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` add `"tier": "element" | "parent"` to every type and a top-level `idRule` (regex, documented) for namespaced ids; keep `optional: true` on new fields so old apps validate. Run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs schemas` and `axf validate --framework` — both must pass unchanged.

Validator (web): `framework/core/validate.ts` → `validateAsset` warns (not errors, until the switch flips) when an id does not match `idRule`; add `assetTier(type)`. Add 4 cases to `framework/spec/fixtures/validation.json` (good namespaced id, bare id, element, parent). `npx -y tsx framework/spec/gen-fixtures.mts` then CI check.

Validator (Kotlin + CLI): mirror the id rule in `framework/android/axf-kernel/.../asset/` validator and in the build-engine validator (`framework/cli/build-engine.mjs` validateAsset). Same fixture cases replayed by `ConformanceTest` (written without a compiler: check the "CI build errors" issue after push).

Element asset types, part 1: add `toggle`, `input`, `icon` as `tier: element` types in `asset-types.json` (data shape: label, icon, action, state keys; skin = style-theme tokens only). One starter each under `framework/assets/<type>/`. `axf validate --framework` passes.

Element asset types, part 2: mark the existing `button`, `slider`, `label` as `tier: element`; add the instance/skin split to their spec (`data.instance` {label, icon, action, state} vs `data.skin` {style tokens}) with the old flat shape still accepted by `asEnvelope` normalisation. Fixture cases in `components.json`.

Parent slots: in `asset-types.json` give every parent type (toolbar, app-menu, nav-menu, context-menu, dialog, container, window) a `slots` block like `layout.slots` (named slots + accepted element types), reusing `compileSlots`/`regionAccepts` from `framework/core/engines/layout.ts`. Fixture cases in `layout-slots.json` for one parent.

Rebinding = hot-swap: `framework/core/runtime.ts` gets `bindSlot(parentType, parentId, slot, elementId)` / `unbindSlot` (stored like `attachToHost` in `widgets.ts`, settings key `axf.bind.<parent>.<slot>`); `swap()` of a parent keeps bindings whose types still fit. Unit cases in `widgets.json` → `bindings`.

Kotlin runtime parity: `AxfRuntime.bindSlot/unbindSlot` + KV `<key>:bind` in the kernel, same rules as the TS version, replaying the `bindings` fixture in `ConformanceTest`. Written without a compiler; push and read the CI issue.

Rename the 39 starter assets to namespaced ids (`axf.<type>.<name>`) with the alias map chosen in step 2 (`framework/assets/aliases.json`, read by `registry.ts` + Kotlin `AssetRegistry`): every app manifest and `framework/defaults.json` still resolve. `axf validate --framework` + `validate apps/demo` + console `npm run build` pass.

React layer: `framework/react/components/Controls.tsx` renders an element asset by id (`<AssetButton id>` etc.) reading instance + skin; a standalone element in a layout region renders through the same path. Element Explorer (`react/studio/Inspector.tsx`) shows tier + bindings.

Compose layer: `axf-ui/components/Buttons.kt`, `Slider.kt`, `Controls.kt` take an element asset id the same way; `ElementExplorer.kt` shows tier + bindings. Android console showcase renders one bound element in its toolbar.

Flip the switch: `idRule` violations become errors for apps with `frameworkVersion` ≥ the new one (old apps keep warnings), `axf init` writes namespaced ids, templates updated. Run the CI template sweep locally (`axf init` for react-ts, next-ts, android-compose + validate).

Docs + close: `framework/spec/PORTING.md` section "Named assets"; CLAUDE.md Status bullet; decisions.md entry; mark the pending item complete and the plan feature built; differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/named-asset-rule.md` (rule for rebuilds).

steps.text: Plugin skeleton: copy `apps/console-web/plugins/_template` to `plugins/asset-designer` (id `ai.amberx.axf.console.asset-designer`, `uiEditor: "builder"`, lifecycle block, `install.mjs`/`uninstall.mjs`), nav → Plugins → Asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab (parent `plugins`). `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check asset-designer` passes; console tsc + vite build pass.

Designer shell `web/Designer.tsx`: type picker (every non-attachable type from `asset-types.json` the designer covers: nav-menu, drawer, app-menu, context-menu, toolbar, layout, style-theme, color-theme), id + label fields, Save/Cancel; `useEditorSync()` so it reloads values on focus (UI-editor rule). Saves nothing yet.

Validation gate: every save runs `validateAsset` from the baked `src/axf/core/validate.ts`; errors shown inline next to the field they name; Save disabled until clean. Server route `POST /api/plugins/asset-designer/validate` mirrors it with the CLI validator (`framework/core/project-check.mjs` pattern). Test in `test.py`.

Built-in ids refused.

Menu editor (nav-menu, app-menu, context-menu): tree of items (label, icon, action, children, divider), drag to reorder, action picker from `rt.actions.list()`, live preview via `rt.swap` on a `ad-preview-<type>` id. Reuses `MenuList.tsx` for the preview.

Toolbar editor: items (icon, label, action, badge counter), `density`/`surface`/`divider`/`collapsible`, widgets start/end picker from `attachable` types (engine-rpc `app-defaults` → `widgets`), live preview through the React `Toolbar`.

`drawer` asset type: add it to `asset-types.json` (hideable chrome, `side` left/right, `width`, `items` like nav-menu, `modal`), `layout.slots` accept it in the `drawer` region, starter `framework/assets/drawer/amberx-side.json`, `framework/defaults.json` names it. Validators on all three ports accept it (Kotlin: `AssetTypeSpec` resource); fixture case in `layout-slots.json`.

Drawer rendering: React `components/Chrome.tsx` draws the drawer region; Compose `axf-ui/components/Chrome.kt` the same (swipe from the edge, scrim from `--fx-opacity-scrim`). Drawer editor in the designer (same editor as nav-menu plus side/width/modal).

Layout editor: region grid (9 regions from `layout.slots`), per-region size/visibility, `data.slots` overrides with accepted-type chips; preview through `compileLayout`. Hidden slots greyed like Appearance does.

Color-theme editor: token groups from the theme engine (`core/engines/theme.ts` token list), colour pickers, contrast warnings (reuse `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks), light/dark pair, preview via `rt.swap`.
Style-theme editor: space, radii, borders, font sizes, opacity tokens (`opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass`), density; preview; numbers clamped to the ranges known themes use.

Templates hook: "Start from" picker listing starters + designed assets + (later) `x.assets.templates` entries; Duplicate / Rename / Export JSON / Import JSON (validated). Export writes a file a user can drop into an app's assets folder.

Installed by default: plugin `enabled: true` in the console's plugin defaults, `framework/catalog/plugins.json` entry (planned → built resolves by itself), `node framework/cli/plugins.mjs --check`, status.json + tracker; Plugin Manager shows it.

Android face (first slice): `axf-devtools` gets an `AssetDesignerModule` placeholder route `asset-designer` listing designed assets received from the console (read-only), so the plugin-inventory shows it on both ports; full editors stay web-only for now (noted as a placeholder capability `axf.designer`).

Tests: plugin `test.py` (validate route, storage, built-in id refused, lifecycle), web unit cases for the drawer slot + layout compile, CI line; `uninstall.mjs --all` leaves nothing (`check --after-uninstall`).

Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-designer.md` (new plugin, so a build report), LOG.md line, web screenshots via `rebuild-shots.mjs`, CLAUDE.md Status, plan epic `x.assets.designer` built via `build_step`, pending item complete.

builds.title: Asset Browser plugin
builds.detail: Browse, preview, import, export and hot-swap assets across apps built on AXF. Installed by default.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Plugin skeleton `apps/console-web/plugins/asset-browser` from `_template` (id `ai.amberx.axf.console.asset-browser`, lifecycle, install/uninstall, nav → Plugins → Asset browser, settings sub-tab). Lifecycle check + console build pass.

Sources: server route `GET /api/plugins/asset-browser/sources` lists asset folders it may read: framework starters (`framework/assets`), every app under `apps/*/src/assets` or `app/src/main/assets/axf` (from `framework/cli/app-bundle.mjs list`), designed assets (asset-designer dataDir when present). Never follows symlinks; roots only.
Browse view: grid by type → source → asset, search box (reuses `consoleSearch.ts` provider pattern), type chips from `asset-types.json`, counts per source. Rows show id, label, origin, tier.

builds.title: Port engine: bring a non-AXF app onto AmberX AXF (bake or rebuild)
builds.detail:
Runs the ports that claude-project parks (pending items port-<name>, manifest x.port, plan in the project at _claude/memory/docs/port-to-axf.md). Brett chose: ask each time between the two ways.

- bake: keep the codebase, run axf init into it (react-ts / next-ts / android-compose), then move its look and chrome into asset@1 assets step by step (colour/style themes, menus, toolbars, nav, dialogs, layout with region slots); UI reads engine tokens only (THEMING.md). Old styles go as each piece moves.
- rebuild: new AXF app from the closest boilerplate (axf boilerplates), old code kept alongside as reference, rebuilt feature by feature on assets/libraries/plugins.

Deliver: axf port <dir> --mode bake|rebuild (analysis report: what maps to which asset types, libraries, plugins; then staged codemods like ui-port.mjs does for UI kits), console + MCP drivers, manifest relation none -> built-on when it starts, fixtures/tests. First real targets: xGallery (MossesX/xGallery, React 19 + Express + SQLite) and whatever claude-project parks.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.said: ask each time between the two ways.

steps.text: Spec first: `_claude/memory/docs/port-engine.md` — the two modes (bake / rebuild), the analysis report shape (`port-report@1`: stack, UI kit found, screens, chrome pieces → asset types, styles → tokens, libraries/plugins suggested, risk list), the staged codemod plan, and what `axf port` refuses (no manifest, dirty git tree). Read `framework/cli/ui-port.mjs` and `claude-project.mjs` first.

CLI entry: `framework/cli/port.mjs` + `axf port <dir> --mode bake|rebuild [--report-only] [--stage N]` in `axf.mjs`; `requireProject` gate; refuses without `--yes` when git is dirty; writes `port-report.json` next to the manifest. `--report-only` works on an empty folder (empty report).

Stack detection: reuse `claude-project.mjs` detection (react/next/android/python…), add UI-kit detection (MUI, Chakra, shadcn, Material3, Compose, Tailwind) by package.json / gradle deps; unit test with fixture folders under `framework/spec/fixtures/port/`.

Analysis, screens + chrome: scan routes/screens (React Router / Next pages / Compose NavHost) and chrome components (app bar, drawer, bottom nav, menus, toolbars, dialogs) → candidate asset list with target type and confidence. Report section `pieces`.

Analysis, styles → tokens: run `portSource` from `ui-port.mjs` in dry mode over the codebase to count colour/size literals and role usages; map to the token list from the theme engine; report `tokens` with unmapped literals. Cap files scanned (size + count) and skip node_modules/build.

Bake, stage 1: `axf init` into the existing project (template by stack) without overwriting app files (`src/axf/` + assets + manifest relation `built-on`), `axf.lock.json`; app still builds (the template guard allows an existing codebase). Checked with a fixture react app.

Bake, stage 2: themes — generate `color-theme` + `style-theme` assets from the detected palette (nearest tokens), apply the literal → `var(--fx-*)` codemod (`ui-port.mjs portSource`) to CSS/TSX/Kotlin files in place with a `.port-backup/`; `--stage 2` only; report lists every file changed.

Bake, stage 3: chrome — generate nav-menu / app-menu / toolbar / dialog assets from the detected pieces and swap the components for the framework ones (`AppShell` / Compose `AppShell`), old components kept under `legacy/` until removed; `--stage 3`.

Rebuild mode: pick the closest boilerplate (`framework/boilerplates/index.json` tags vs detected features), `axf init --boilerplate` into `<dir>-axf` beside the old code, write `PORT-PLAN.md` with screen-by-screen mapping and the old file for each; report `rebuild.plan`.

Drivers: engine-rpc `port` / `port-report`, console `POST /api/port` + `GET /api/port/report?dir=`, MCP `app_port(dir, mode, stage)` (write, needs the console token); manifest `framework.relation` none → built-on when stage 1 runs (`project.mjs` validates).

Console view: Plugins → **Port** (or Wizards view section): pick a folder from allowed roots (project-wizard's `AXF_WIZARD_ROOTS` rule), run the report, show pieces/tokens tables, run stages one at a time with the file list and a diff count; rebuild plan rendered as a checklist.

Pending items hook: `port-<name>` items (parked by claude-project) get a "Run port" button in Pending rows (slot `pending.item`) that opens the console view on that project; `claude-project` writes `x.port.engine: "axf port"` into the manifest.
First real target, xGallery (MossesX/xGallery, React 19 + Express + SQLite): BRETT attaches the repo; run `--report-only`, review the report together, record the mode choice. No codemod yet.
xGallery bake stage 1–2 on a branch in that repo (init + themes), app builds; note unmapped literals; push branch `axf-port` for Brett to look at on the phone.
Tests: `framework/spec/check-port.mjs` over the fixture folders (detection, report shape, stage 1 idempotent, stage 2 backup + dry run, refusals: no manifest, dirty tree, symlinks); CI line.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/app-port-engine.md`, LOG.md, CLAUDE.md Status + `axf port` in Build/run/test, pending complete; decisions.md note on bake vs rebuild defaults.

builds.title: lib-clone: any AXF app clones its own install with current data
builds.detail:
Turn xGallery's New project wizard (MossesX/xGallery: server/src/routes/newproject.ts, src/pages/dev/newproject/NewProjectWizard.tsx, kit/new-project.mjs) into an AXF library so every app built on AXF can clone its install into a new project. Brett: keep the xGallery wizard as is and make it a library for AXF.

What the xGallery wizard does today (reuse the design): renamed copy from the kit, GitHub repo, per-project deploy key installed on the VPS + Actions secrets (VPS_SSH_KEY, ADMIN_PASSWORD, HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN), Hostinger DNS for site + dev panel, Claude GitHub app access, push main, wait for the site deploy, push panel, wait, first-session prompt; resumable, no secrets stored.

New for the library: clone WITH current data (database snapshot + media/files, consistent copy, secrets and sessions stripped, owner reset), the copy gets its own project.manifest.json + _claude/ (claude-project), cross-port contract (web + Android) for the clone action exposed through the interop gate (default-deny), a settings tab (plugin manager rules: no own settings screen), console + MCP drivers. Open questions for Brett at build time: which data is copied by default, and whether the clone keeps users/members.

notes.text: Oct 18 2026: the project-creation half is built as the console plugin project-wizard (Opus): repo/folder/new AXF app → GitHub/VPS/local homes → manifest, _claude/, Claude.ai project kit, all on claude-project. lib-clone still covers the cross-port library and cloning an install WITH its data; reuse wizard.mjs for the homes and kit.

origin.said: keep the xGallery wizard as is and make it a library for AXF.

steps.text: BRETT decides the two open questions before any code: (1) which data a clone copies by default (database snapshot + media? settings? sessions never), (2) whether users/members come along or the clone starts with the owner only. Write both into this item's notes and `_claude/memory/decisions.md`.

Contract `clone@1`: `framework/core/clone.ts` (TS reference) — `CloneRequest` {name, id, homes (github/vps/local like project-wizard), data: {database, media, settings, users}, stripSecrets: true}, `CloneReport`, pure validators (name/id rules from `claude-project.mjs`), exposure descriptor `clone.run` default-deny REMOTE (INTEROP.md). Fixture `spec/fixtures/clone.json` + `gen-fixtures`.

Kotlin mirror `ai.amberx.axf.kernel.clone` (same validators, `ConformanceTest` replay) + Python `framework/python/axf_libs/clone/contract.py` (used by server parts). Placeholder capability `axf.clone` declared in the kernel.

Library scaffold: `axf new-library clone --template service-provider --ports web,android,python` → `framework/libs/clone` (web `AxfWebLibrary` with a settings group "Clone", no own screen), `framework/android/lib-clone`, `framework/python/axf_libs/clone`; `axf compile-library clone` passes. Catalog `libraries.json` entry.

Data snapshot (server, Python): `axf_libs/clone/snapshot.py` — consistent copy of a SQLite db (`sqlite3 .backup`) and listed media folders into a temp dir, strip secret-looking files (reuse project-wizard's patterns), reset owner per the step-1 decision; unit test on a fixture db.

Homes + kit: reuse `apps/console-web/plugins/project-wizard/wizard.mjs` (`run`, `kit`, `link`) for GitHub/VPS/local homes, manifest, `_claude/`, Claude.ai kit; `clone` calls it with `source: folder` after the snapshot is unpacked into the new folder. One code path, no second copy of the wizard.

Web side: `framework/libs/clone/client.ts` (`CloneClient` over the app's API, token via a credential provider like `libs/mcp`), Settings → Clone group (name, id, data toggles from the decision, homes), progress stream (SSE like project-wizard), done screen with links. Gate: `rt.uac` must hold `clone.run`.

Android side: `lib-clone` `CloneModule` → Settings group + `CloneScreen` route `clone` calling the same API through axf-network; `AxfClone` registers the `axf.clone` provider; written without a compiler, CI `:lib-clone:testDebugUnitTest` with a fake server.

Console + MCP drivers: console plugin-free route `POST /api/clone` (admin only) running the Python engine; MCP `app_clone` (write, confirm required = destructive annotation); the console's own Settings → Plugins lists lib-clone like other libraries.

xGallery hook: xGallery keeps its wizard; add a `clone` endpoint there that imports `axf_libs.clone` (or calls the console API) so its New project wizard's "clone with data" uses the library — only after Brett attaches MossesX/xGallery.

Tests + CI: `framework/spec/check-clone.mts` (fixtures, validators), Python `axf_libs/clone/test.py` (snapshot strips secrets, resets owner, refuses symlinks/outside roots), lifecycle not needed (library). CI lines.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/lib-clone.md`, LOG.md, CLAUDE.md Status, `libraries.json`/tracker, pending complete.

Brett chose the wrapper over a native rewrite: the existing web console runs inside an Android app shell, same way AmberX loads its web plugins. One codebase; every console change shows on the phone at once.

Reuse AmberX's Android shell/bridge pieces (apps/amberx-droid) rather than writing new ones.

1. Android app shell loading the console (console.amberxai.com), with sign-in kept, back button/navigation, pull-to-refresh, offline screen.
2. Native bridges where needed: push notifications (build start/finish/fail/land alerts), mic for voice, background wake, file share/download (APKs), deep links that open a console screen.
3. Console UI stays asset-driven; phone layouts come from the existing three-layouts/phone assets, no hard-coded styling.
4. APK built in CI next to amberx-debug.apk; listed under Apps in the console/axHub for install.
5. UI Review with three options (--choices) for the shell chrome. Tests. Add to Shipped features.

Progress: append `<time> START|DONE <step>` to PROGRESS.md here at each step; don't stop between steps. Commit, don't push.

steps.text: Shell app scaffold: apps/console-droid (Capacitor shell, server.url console.amberxai.com, allowNavigation console + hub, project manifest, package ai.amberx.console.droid)
Shell behaviour: sign-in kept (cookie flush), back button through web history, pull-to-refresh (guarded by the page's scroll state), offline screen from tokens
Native bridge ConsoleShell plugin: downloads (APKs via DownloadManager with the session cookie, own hosts only), share sheet, deep links (axfconsole:// + https App Links → console route)
Alerts: background wake (WorkManager periodic check of /api/alerts, reusing AmberX HubRules.consoleAlerts/mutedTypes), notifications channel, quiet when AmberX is installed; mic permission for voice
Console web side: shell detection + bridge client (framework-free plugin-free module in console-web), pull-to-refresh guard, notification mode setting
CI: console-droid job (APK console-droid-debug.apk next to amberx-debug.apk, unit tests), ci-scope output, app bundle → Apps catalog
UI Review: three shell-chrome options as assets (--choices), tests, Shipped features, docs, THREADS + report

step.text: 4a. `AxfWebTab` web view composable, locked down: allowed hosts only (own domains from manifest/settings), refuse other links with a toast (never the outside browser), JavaScript on, file access off, popups off, geolocation off, mixed content blocked; unit test of the allow rule (pure function `hostAllowed`).

4b. `AxfWebTab` state: one WebView per tab, lazily created, retained across recompositions (`remember` + `AndroidView` holder keyed by tab id), `FLAG_SECURE` honoured from the activity; manual check on the emulator that switching tabs keeps scroll position.

5a. Hub session cookies: `CookieManager` scoped to the app, `android:allowBackup` rules + `dataExtractionRules` exclude the WebView data; sign-in happens on the hub's own login page inside the tab (no JS injection, no off-hub navigation).

5b. Sign-out: a "Sign out of hub" setting clears cookies for every tab and reloads them; the console tab's own token stays in the SecureStore (untouched); unit test that sign-out does not clear SecureStore keys.
6. Downloads: only axHub Apps page APK links, handed to `DownloadManager` with the hub cookie (as `apps/axhub-android` does); everything else refused with a toast; unit test of the link rule.
7a. Cover slot: active non-console tab fills `app.frame.cover` below the bar; back button goes back inside the web view first, then returns to the Console tab (`BackHandler`).
7b. Loading + errors: pull-to-refresh, a "Loading…" bar, a plain error card (offline, 4xx/5xx, refused frame) with Retry, all from theme tokens; emulator check.
8a. Settings → Plugins → App tabs: pick tabs (switch per built-in), order (up/down), reset; `SettingsGroup`/`SettingSpec` with parent = Plugins.
8b. Custom tabs: add name + https address on an allowed host (validated with `hostAllowed`), remove; stored in `app-tabs.custom` with the web plugin's JSON shape.

9. Install: `apps/console` manifest module list + `android-compose` template behind an init option `--app-tabs` (default off; on for the console) in `template.json`, catalog `plugins.json` entry, status.json + tracker (`tracker.mjs --check`).
10a. Tests: `lib-apptabs` unit tests (allowed-host, link rule, settings parity, tab list from manifests) + Compose UI test for bar + cover; CI job line in `android.yml`.

Depends on the pending `axhub-agent-host` for sessions and on axHub's admin API (its step 4). Work on it a little at a time: every sub prompt ships something usable.

steps.text: 1a. Pilot contract on Kotlin, types: `axf-pilot-core` pure-Kotlin module (`framework/android/axf-pilot-core`) with `PilotPluginManifest`, `PilotStep`, `BuildPatch`, `BuildRequest` (incl. `hidden`/`assets`) data classes mirroring Build-Pilot's `src/pilot/contract.ts` after its Fable rebuild (`build-pilot-contract`).
1b. Manifest checks + `servesStack`/`pluginsFor` in Kotlin, replaying `spec/fixtures/pilot-contract.json` (copied from Build-Pilot's generated fixture into `framework/spec/fixtures/`).
1c. `compose` merge + conflict rules in Kotlin, same fixture section; `PilotContractConformanceTest` in CI (`:axf-pilot-core:test`).

1d. Fixture sharing: a script in Build-Pilot (`npm run fixtures:export`) writes the fixture; AmberX-AXF CI fails if the copied fixture's hash differs from the one Build-Pilot publishes in its README (manual sync, documented).

2a. Pilot API client, models: Kotlin data classes for `/api/projects`, `/api/catalog`, `/assemble`, `/build`, `/apk`, `/metering/me` responses mirroring `server/main.py`; kotlinx.serialization, lenient unknown keys.
2b. Pilot API client, transport: `PilotClient` over axf-network with the token from SecureStore and the hub-admin sign-in reused (cookie provider), timeouts, no redirects, typed errors.
2c. Pilot API client, tests: MockWebServer test per route (happy path, 401, 5xx, malformed JSON), token never logged; CI job line.

3a. Android plugin face: define the `android/` part of `pilot-plugin@1` (a Compose `steps` composable entry + the same `contribute`/`check` shape) as Kotlin interfaces in `axf-pilot-core`; manifest field `android: { module }`.

3b. Loader: reads bundled plugin manifests from assets, instantiates Android parts by registered factory (open registry), lists web-only plugins separately; unit test with two fake plugins (one Android, one web-only).
4a. Pilot Home screen: stacks + projects list from `PilotClient`, New project button, error/empty states from theme tokens.
4b. Designer shell: steps from the loaded plugins in order, step navigation, autosave through the API (debounced), unsaved marker.
4c. Build step, part 1: review (composed request summary) + assemble with the agent (calls `/assemble`, shows ops, approve/deny).
4d. Build step, part 2: build + validate (`/build`, `/validate`), history list, retry; generic UI only.
5a. `android-app` plugin Android part: App setup form (name, id, package) with validation parity to the web plugin.
5b. `android-app` boilerplate browser: list from the catalog with screenshots (`GET /api/boilerplates/<id>/screenshots/<file>` through the console), pick one.
5c. `look` plugin Android part: slot picks per type from `framework-assets` (engine-rpc through the console), preview chips.
5d. `build-options` plugin Android part: switches from `GET /api/build-options`, defaults off, descriptions.
5e. `feature-manager` Android part, 1: FeatureList rows (catalog features, grouped), search, selected set.
5f. `feature-manager` Android part, 2: Chrome section (banner/toolbar entries) + Customize/Build now actions wired to the designers (step 6) and the Build step.
5g. `custom-features` Android part: metered Claude request form, usage from `/metering/me`, result list; refused when no key with a clear note.

6a. Banner designer on Android: builds the same asset@1 `banner` document as `src/pilot/designers.tsx` (surface, logo, divider, attach list); widget picker from the engine's app defaults (`typeLabels`/`typeIcons` via the console API).
6b. Toolbar designer on Android: items + widgets start/end + density/surface/collapsible, same asset@1 output; unit test that both designers emit documents that pass the Kotlin validator.

7a. Live preview, frame: a floating phone-frame composable (window via `windows/` engine) rendering the composed request's theme through the Kotlin theme engine; shrink to a pill, drag (same as the web `ScreenMock` behaviour).
7b. Live preview, content: nav/toolbar/banner from the picked assets, screens as placeholders with the boilerplate's screen kinds; updates on every designer change (debounced).
8. APK builds from the phone: Build APK → poll `/apk` → download via `DownloadManager` → install prompt; progress widget bound to a counter (`counter`/`progress` widget kinds).
9a. axHub admin client, models: Kotlin data classes for the hub's step-4 admin API (services, jobs, approvals, audit, users, projects) from its OpenAPI/JSON shapes; lenient parsing.
9b. axHub admin client, transport + tests: `HubAdminClient` over axf-network sharing the AXHub app's session (cookie jar), CSRF header handling, no redirects; MockWebServer tests per route.
9c. Approvals list screen native (replaces the web view the AXHub app uses today): list, filters, pull to refresh.
9d. Single approval screen: details, Approve/Deny through the API with the hub's CSRF rules, PIN prompt when the hub asks, result toast; one-tap link rule honoured from notifications.
10a. Services: list/describe/call with a JSON args editor, destructive confirm card (same rule as lib-mcp's gate).
10b. Jobs: list, detail with progress, cancel.
10c. Audit log viewer: paged list, filter by user/tool, detail sheet.
10d. Vault names: list of names only, set/rotate (write-only; values never shown).
10e. Users + permissions: list, per-user permission switches (`console.*`, `agents.*`, `apps.download`), add user (temporary password flow as the hub does).
10f. Projects tree browser over `axhub.memory_*` (read + edit text files with approval), Apps page (download APKs through `DownloadManager`).
11a. Native tab bar in slot `app.frame.top` (from `console-android-app-tabs` step 1) switching Console / Pilot (native) / axHub (native), each with its own back stack (`NavHost` per tab).
11b. Tab choice shared with the web console through the `app-tabs.*` settings keys (settings-from-axHub when it lands); unit test of the mapping.

steps.text: 1a. Framework embed@1 (web reference): `core/engines/embed.ts` — the marker a host app puts on the pages it embeds (query `?axf-embed=<host>[&axf-embed-hide=…]`, user agent `AXF-Embed/<host>[/<types>]`), host id rules, hidden-chrome cleaning (hideable types only, default banner, `none`), host helpers `userAgentSuffix` / `embedUrl`; fixture `spec/fixtures/embed.json`.

1b. Hide engine forced layer + runtime (web): `hiddenSlots(overrides, defaults, forced)`; `AxfRuntime.embedded` (detected from the page or passed), `embedHiddenSlots`, `slotHiddenByHost`, `setSlotHidden` refuses host-shown chrome with a toast and never writes an override; `AppShell` marks `.fx-frame[data-axf-embed]`; lib-settings greys the slot picker out ("Shown by <host>"); `spec/check-embed.mts` in CI.

1c. Kotlin twins: `EmbedEngine` (same fixture), `HideEngine.hiddenSlots(…, forced)`, `AxfRuntime(embedded = …)` + `slotHiddenByHost`, Compose settings chips greyed; `EmbedConformanceTest` + the hide fixture's forced cases in `ConformanceTest`.

2. Dev Console: remove the App tabs plugin cleanly (`uninstall.mjs --all`, lifecycle check clean), strip its doc lines, keep the `app.frame.top` / `app.frame.cover` slots for other plugins; the console stands alone with its own banner.

3a. Patches app scaffold: `axf init apps/patches` (android-compose, developer app: look + settings from axHub, hub library), app id `patches`, package `ai.amberx.axf.patches`, project manifest (repo `MossesX/patches` reserved), own layout asset `patches-tabs` (top tabs, no menubar/toolbar/status, full width), nav asset `patches-tabs` with the three tabs, manifest hides toolbar/app-menu.

3b. lib-hub `WebAppView`: a full web-app WebView (JavaScript + DOM storage on, cache allowed, origin allowlist with the hub origin for the sign-in wall, no file/content access, no mixed content, downloads to the hub app catalog handler), user agent suffix from `EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix("patches")`, `WebAppHolder` that keeps one WebView per tab alive across tab switches (reparented, never destroyed until the activity goes), back button = page history.

3c. Patches views: three routes (console / pilot / axhub) each rendering the holder's WebView for that tab; the Patches banner (logo, day/night switch, clock, settings button) is the one banner; hub sign-in via the developer-app waiting screen (shared cookie store = one session for every tab); Settings → Patches group: hub address, each tab's URL, reload tab, open in the phone's browser.

4. Wiring: CI (`android.yml` builds every app `app-bundle.mjs list --android` finds → `patches-debug.apk` + app catalog entry), `project.manifest.json` validated (`axf project validate --all`), `framework/catalog` + tracker, CLAUDE.md status, rules note (Android hold exception for Patches), PORTING.md, decisions.md.

5. Proof: web checks (`check-embed`, `check-widgets`, `check-appearance`, `check-app-menu`, `check-hub`, `axf validate --framework`, console typecheck), before/after web screenshots (console with and without the tab group; console embedded = no banner), push `fable/patches-wrapper` (Android shots by `rebuild-shots.yml`), differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/patches-wrapper.md`, LOG.md line, change-log result.

# Build: x.engine.dev

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "Live reload (axf dev) + device hot reload" (x.engine.dev) [Build engine] — Phase 1, model Opus.
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (4 left, ~2 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Web hot reload: `framework/react` `useDevServer(url)` long-polls `/events` from `dev-server.mjs` and re-registers changed assets (`registry.register` + `rt.refreshFromSaved`); `axf dev` prints the URL; demo app opts in with `?axfDev=`.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) Android end to end on the emulator (CI): `rebuild-shots.yml`-style job step that starts `axf dev --framework` on the runner, points the emulator at `10.0.2.2:7070` (setting `axf.devServer`, flag `axf.hotReload`), edits a theme file, screenshots before/after and asserts the pixel diff > 0.
[ ] s3 (~30 min) Robustness: dev server validates every changed file before announcing it (invalid → `/events` carries `error` and the device shows a terminal line), ignores editor temp files, handles rename/delete; `check-dev-server.mjs` test with a temp folder.
[ ] s4 (~30 min) Docs + status: README section "Live reload on a phone" (PC IP, same Wi-Fi), plan warning cleared, status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`.
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step x.engine.dev <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link x.engine.dev --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Tick every step as you finish it (orchestrator.mjs act step x.engine.dev <stepId> done). When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note x.engine.dev "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): make a plugin with a toolbar of programmable actions for filtering, sorting and searching grids. Toolbar name: Share Search. HELD: Brett said 'send to orchestrator and hold off on build' — don't start until he says.

builds.title: Approval history with costs: every approval recorded with details + cost, browsable in Console + axHub
builds.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): 'Add cost of approval every time something is approved and display costs, as well as all details and history of past approvals browsing. Can you alert when needing approval without stopping and restarting.' Context: he asked whether sending an approval and waiting costs tokens. Answer given: waiting is free, but each retry check re-reads the conversation (mostly cached). The 15 s x10 then 1 min rule costs about 10-15 checks per 5 minutes. HELD: queued, not started. Picks (cards): profile Refactor, held; history in the Console AND on axHub's approvals page.

Scope:
1) Cost per approval: every approval records the session's token/cost spent while it waited (number of checks, tokens in/out, cached vs not, USD from framework/schemas/model-pricing.json), plus the time it waited and who/what asked (session, surface, machine, build ref, reason title/description, exact call, result).
2) History browser: every past approval with all details and its cost; filter/sort/search, totals per day/build/session. Console = History view in the approvals-banner plugin (framework DataGrid, expanding rows). axHub = same list on its approvals page. Approve stays on the first screen.
3) Alert without stopping/restarting: a hub-side wait (axhub tool, e.g. approvals.wait / long-poll on the confirmation id, up to ~10 min per call) so a session makes ONE call that returns the moment Brett approves. No retry loop and no session restart. The AmberX app push (already shipped, amberx-push) fires when the approval is created. Then update the shared retry rule (15 s x10, then 1 min) to 'one wait call, re-issued only if it times out' — Brett to confirm that rule change at build time.
Work spans MossesX/axHub (wait tool, cost fields, approvals page history) and AXF (approvals-banner History view, cost capture via codebase-changes hooks / session transcript).

builds.title: Run unless blocked: 2-min countdown → urgent alarm (red banner + loud AmberX ring) → 1-min grace → runs; Block anytime; zero session tokens
builds.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): 'Can you send notification that a command is about to be ran and I can intercept it from the banner and block it before axhub tries sending it.' HELD: queued, not started. Picks (cards): profile Refactor, held; countdown 2 minutes.

Design: a third tool policy next to allow / confirm, e.g. 'veto' (run unless blocked). A session's call returns a job id at once; axHub holds the call for the countdown (default 2 min, per-tool override possible later) and immediately pushes through the AmberX app (rule: all axHub pushes come from AmberX) and shows it in the console's banner (approvals banner or its own) with the reason title, the exact call, a live countdown, Block and Run now. No action = runs at zero. Block = cancelled, never runs, the session sees 'blocked' when it next looks at the job. Sessions never poll during the countdown: they carry on and read the job result once at the end only if they need it, which saves the re-read cost of approval checks. Approvals (confirm) stay for risky calls: deletes and free-form root shell. Brett picks which tools move to veto (proposal: merge-pr, redeploys, container restarts). Every veto call is logged with its outcome (ran / blocked / ran early) in the approvals history (approval-costs build). Related: approval-costs (history, wait call, resume), axhub-github-write.

steps.text: card@1 asset type in framework/schemas/asset-types.json (+ axf schemas): id, owner (plugin id or "console"), title, icon, kind (stat | list | meter | chart | feed | status | actions | custom), size (s | m | l | wide | tall), data {service (plugin_services capability), path, refreshSec, live:boolean}, slots (headline, value, sub, rows, sparkline, actions), emptyState, actions (ids run through the action engine), level (Simple/Basic/Developer/Administrator), minRole (UAC), defaultVisible, order, category. Open registry: unknown kinds render the custom slot, never fail.

plugin@1 gets `cards: ["cards/<id>.json", …]` (card assets ship inside the plugin folder, so plugin-lifecycle@1 removes them on uninstall); plugin-inventory@1 engine lists each plugin's cards (framework/core/engines/plugins.ts + server/engine.py twin) so anything can detect them; future card SDK attaches cards to a plugin by writing this list.

home-cards@1 engine (TS reference, framework/core/engines/cards.ts): collects every card from enabled plugins + console-owned cards, applies saved visibility/order/size, level and role; hidden cards stay in the output with `hidden: true` so Home ALWAYS renders (mounts) every card and only hides it (instant show, data kept warm). Fixture spec/fixtures/home-cards.json; Kotlin twin recorded as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android on hold).

card-layout@1 asset type: columns per window class (compact/medium/expanded), gap + density tokens, grouping (none | plugin | category), "show all / hide all" default, sort (manual | category | plugin). 3 starter layouts: grid-auto, two-column-dashboard, compact-list. Hot-swap via runtime.swap('card-layout', id); tokens only (THEMING.md).

Placeholders for the future card SDK: `axf.cards@1` capability service (list/register/unregister cards at runtime), extension point `home.cards`, typed NotImplemented card designer entry, so a designer plugin can later author card assets and attach them to any plugin without kernel changes.

builds.title: PR browser + Batch Manager
builds.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Grid of push batches with live badges, Merge/Hold on rows, expandable PR sub-grid, failing check + Fix. Dense: small type, small badges, no clutter. Left click opens review, right click menu. PR BROWSER (Brett, Oct 31): a tab listing every open PR across AmberX-AXF, axHub and Build-Pilot. One dense line per PR with everything: number, title, branch, built by (agent/session), live checks badge, behind main, mergeable/conflict, in which batch, age, cost. Expand a row: every check with its error lines, files changed, commits, description, linked build/plan, and actions: Fix, Merge (via batch), Add to batch, Close. Sort/search/filter like every grid; live updates. ROW LEAD (Brett): every row starts with the PR number + a plain-English line of what it does (e.g. '#187 Audio Extract: pulls audio out of screen recordings, no mic'), written from the actual diff not just the title; badges follow on the same line. SCREENSHOTS (Brett): every PR gets BEFORE (main) and AFTER (PR branch) screenshots of the screens it touches, captured automatically by CI/headless browser (web) and emulator (Android); small before/after thumbnails on the row, side-by-side or slider compare in the expanded view, stored with the PR. SCREENSHOT CORRECTION (Brett): do NOT build a new capture system - REUSE the existing pre-build and post-build screenshots the framework already takes (find them first). BEFORE = the existing pre-build screenshot. AFTER: if the PR/build is not done yet, show a PREDICTED screenshot (rendered mockup of the expected result from the build spec + diff so far, clearly badged 'Predicted'); as soon as the build finishes, the real post-build screenshot replaces it automatically (badge 'Real'), live, no refresh. FEATURE SHOTS (Brett): the existing pre/post-build screenshots are NOT enough - they must show the ACTUAL FEATURE the PR built. Per PR, build a feature map from the diff (changed plugins, components, routes, menus, dialogs -> the screens and states that show them). builds.title: Framework grid: built-in sort, search, filter + Date and time column
builds.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Every grid that lists builds, tasks, asks or anything else is sortable, searchable and filterable, taking little screen. Basic filter attached by default. Tap header sorts, tap again reverses, long-press adds a second sort. One thin row: small search box + filter icon; on phones just a search icon. Filters hidden until used, then small clearable chips. Custom tables move onto the framework grid. Android parity. Per grid: right-click a grid or its header -> Filter -> off/on for this grid; 'All grids...' lists every grid in the app with the right-clicked one scrolled into view and highlighted, a switch per grid; a default switch decides whether new grids get the filter (on). Defaults are decided per grid by the build: on for data grids with many rows or columns (builds, asks, changes, plugins, PRs), off for small lists (settings, keys, short pickers); record the choice and reason per grid. On grids where it is off, hovering the header for a moment shows a tooltip 'Add the filter to this grid?' with Enable (long-press on phones). Framework grid (part of the app, not the filter plugin): every grid that has no date/time column gets an automatic 'Date and time' column (row created / last changed), hidden by default; grids that already show a date/time get nothing. Right-click the header -> Show/Hide 'Date and time'. Web + Android. UPDATE (Brett): build BOTH into the framework grid. Sort/search/filter live in the framework (not the Basic filter plugin); smart per-grid defaults, right-click on/off, All grids list and hover offer all framework features. Date and time column is ensured at first render: if a grid renders without one, the framework adds the hidden column then. New grids get everything automatically. CI check flags any table not built on the framework grid.

builds.title: Agent swarm: headless specialist agents, conflict-free, token-cheap
builds.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Brett's own agents aren't programmed well; Claude designs as many specialist agents as needed with specific skills. The build orchestrator splits each build into jobs and dispatches them to agents so many builds run at once without stepping on each other. Each agent runs its own headless Claude Code run with ONLY what the job needs: the task, the exact leased files, and the few relevant snippets the orchestrator pre-extracts (no CLAUDE.md dump, no repo exploring). Token efficiency is a hard requirement (sub-agents cost a fortune): cheapest capable model per job (small model for docs/manifests/renames, Sonnet/Opus for code, Fable only for design/contract work); max turns and token budget per run, killed when over; only the tools the job needs; shared skill prefix first so prompt caching applies; short structured JSON report back. No conflicts: file leases per job, overlapping jobs sequenced, shared files (notes, registries, catalogs, tracker) written only by the orchestrator after merge, pre-push lease check, batch merge. Cost meter: tokens and dollars per agent, job and build, visible in the orchestrator. Persona: every agent has Amber's persona (blunt street slang, heavy cussing, wild, still honest about builds), as the full few-line Amber persona (Brett: it's like five lines) in the cached shared prefix. It applies to reports and anything said to Brett; code, code comments and commit messages stay clean and professional. Agent statuses (set from a dropdown on each agent's row in the Agent manager, with a note): On duty (gets work), Off duty (skipped, keeps everything), Injured (keeps failing; no new jobs, flagged for a fix), Medical leave (benched until a date, then back on duty automatically), Probation (small jobs only, Brett notified every run), Fired (never assigned again, kept greyed in history), Custom (Brett names it and picks whether it gets work). The orchestrator only dispatches to agents whose status allows it. Spend per agent on its row: dollars and tokens all time, this week, today, average per job; optional spend cap that auto-benches the agent when hit. Sortable by cost. Status and spend also shown in the session browser. CARDS (Agent manager): one card per agent with photo avatar (unique look per agent), name, role, specialty on its own line, status badge, hiring date, spend (all time, week, today), jobs done, success rate, failures, avg cost per job, favorite model, last seen, Amber-style catchphrase; tap for profile: bio, skills, spend cap, status history, feed of latest runs with cost (opens the session browser). Social profiles live inside the system only, no real social media accounts. GROUP CHAT: a chat window like a normal conversation, switch to enable/disable for all agents plus per-agent; main room plus each agent's history on its profile. The orchestrator ('Boss') posts every assignment (task, files, model, budget) and lease decisions in the chat; agents report done/failed and hand off; banter in Amber persona (fighting over files, chilling, beer while Gradle runs). Work lines are built from orchestrator messages and agent reports (no extra tokens); banter comes from one cheap small-model batch; zero cost when off. DISCIPLINE: Suspend (Brett picks duration + reason; no jobs until it ends, then auto back on duty); Rage-quit (after N consecutive failed jobs, N set by Brett, default 3, agent quits itself and posts it in chat, status Quit, no jobs); Rehire button on the card puts them back on duty. All logged in status history and posted in the group chat. SALARY: each agent has a weekly salary that IS its token budget (replaces the plain spend cap); card shows salary, spent this pay period, left. Broke agents take no new jobs until payday or Brett tops them up, and say so in chat. Raises and pay cuts (docked) set by Brett, posted in chat by Boss. Finishing a job under its budget earns a bonus shown on the card (bragging rights, not real money). Coworker reactions in the group chat when someone gets a raise or bonus (jealous, cussing, Amber persona). Banter rules: no jokes about race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexuality or other identity. CHAT SETTINGS SUITE: Vibe slider 1-500 (1 = straight to the point, no sarcasm; 100 = chill; 250 = full Amber; 500 = off the rails). The slider is a hard ceiling: every message gets a vibe score; anything above the setting is toned down or dropped before it shows. Also: chattiness (assignments only .. constant banter), cussing (clean .. filthy), drama (fights, jealousy, shit talk) sliders; per-agent overrides of every slider; daily banter budget in dollars (quiet when hit); presets (All business, Work crew, Break room, Off the rails) + save your own; live preview message that changes as sliders move. Color by vibe: a checkbox (also in the chat window's context menu) colors every message by its vibe score; Brett picks the base color; light near 1, darker as the score rises, darkest at the ceiling. ID CARDS ARE ASSETS (Brett, Oct 31): new asset type agent-card@1 in the asset@1 envelope, registered in asset-types.json, loadable by any AXF app on web + Android, hot-swappable like every other asset. Cards are BRANDED: logo slot (brand logo asset, top/watermark/corner per design) and styled ONLY from theme tokens (color-theme + style-theme), so swapping the theme rebrands every card. Ship 4 starter designs: (1) Corporate badge - vertical lanyard ID, logo banner on top, photo, name, role, employee ID, barcode; (2) License - horizontal, small-type fields, logo hologram watermark, ID number, issue date = hire date; (3) Trading card - big photo, foil border in the theme accent, stats on the back (jobs, success rate, spend, favorite model); (4) Backstage pass - dark, neon accent, status badge big, catchphrase. Identity fields editable per agent: name, role, specialty, photo, employee ID, internal email (display/identity inside the system only, no real mailbox unless Brett asks), hire date, status, catchphrase, signature, QR to the agent's page. Card designer: edit any design's layout/fields/logo placement and Save as new (new asset). Gallery to pick the DEFAULT design (Brett picks from a preview page rendered FIRST, before the rest of the build), plus per-agent override. Flip for front/back.

# Chat Viewer: every session stored, synced, searchable, exportable as 2-voice audio (Brett, Nov 1 ~3 AM)

Read CLAUDE.md, _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md, _claude/persona.md. Opus, one session. Git login works: plain `git push`. Merge origin/main first (other builds are landing).

Brett: store ALL our sessions (claude.ai text + voice chats, Claude Code sessions, headless build sessions) as transcripts in a viewer. When it loads, it checks for updates: new sessions, continued ones, changed ones, and updates the stored copies. Export any session as AUDIO with two separate voices: one for Brett, one for Claude (Amber).

IMPORTANT reality: claude.ai has no API to pull a user's chats, and we must NOT scrape claude.ai with Brett's login/cookies. Supported inputs:
1. Claude data export: Brett downloads it from claude.ai (Settings > Privacy > Export data) and uploads the zip (or conversations.json) in the viewer (phone file picker). Parse it, upsert by conversation uuid, detect new/changed by updated_at + message count/hash, keep versions.
2. Claude Code sessions: auto-sync the JSONL session files from ~/.claude/projects (root and axfbuild) on the VPS on a timer + on viewer load; incremental (byte offset/mtime).
3. Headless build logs (/root/axf-builds/*/*.log, /home/axfbuild/wt-*/*.log) as 'build sessions'.
4. Hub drop folder: Claude chat sessions can push conversations through axHub memory_write into project amberx-axf, area data, path `sessions/claude-ai/<uuid>.json` (schema below); the viewer ingests that folder too. Document the schema and add a line to _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md: when Brett says 'sync my chats', Claude uses recent_chats/read_conversation and writes each new/updated conversation there.

## Store
session@1 schema (framework/schemas + validators): id, source (claude-ai-text|claude-ai-voice|claude-code|headless|hub-drop), title, startedAt, updatedAt, project, messages [{role: user|assistant|tool, text, at, kind (speech|text|tool), toolName?}], hash, version history. Stored on the console data volume (SQLite or JSON files; your call, justify), not in git. Redact secrets (tokens/keys/passwords patterns) on ingest.

## Viewer (console plugin + AmberX entry 'Chats')
- List: framework DataGrid (sort/filter/search, date columns), source badges, 'updated' badge for changed sessions, counts.
- Full-text search across everything (SQLite FTS or similar), jump to the hit.
- Session view: chat bubbles (Brett vs Amber), tool calls collapsible, timestamps, copy/share, export text/markdown.
- 'Check for updates' on load + button: shows new/changed/unchanged counts.

## Audio export
- Export a session (or a range) as an audio file with TWO voices: Brett's voice and Amber's voice (configurable). Use a TTS that runs on this VPS for free by default (e.g. Piper with two different English voices; install into a container or venv, no GPU), with an optional provider setting (OpenAI/ElevenLabs) if a key is saved in the console keys. Skip tool-call noise; read only spoken/text turns; short pause between turns; chapters per hour. Output mp3/ogg stored on the hub, with a player in the viewer and a download link. Long sessions render in the background with progress.

Framework controls + theme/scale tokens only, phone-first. Tests: export-zip parsing + upsert/new/changed detection, Claude Code JSONL incremental sync, hub-drop ingest, redaction, search, audio render (short sample) with two voices. Local test block from .github/workflows/android.yml + theme/controls/lifecycle/menu-reach checks. Phone + desktop screenshots to UI Review via framework/cli/shot.mjs, group 'Chat viewer - Nov 1' (use demo/redacted sessions in screenshots). Add an install_steps part. Commit, fetch+merge origin/main, retest, `git push origin HEAD:main` (never force). Report at _claude/builds/reports/chat-viewer.md incl. how Brett gets his claude.ai export in.

origin.brief:
# GitHub App for the whole stack: one-click setup, tokens that never die (Brett, Nov 1 ~4 AM)

Read CLAUDE.md, _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md, _claude/persona.md. Opus, one session. Git login works: plain `git push`. Never print secrets (private keys, client secrets, tokens) anywhere: logs, reports, commits, screenshots.

Why: personal tokens keep dying (401s, 403s on the banner), and the current fine-grained token can't create repos (the axp-backup build at /root/axf-builds/axp-backup is waiting on 3 private repos: axp-xchat, axp-devstudio, axp-demo). Brett wants this fixed for good.

## 1. One-click setup (GitHub App Manifest flow)
- Console page (behind the existing auth wall, admin only): Settings > GitHub > 'Create GitHub App'. It POSTs a manifest to https://github.com/settings/apps/new (personal account MossesX): name 'AmberX AXF Bot' (add suffix if taken), homepage the console URL, redirect/callback to the console, no webhook needed (or webhook off), public: false.
- Permissions (repository): Administration RW, Contents RW, Pull requests RW, Actions RW, Workflows RW, Issues RW, Checks R, Commit statuses R, Metadata R.
- Callback: exchange the code (POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions), store app id, slug, client id, client secret, private key PEM and webhook secret in /opt/axf/.axf-console/github-app/ (dir 700, files 600, root-owned), never in git. Then send Brett to the install page (https://github.com/apps/<slug>/installations/new) with 'All repositories'. Detect the installation id after install (GET /app/installations with an app JWT).
- Also offer 'Authorize as Brett' (OAuth user-to-server via the same app, with refresh tokens, stored the same way): needed because INSTALLATION tokens cannot create repos on a personal account; user access tokens from the app with Administration write can (POST /user/repos). Refresh automatically (8 h access / 6 month refresh); banner when refresh fails.

## 2. Token broker
- framework/cli/github-token.mjs (+ a tiny Python twin for the console server if it needs it): `installation` -> mints a JWT from the PEM, exchanges for an installation token, caches it (refresh at 50 min), prints it only to stdout for callers; `user` -> the refreshed user access token.
- /usr/local/bin/axf-git-cred: use the installation token first, then the old GITHUB_TOKEN as fallback. `gh`: wrapper or GH_TOKEN via a helper so gh uses the app too. Keep the old token working as fallback until Brett deletes it.
- Point every GitHub caller at the broker: push banner, live-key-checks, activity banner GitHub part (the 403s), build_land/build_start paths, the console updater, CI-status reads. Repo creation (`axf repo create <name> --private`) uses the user token.
- axHub's github connector (MossesX/axHub, packages/connectors or the rest service config): add app-based auth via the same broker or its own JWT exchange; clone axHub next to the worktree, test (pnpm test, Node 22 via docker node:22), push its main, redeploy through Coolify the same way earlier builds did (token saved in the console, never printed). If that's too big, leave axHub on the old token and banner it as a follow-up.

## 3. Health + banner
- health@1 check: app key valid, installation present, installation token mints, user token refreshes, rate limit remaining. Red banner with the exact fix if any fail. Old-token expiry warning.
- After setup works: re-run the axp-backup push automatically (create the 3 private repos with the user token, then `bash /root/axp-backup/bin/backup.sh` or whatever finish script that build left; read /root/axf-builds/axp-backup/axp-backup.log and /root/axp-backup/REPORT.md first). Never commit secrets; the backup's own secret scan must pass.

Framework controls + theme/scale tokens only. Tests: manifest generation, callback exchange (mocked GitHub), file perms, JWT + token cache, git credential helper order + fallback, user-token refresh, health check states. Local test block from .github/workflows/android.yml + theme/controls/lifecycle checks. Phone + desktop screenshots of the setup page (no secrets on screen) to UI Review via framework/cli/shot.mjs, group 'GitHub App - Nov 1'. install_steps: new part 'GitHub App (no more tokens)' with the 3 taps. Commit, fetch+merge origin/main, retest, `git push origin HEAD:main` (never force). Report at _claude/builds/reports/github-app.md: what Brett taps, where things are stored (paths only), what now uses the app.

# Build: orch-live-sync (Urgent profile)

Requested by Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice). GO given. Build it now, start to finish.

## Problem
The Build orchestrator on main is stale. `_claude/builds/profiles/*/orchestrator.json` is a read-only export of `_claude/builds/store.json`, regenerated after every store write. Sessions write the store on their own feature branch, so main never sees step progress until (if ever) the branch merges. Branch and PR fields are left blank. Result today: in the Urgent profile, dock-engine (done in open PR #245, branch claude/molly-fable) and token-control (done in open PRs #246 claude/token-control and #250 claude/token-control-opus) still show pending with 0 steps done, and theme-editor has an unmerged branch claude/theme-editor nobody linked. Banners and THREADS are wrong as a result.

Brett's rule: every completed step, no matter how small, must reach the orchestrator and appear on main immediately. The orchestrator must be aware every step of the way so it can update the banners and the threads.

## First (before code)
1. Register this build in the Urgent profile through the orchestrator/store (id `orch-live-sync`, category Urgent, branch claude/orch-live-sync), with the steps below. Register the in-progress banner entry per the standing session rules.
2. Check the pending build queue per the standing rules.

## Steps
- s1 Live status writes to main: a small module (e.g. framework/cli/builds-live.mjs or inside the store IO) so that every store write that changes build/step status (step done, build status, notes, branch, pr) is committed to main immediately as its own tiny status-only commit (store.json + journal + regenerated exports only), independent of whatever feature branch the session is on. Use a separate worktree or git plumbing on origin/main; fetch, apply, commit, push; on non-fast-forward, refetch and re-apply the journal entry (rebase-retry, bounded); never force-push. Code changes stay on the feature branch/PR as now. Avoid conflicts between parallel sessions (journal-append semantics, per-build records). When the feature branch later merges, resolve.py / union merge must not regress statuses (newer rev wins).
- s2 Branch + PR auto-link: when a session creates/pushes a branch or opens a PR for a build, the build's `branch` and `pr` fields are set and written live (s1). Build status shows built-awaiting-merge when all steps are done but the PR is unmerged; complete when merged.
- s3 Reconciler: on every session start and on a timer (VPS cron or the existing hub scheduler), scan open PRs and claude/* branches on GitHub, match them to builds (branch field, build id in branch name/PR title/body, step ids in commits), mark finished-but-unlisted work, fill missing branch/pr fields, and flag orphans in a report and a banner alert. Write results live (s1).
- s4 Banners + THREADS follow the store: every live status change pushes the banner update and appends a THREADS.md entry (one line per change, union-merge friendly).
- s5 Session-start rule: update the session rules / CLAUDE docs so no session trusts the main export alone; it runs the reconciler and reads the live store first.
- s6 Backfill now using the new tools: Urgent profile -> dock-engine all steps done, branch claude/molly-fable, pr #245; token-control s1-s3 done (pr #246, branch claude/token-control), s4-s14 done (pr #250, branch claude/token-control-opus); urgent-builds is complete and merged (2a057cc4), hide/archive it from the active list; theme-editor: inspect branch claude/theme-editor, mark the steps it actually completed, link the branch, and if all 5 steps are done open a PR for it. Run the reconciler across all five profiles (angel, big-dog, breakroom, refactor, urgent) and report what it fixed.
- s7 Tests (store write retry, parallel writes, merge no-regress, reconciler matching), full local CI block, report `_claude/builds/reports/orch-live-sync.md`, THREADS.md, open the PR.

Mark each step done through the store as you finish it (that write itself should go live once s1 exists). Code, comments and commits stay clean and professional.
## ADDENDUM (Brett, Nov 3 2026 voice) — read before finishing
- s8 Per-step branch + PR: every step record gets its own `branch` and `pr` fields (plus `merged`/`mergedAt`), set live when that step's work is pushed / PR'd / merged. A build can span several branches and PRs (e.g. token-control: s1-s3 in #246 claude/token-control, s4-s14 in #250 claude/token-control-opus). Build-level branch/pr stay as a summary (list). Reconciler (s3) matches per step. Migrate existing records with empty values; schema + projections + Steps view column.
- s9 Keep live status commits cheap: status writes are plain scripts/git plumbing, zero model involvement beyond one CLI call per step; add paths-ignore for `_claude/builds/**` and THREADS.md to .github/workflows/deploy.yml (and any other workflow on push to main) so status-only commits never trigger CI/deploy; debounce/batch writes within a few seconds into one commit.

## ADDENDUM 2 (Brett, Nov 3 2026 voice: "you fix it, I trust you")
- s10 Resolve every claude-sync hold and stop them piling up. Brett delegated the pick to these rules; apply them yourself, don't ask:
  - `_claude/builds/store.json` + journal: merge per record by `rev`/updatedAt, newest wins, never drop a record from either side. Orchestrator/pending/queue exports: regenerate from the merged store (never pick a side).
  - THREADS.md, STATUS.md, decisions.md, LOG.md, sessions/*, handoff notes: union merge (keep every unique line/entry, dedupe identical ones, keep chronological order, decision numbers kept unique).

# Build: headless-tabs (Urgent profile)

Requested by Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice). GO given. Build it now.

## First
- Register in the Urgent profile through the orchestrator/store (id `headless-tabs`, branch claude/headless-tabs) with the steps below + in-progress banner entry, per standing rules. Check the pending queue.

## What Brett wants
1. Every terminal tab in the console's terminal (the Windows Terminal plugin / terminal in the console) runs on a session that never dies, like Mosh/Moshi: it survives disconnects, reloads, phone sleep, and stays current. Browsers can't speak Mosh (UDP), so: every tab is backed by a persistent tmux session on the VPS, attached over the console's websocket/pty bridge with automatic reconnect + resume (scrollback replay on reattach, no lost output). The same tmux sessions must be attachable from Brett's Moshi phone app (document the one-line `mosh`/ssh + `tmux attach -t <name>` command in the help pack and show it in a tab menu item "Open in Moshi" that copies it). Closing a tab detaches, it doesn't kill (explicit "Kill session" with confirm).
2. Every time a headless session starts (deploy/claude-headless.sh, `vps.build_start`, agent swarm jobs, orchestrator-launched builds), the console automatically opens a NEW tab attached to that build's tmux session (axf-<name>). Works for builds started while the console is closed too: on open, tabs for all running headless sessions appear.
3. Tab title bar: the agent running it (agent/persona name from the session's env/brief/swarm roster, e.g. the swarm agent name, else the build name) + model + a real-time cost counter that climbs as it spends. Cost: run claude -p with `--output-format stream-json --verbose` (or tee it alongside the human log) and sum usage per message (input, output, cache read, cache write) x the model's price table (config file, not hard-coded in UI); final value reconciles to the result event's total_cost_usd. Expose cost via a small server route/websocket so the title updates live. Show status dot (working / waiting / done / failed).
4. The tab splits into two panes; split direction vertical or horizontal (toggle in the tab menu + default in Settings, remembered per tab). Pane A = the live session. Pane B = the context chain: as the session reads CLAUDE.md and every file it pulls in (imports/@ references, .claude/rules, _claude/rules/RULES.md, shared rules, instructions, persona, memory, THREADS etc.), show the chain as a tree in the order it happens, and print the rules it picks up ONE AT A TIME, deliberately slower than real time (typewriter/reveal pacing, speed setting, skip-to-end button), so Brett can watch what the agent is learning. Source the chain from the session's actual reads (stream-json tool events for Read, plus the CLAUDE.md load order Claude Code uses); rules = the bullet/heading items of each file.
5. Tokens only, follows the hub look, phone-friendly (on narrow screens the split stacks and becomes swipeable).

## Steps
- s1 Persistent tmux-backed tabs + reconnect/resume in the console terminal; Moshi attach command; detach vs kill.
- s2 Headless launcher emits session-start events (claude-headless.sh + build_start path + swarm/orchestrator launches) with build name, agent, model, tmux session; console auto-opens tabs, and lists running ones on load.
- s3 stream-json capture alongside the human log; cost meter service (price table config) + live route.
- s4 Tab title: agent, model, live cost, status dot.
- s5 Split pane with vertical/horizontal toggle + setting.
- s6 Context chain pane: tree in read order + slow rule-by-rule reveal, speed setting, skip.
- s7 Help pack, tests, check-theme/check-controls, lifecycle, UI Review shots, report `_claude/builds/reports/headless-tabs.md`, THREADS.md, PR.
Mark each step done through the store as you finish it. Android port: log as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android on hold). Code, comments and commits stay clean and professional.
## ADDENDUM (Brett, Nov 3 2026) - where it goes
Everything in this build goes INTO the console's existing built-in Terminal plugin (Terminal v0.3.0: frameless window, tab strip as title bar, connections, profiles, Windows keys; window engine resize/snap/maximize from refactor-all s17-s23, see `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/windows-terminal.md` and `windows-terminal-fable.md`). Extend that plugin; do NOT create a separate terminal plugin or a second terminal UI. Persistent tmux sessions become the Terminal's session backend / a connection type, auto-opened headless tabs are Terminal tabs, title/cost/status live in its tab strip, the split + context-chain pane are Terminal pane features. Bump the Terminal plugin version and keep every existing feature working.

## ADDENDUM 2 (Brett, Nov 3 2026) - clarification, overrides any ambiguity above
Target = the Terminal PLUGIN produced by the Refactor build `windows-terminal` (the Windows-Terminal-style plugin, v0.3.0, in the console's plugins folder). # Model UPGRADES need Brett's approval; downgrades don't (Urgent, Opus)

Replaces the stopped build model-switch-approval (folder /root/axf-builds/model-switch-approval, ignore any work there).

Brett Nov 3 2026 (voice), angry: a headless build (agent-swarm-fable-rebuild, PR #247) approved its own Opus -> Fable phase switch in the orchestrator (`orchestrator.mjs act approve`) because its brief said "do every step". Brett: "It cannot be switching the model without my approval. That's not even a veto. That's an approval." Then: "You can downgrade, but you can't upgrade."

New project rule (add to _claude/rules/RULES.md and the decisions log, dated Nov 3 2026): a build may switch to a LOWER model on its own (downgrade, e.g. Fable -> Opus): allowed, no approval, just recorded. Switching to a HIGHER model (upgrade, e.g. Opus -> Fable) needs Brett's explicit APPROVAL (confirm policy), never a veto countdown and never self-approved by a session, agent, headless build or the orchestrator. Ranking: Fable is above Opus (Brett's call). Put the ranking in model-policy (one ordered list, config not code) so future models slot in. A session that reaches an upgrade stops there and asks.

Enforce it:
1. orchestrator approve/phase logic (orchestrator-core.mjs apply + CLI + console server): a downgrade phase passes by itself (record it); an upgrade phase refuses unless approved by Brett: his own signed-in console click or an axHub approval he approves. Detect non-human sources with the same signals used for 'who asked' on approvals (X-Axhub-Source, AXF headless env, agent env). Record who approved and when.
2. vps.build_start / claude-headless.sh / agent job router: launching or relaunching a build on a higher model than its orchestrator step's model is an upgrade too: refuse or hold for approval the same way.
3. Briefs (orchestrator `brief`, headless guidance, agent jobs): say plainly upgrades need Brett and the session stops and asks; downgrades are fine. Remove any wording that lets a session approve an upgrade.
4. Request path: an axHub approval (confirm policy, not veto) titled with the build, the phase and from -> to model; approving it records the approval in the orchestrator.
5. Audit: list every upgrade approved so far by a non-human source (the store's journal), report in the PR; mark agent-swarm-fable-rebuild's s7 Opus -> Fable as self-approved (not Brett's). Note: xlayout-opus and token-control-opus were Fable -> Opus (downgrades), fine under the new rule.
6. Tests for refusal, downgrade pass-through and the approval path; THREADS row (profile urgent); PR (push banner merges it).

Rules: one session, no sub-agents, stay on Opus. Don't approve any phase yourself while doing this.

# Build: menu-scroll (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): "The application menus need to be scrollable when they reach beyond the screen." Assigned agent: **Janitor Joey** (book on his agent-swarm card; set AXF_AGENT=janitor-joey if supported, else record in report + store note). Register in Urgent (id `menu-scroll`) + banner entry.

## Fix (framework level, so every app and plugin gets it)
- Application menu bar dropdowns, their submenus, and also context menus / overflow (⋯) menus: when a menu is taller than the space left in the viewport, cap its height to the available space (respect safe-area insets, the banner/toolbars, and the on-screen keyboard; use visualViewport on mobile) and make it scroll vertically inside.
- Smooth touch scrolling on phones (overscroll contained so the page behind doesn't scroll), wheel + keyboard arrow navigation scrolls the highlighted item into view, subtle top/bottom fade or chevron hints when there's more.
