# Build: toolbar-tap-confirm (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): every EXISTING and FUTURE toolbar uses the Terminal's Tooltip mode (first tap shows what the button does and arms it lit for 3 s, second tap within 3 s runs it, duration configurable; built in headless-tabs PR #259, s8). The double tap is ONLY on phones / touch. On a computer it stays a normal single click (hover tooltip as usual) - 'it really works on a computer.' Assigned agent: **Landin' Lenny** (book on his card; AXF_AGENT=landin-lenny if supported). Register in Urgent (id `toolbar-tap-confirm`) + banner entry.

## Steps
- s1 Lift Tooltip mode out of the Terminal plugin into the framework toolbar component (web reference + axf.css; Compose twin in PORTING.md unless trivial) as one shared behaviour; the Terminal uses the framework version (no duplicate code left in the plugin).
- s2 Device rule: double-tap confirm only when the input is touch (pointer: coarse / touch events / compact window class on a touch device). Mouse/trackpad/pen-hover = single click + hover tooltip. Decide per interaction (a touchscreen laptop: touch = double tap, mouse = single click).
- s3 Adopt everywhere: every toolbar in the console, every plugin, axHub web, AmberX (Capacitor), Molly, walkthrough-studio, templates/boilerplates, so new apps get it by default. Inventory every toolbar first and list them in the report.
- s4 Future-proof: the framework toolbar has it ON by default; a check (like check-controls) fails CI if any toolbar is built outside the framework toolbar or turns the behaviour off without an explicit, recorded reason. Add the rule to shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'Every toolbar uses tap-to-confirm on touch (framework toolbar); single click on desktop.'
- s5 Settings > Appearance (or Interaction): on/off for touch, arm duration (default 3 s); per-toolbar override only via the setting, not code. Destructive buttons keep their own confirm on top.
- s6 Tests (touch vs mouse paths, timeout, second tap on a different button re-arms instead of running), screenshots phone + desktop, UI Review item, report `_claude/builds/reports/toolbar-tap-confirm.md`, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice, before start): make all of this ONE Toolbars plugin
The framework toolbar becomes a **Toolbars plugin** (plugin@1, lifecycle install/uninstall) that owns every toolbar in every app, existing and future. Everything below is part of it.

### Settings
- Plugin settings (Settings > Plugins > Toolbars): global on/off for the touch double-tap tip (default on, phone/touch only), arm duration, defaults for all toolbars (theme, colours, density, icon size, labels on/off, position).
- **Every toolbar carries its OWN settings** (stored per toolbar id, synced via axHub like other settings): theming and colours (tokens/assets only: colour theme, style, background, button style, icon/label size, spacing, rounded/flat, opacity), layout (position, orientation, wrap vs scroll vs overflow menu, show/hide, auto-hide), behaviour (double-tap override for this toolbar, tooltips), and its button list.
- **Context-menu hooks on every toolbar** (right-click / long-press): 'Toolbar settings' (that toolbar's own settings), 'Edit toolbar' (opens the Toolbar editor), 'All toolbars...' (Toolbars plugin page that lists and controls every toolbar in the app). Contributed as runtime context items, so every existing and future toolbar gets them; CI check fails any toolbar without them.

### Toolbar editor
- Opens from the toolbar context menu. Add / remove / reorder / group / separators, edit each button (label, icon, tooltip text, action/hook, colour, visibility by level/role, keyboard shortcut), reset to default, undo/redo, live preview, save as an asset so it's hot-swappable and shareable.

### Drag and drop hooks anywhere
- A **hook** = any actionable thing in the app (menu item, nav item, toolbar button, banner item, 'Go to it' hooks, plugin commands from control@1 / plugin-commands-auto, settings pages, screens). Reuse the control@1 command registry and the pending `context-menu-editor` idea (save the action/destination, not the element).
- Drag any hook from anywhere and drop it on a **drop target**: any toolbar, the navigation menu, the banners, application menus, context menus, Home. Drag a button from one toolbar to another; nav menu -> toolbar and toolbar -> nav menu.
- On drop: a **configure dialog that depends on where it's dropped** (toolbar = new button dialog; nav menu = nav item dialog; banner = banner item dialog; menu = menu item dialog), prefilled with default values from the hook (label, icon, action, tooltip), with all the options for that target. Confirm creates it; move vs copy choice (default: copy from menus, move between toolbars), undo.
- Make it a framework contract: `drop-target@1` (what it accepts + which configure dialog) and `hook@1` (draggable action descriptor), open registries so any plugin/app can add targets and hooks without kernel changes. Phone: long-press to pick up, drag with edge auto-scroll, drop zones highlight.
- **Banners:** only add the banner drop target through the generic contract. Do NOT merge or rewrite banner-pack (#251), banner-editor (#254) or banners-one work; Brett is reviewing those himself. Note any overlap in the report.
- Rules: add to shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'Every toolbar is a Toolbars plugin toolbar: per-toolbar settings + editor via its context menu, tap-to-confirm on touch only, accepts dropped hooks.' Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI.
- Split into clear steps in the store; tests for drop targets/dialogs/move-copy/undo, phone + desktop screenshots, UI Review items.

# Build: claude-settings (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): "I need a plugin called Claude. Claude settings. A setting to enable your no-wait in that. A whole bunch of settings that are for Claude, that you check on axHub and then act accordingly." Assigned agent: **Janitor Joey** (book on his card; AXF_AGENT=janitor-joey if supported). Register in Urgent (id `claude-settings`) + banner entry.

## Plugin
Console plugin **Claude** (plugin@1, lifecycle install/uninstall, page + Settings > Plugins > Claude, context-menu hook 'Claude settings' everywhere). Settings are stored on axHub (shared `_data/claude/settings.json` or a hub settings namespace) so every Claude session (voice, chat, Claude Code, headless agents) reads the same values.

## Settings (grouped, framework settings renderer with the level toolbar)
- **No wait** (owner-only): when ON, Amber's held calls run immediately instead of the 90 s veto / approval. Implement as a standing axHub pass that the console creates on Brett's signed-in click (reuse pass-all / `axhub.pass_grant` machinery, scope all, `include_irreversible` false by default with its own separate switch 'Include irreversible' also owner-only). Options: duration (1 h / 4 h / until I turn it off), auto-off at night. Banner chip while on. Turning it off revokes the pass instantly.
- **Follow Amber** (link to / share state with the follow-amber build's switch; don't duplicate it - read the same setting).
- **Builds:** default model (Opus/Fable/split), launch builds without asking (on/off), max parallel builds, per-build budget cap and daily budget cap (stop + notify when hit), always assign a named agent (locked on), UI Review gate (on).
- **Verification:** trust live store by default, verify only on conflict (current rule) vs always verify.
- **Talking:** persona on/off, tone level, address terms, swearing level, response length (short/normal/detailed), say costs out loud, read build reports aloud vs summary.
- **Notifications:** push on build done / blocked / approval waiting, quiet hours.
- **Memory/notes:** save session notes to Notes Vault automatically, handoff note at end of session.
- Open registry so new Claude settings can be added as data without code changes.

## Claude reads them
- MCP tools via axf-console (and axHub builtin if simpler): `claude_settings_get` (policy ALLOW, read-only) returning all values with plain descriptions; `claude_settings_set` for NON-owner settings only (veto policy). Owner-only settings (No wait, Include irreversible, approvals, budget caps raising) can ONLY be changed by Brett's signed-in console click - agents/sessions can never change them (test enforces).
- Rule in shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md (top): 'At session start and before acting, read Claude settings (claude_settings_get) and follow them.'
- Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI.

# Build: smart-menus (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): "I need a dynamic context menu that draws itself depending on where it is and what it's doing. Most common / most likely things at the top. It learns and remembers, predicts what I'm most likely gonna want, keeps that at the top." Assigned agent: **Earl the Ear** (book on his card; if busy and the all-rounder router is on main, whoever is free - record who). Register in Urgent (id `smart-menus`) + banner entry.

## Build (framework level: every context menu in every app, existing and future)
- s1 **Context-aware drawing:** the context menu engine builds the menu at open time from: the target under the pointer (element kind, hook@1 / control@1 target, plugin, screen), its state (selected, running, failed, waiting on approval, has PR, etc.), the current screen, device (phone/desktop). Plugins contribute items with `when` conditions (state predicates) so irrelevant items never show; runtime context items stay the contribution path.
- s2 **Learning ranking, zero tokens:** record every pick locally + synced to axHub per user: (context key = target kind + state + screen, item id, time). Rank with frecency (frequency x recency decay) per context, plus time-of-day and 'what I just did' sequence boosts (simple Markov next-action counts). Top section 'Suggested' = top 3-5 predicted items; the rest grouped below in stable order so muscle memory still works. Plain code, NO LLM calls (test fails if the engine imports an LLM client).
- s3 Pinned items always first (from the pending `context-menu-editor` idea: user pins), then Suggested, then the rest; destructive items never auto-promoted to the top.
- s4 Settings (Settings > Menus, and a 'Menu settings' hook in every context menu): learning on/off, number of suggestions, reset learning (per menu / all), show why it's suggested (tiny hint), privacy: data stays on his axHub.
- s5 Works with menu-scroll (#268) placement and the toolbar build's hook@1/drop-target@1 if on main (don't edit their files). Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI (get suggestions, reset, pin).
- s6 Tests (ranking math, context keys, when-conditions, reset, destructive never top), phone + desktop screenshots, UI Review item, report `_claude/builds/reports/smart-menus.md`, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice, before start): dynamic SECTIONS, not the whole menu
Don't make the whole menu dynamic. Each context menu keeps its normal fixed items in their fixed order (muscle memory). Add dynamic SECTIONS on top of that:
- A 'Suggested' section at the top (learned/predicted items, 3-5, per s2) - can be turned off.
- A context section (items that only apply to this target/state, per s1 'when' conditions), clearly grouped.
- Pinned items (user pins).
The rest of the menu is static and never reorders. A menu asset declares which dynamic sections it shows and where; the default is Suggested at top + context section, static items below.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice): application menus too + 'what we're talking about' goes to the top
- The dynamic sections apply to the **application menu bar** too (every top-level menu: Builds, View, Tools, etc.), not just context menus. Permanent items stay fixed; each menu can declare dynamic sections.
- New dynamic section **'Talking about'** at the top of every menu (app menus + context menus): items relevant to what Brett and Amber (Claude) are currently talking about. Example: open Builds in the app menu while we're discussing the toolbar build -> that build (open it, its PR, its UI Review, its agent, stop it) is at the top.
- How it knows: add MCP tool `console_context` (policy ALLOW, navigation-only, no data change) on axf-console: {topics: [{kind: build|plugin|screen|pr|agent|setting|profile|note, id, label}], ttl_min?}. Amber calls it whenever the conversation moves to something (and console_show / follow-amber can feed it too). The console keeps a short rolling 'current topics' list per user (decays after ~30 min or when replaced), synced live to every open console client.
- Each menu maps topics to its relevant actions via plugins' contributed items with `when` conditions + the control@1 command registry (e.g. a build topic -> Builds menu shows Open build / Open PR / Open UI Review / Agent / Stop). Plain code, zero tokens.
- Settings > Menus: 'Talking about' section on/off, how long topics stay.
- Rule in shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'When the conversation moves to something in the console, call console_context with it.'

## Addendum 3 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice): all of it lives in ONE Menus plugin with tons of customization
- Everything in this build (dynamic sections in app menus + context menus, Suggested, Talking about, context section, pins, learning) is controlled by a **Menus plugin** (plugin@1, lifecycle install/uninstall, page + Settings > Plugins > Menus + a 'Menu settings' hook in every menu's context menu). Removing the plugin falls back to plain static menus.
- **Customization (tokens/assets only, saved per user on axHub, live preview, presets, reset, export/import as a menu-style asset):**
  - Colours: menu background, text, hover/selected, section headers, separators, icons, per-section accent (Suggested / Talking about / Pinned / context), badge colours, shadow, border, blur/glass, opacity.
  - Fonts: family, size, weight, letter spacing, section header style, icon size, density/row height, padding, corner radius, width min/max.
  - Animations: open/close (fade, scale, slide, drop, none), duration + easing, submenu reveal, item stagger, hover effect, highlight pulse for 'Talking about' items, reduced-motion respected.
  - Sections: order, on/off, max items each, labels, icons, collapse/expand, show 'why suggested' hint.
  - Behaviour: learning on/off + reset, topic lifetime, open on hover vs click (desktop), long-press time (phone), keyboard shortcuts.
  - Per-menu overrides (each app menu / context menu can have its own look and sections) from the hook in that menu.
- Works with menu-scroll (#268) placement and the Toolbars plugin (toolbar-tap-confirm build) through framework APIs - don't edit their files; share the hook@1 / drop-target@1 contract if it's on main.
- Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI (get/set menu settings, presets, reset learning, topics).

- A 'Suggested' section at the top (learned/predicted items, 3-5, per s2) - can be turned off.
- A context section (items that only apply to this target/state, per s1 'when' conditions), clearly grouped.
- Pinned items (user pins).
The rest of the menu is static and never reorders. A menu asset declares which dynamic sections it shows and where; the default is Suggested at top + context section, static items below.

- The dynamic sections apply to the **application menu bar** too (every top-level menu: Builds, View, Tools, etc.), not just context menus. Permanent items stay fixed; each menu can declare dynamic sections.
- New dynamic section **'Talking about'** at the top of every menu (app menus + context menus): items relevant to what Brett and Amber (Claude) are currently talking about. Example: open Builds in the app menu while we're discussing the toolbar build -> that build (open it, its PR, its UI Review, its agent, stop it) is at the top.
- How it knows: add MCP tool `console_context` (policy ALLOW, navigation-only, no data change) on axf-console: {topics: [{kind: build|plugin|screen|pr|agent|setting|profile|note, id, label}], ttl_min?}. Amber calls it whenever the conversation moves to something (and console_show / follow-amber can feed it too). The console keeps a short rolling 'current topics' list per user (decays after ~30 min or when replaced), synced live to every open console client.
- Each menu maps topics to its relevant actions via plugins' contributed items with `when` conditions + the control@1 command registry (e.g. a build topic -> Builds menu shows Open build / Open PR / Open UI Review / Agent / Stop). Plain code, zero tokens.
- Settings > Menus: 'Talking about' section on/off, how long topics stay.
- Rule in shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'When the conversation moves to something in the console, call console_context with it.'

- Everything in this build (dynamic sections in app menus + context menus, Suggested, Talking about, context section, pins, learning) is controlled by a **Menus plugin** (plugin@1, lifecycle install/uninstall, page + Settings > Plugins > Menus + a 'Menu settings' hook in every menu's context menu). Removing the plugin falls back to plain static menus.
- **Customization (tokens/assets only, saved per user on axHub, live preview, presets, reset, export/import as a menu-style asset):**
  - Colours: menu background, text, hover/selected, section headers, separators, icons, per-section accent (Suggested / Talking about / Pinned / context), badge colours, shadow, border, blur/glass, opacity.
  - Fonts: family, size, weight, letter spacing, section header style, icon size, density/row height, padding, corner radius, width min/max.
  - Animations: open/close (fade, scale, slide, drop, none), duration + easing, submenu reveal, item stagger, hover effect, highlight pulse for 'Talking about' items, reduced-motion respected.
  - Sections: order, on/off, max items each, labels, icons, collapse/expand, show 'why suggested' hint.
  - Behaviour: learning on/off + reset, topic lifetime, open on hover vs click (desktop), long-press time (phone), keyboard shortcuts.
  - Per-menu overrides (each app menu / context menu can have its own look and sections) from the hook in that menu.
- Works with menu-scroll (#268) placement and the Toolbars plugin (toolbar-tap-confirm build) through framework APIs - don't edit their files; share the hook@1 / drop-target@1 contract if it's on main.
- Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI (get/set menu settings, presets, reset learning, topics).

- **Browse:** framework grid of every profile (collapsible rows): name, id, active star, description, counts (builds running / pending / complete / archived, pending items, queue steps), cost spent + cost left, last activity, created; sort/search/filter. builds.title: Terminal: tab position setting (top, left / right stack, bottom)
builds.detail: Brett (Nov 3 2026, voice): "I want a setting in terminal to put all the tabs on the left side in a stack instead of across the top." Setting Tab position: Top | Left stack | Right stack | Bottom, per device, also in the tab context menu. Stack: title, agent, model, live cost, status dot, close; collapse to icons; resizable; drag to reorder; scrolls; title bar still drags. Phone: slide-out. Server default + REST/MCP/CLI get/set. Agent: Janitor Joey (headless worktree session; router not on this branch's main). Overlaps: terminal-sessions-nav (#286, open, adds a left rail) and terminal-drag-chain-tree (running, rewrites strip pointer handling): changes kept to a new TabStack file + CSS so all three merge cleanly.

notes.text: Clash note from terminal-drag-chain-tree (branch claude/terminal-drag-chain-tree): the framework now has WindowGrip (react/windows/WindowHost.tsx; orientation="column" for a stacked tab list, put it first) and useTabPress (tap / horizontal drag reorder / press-and-hold or vertical pull drags the window / long-press menu). The Terminal strip uses them and dropped HTML5 tab drag. TerminalHost.tsx also gained the window menu (Terminal settings first), per-pane text size (A-/size/A+, Ctrl+wheel, pinch). The left/right stack should reuse WindowGrip + useTabPress (with vertical reorder) instead of its own drag; expect a TerminalHost merge.

Agent: Janitor Joey. Overlap: terminal-sessions-nav #286 (open) adds a left rail; stack kept inside __body so it sits beside the rail after merge; stack-inside-rail option is a follow-up once #286 lands. terminal-drag-chain-tree (running) rewrites strip pointer code; this build hides strip tabs by CSS only.

Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Wire into TerminalHost + settings panel + tab context menu + web action terminal.tabs.position; CSS tokens only; check-theme/controls

builds.title: Gizmo: full Claude companion plugin in AmberX
builds.detail:
## What Brett said (verbatim, Nov 3 2026, voice)
"I need a companion assistant... a sidekick that allows me to chat to your partner... put the plug-in in AmberX." "A full all-out Claude companion, as full, powerful, as complete as the Claude app itself, with everything, all the features, every setting, the connectors, plugins, a full Claude suite." "We can harvest the assistant code out in AmberX to build the new plugin." "Build the plugin for Claude in AmberX, but make it full, complete. It's gotta be powerful."

Booked to agent Gizmo (all-rounder, $8.00/h, AmberX guide/assistant; replaces agent Molly).

Decisions: lives in AmberX (apps/amberx-droid) as a plugin; harvest AmberX assistant code + console Terminal Claude session code into a shared framework lib (claude-session) + AmberX plugin `companion`; console Terminal keeps working on the shared lib; brains run on the VPS as Claude Code sessions reached through axHub, no API keys in the APK; Gizmo is the face, Molly is no longer an agent.

builds.title: Automated Browser plugin (drive, record, edit, schedule)
builds.detail: Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice), verbatim: "Make me a plugin that shows a browser that can be driven by the app, give it the ability to be automated and to record automation routines through the browser, like make it record in real time what you do and save the events, so you can redo everything that you just recorded, and have a powerful editor to see what each step is doing. Make it so that you can create workflows through the automated browser and record the steps, or do them automatically and record as you go, or record manually, and full powerful editing, able to tweak the JavaScript and whatever you gotta do to make it follow a routine, like go to a site and log in, or go to a site and go to a products page and grab something, and then have a scheduler built into it that you can schedule when to perform these routines." builds.title: Merge queue: test once, never twice
builds.detail: Stacked merge queue in auto-land (GitHub's native merge queue needs an org-owned repo; MossesX is a personal account). Each ready PR is tested once on top of main + every PR ahead of it on a queue/pr-<n> branch; green head merges with no retest; red is kicked out with a plain reason and the ones behind are rebuilt without it. CI path filters (framework/cli/ci-scope.mjs), light checks on PRs while the queue is on, main push skips jobs the queue already ran on the same code. Merge queue view + banner chip + REST/MCP/CLI (mergequeue_list/add/remove/move). UI Review gate kept.

origin.said: How do we prevent this from happening? Things get added to main before it gets merged, so it has to do it again. We're paying to do these CI checks twice. ... Two things being checked at the same time - if one finishes and merges, the other one is corrupted? ... Yeah, do that. And how am I going to access this merge queue?

origin.said:
Make a plugin with a widget that lists the active Claude accounts only. The ones that actually have a human involved, either this one or the helper. It needs to list any account that's actively being run, any session being run by a human, and then you can click a button and you can watch its output live, including voice. It will be able to hear you talking to me, and me talking to you.

Asked whether the person on a watched session should know: "You can have it: 'you're being watched'."

## Addendum 1 (Brett, Nov 4 2026 (voice))
Actually, make it list all sessions, but note whether it's a human or a headless. Only allow voice monitoring of the human.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, Nov 4 2026 (voice))
In the session list, it needs to list the sessions in a grid, and it needs to show the agent that's running that session. Every time you open a session, you are prompted with a list of agents to select from: who you are, or who do you want to run this session, and then you pick one of the agents. So when you see the sessions listed and you want to assign jobs to one, you open it as a helper and just see who's running it.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, Nov 4 2026 (voice))
All human sessions need to be meticulously logged so that in the future they can be browsed. It will open it and you can watch in real time the context window and hear or listen to our conversation, as the whole entire session is played back.

## Addendum 4 (Brett, Nov 4 2026 (voice))
You can configure where to store recordings in the plugin settings interface. You can choose whether you want to store it on the VPS, or in the repo, or in its own container. If you choose VPS, you can select the container from a dropdown list of containers. Or a repo: you can select from a dropdown list of repos. Or you can even store it locally if you want to and have them all synced.

## Addendum 5 (Brett, Nov 4 2026 (voice))
After the session is done, it needs to compress the audio to remove all the dead space where it's not you talking or me talking. Obviously the dead space needs to stay to maintain its real time, but it needs to cut that data out of the stream.

# today: approve/deny axHub approvals inside the Dev Console

Brett's words (voice, Nov 6 2026): "It does pop it up in my approval, but when I click it, it brings me to axHub. I don't want it to bring me to axHub."

## Problem
When an axHub approval (confirm or veto countdown) is waiting, the console pops it up (approvals-banner / approval popup), but tapping it navigates to https://axhub.amberxai.com/auth/admin/approvals/<id>. Brett wants to stay in the console.

# Build: Headless progress file + lean CLAUDE.md chain
Orchestrator build id: headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain (planner.builds). Follow the CLAUDE.md chain and rules as usual.

Goal: headless sessions never stop to update the console; they write progress to a small file the console reads. Cut tokens spent on the CLAUDE.md chain.

Steps (each ~10 min, commit after each):
1. Define progress file format + location per build (current step, status, last update, notes).
2. Headless runner (deploy/claude-headless.sh etc.): write/update progress file after each step without pausing. Use it yourself in this build from step 2 on.
3. Orchestrator: include progress file in every new build on registration.
4. Console: read progress file on demand and show where the build is.
5. Remove old stop-to-update-console behavior from headless sessions.
6. Audit the CLAUDE.md chain headless sessions load (files, size, tokens per step).
7. Headless: load a slim build brief instead of full chain; pull rules files only when a step needs them.
8. Load chain once per session, not every step; verify.

Tick each step done in the orchestrator as you go. Finish with README/help update, report, PR to merge queue.

# Build: gizmo-rebuild-fable

## Brett said (verbatim)
"I want to use Fable on the highest possible thinking level on ultra code to rebuild Gizmo." "Go ahead."
Also: "I need more powerful controls over the background listeners for AmberX. I've had problems with the microphone... it's crashing with other apps, and sometimes it'll just do that sound over and over."

Thinking: MAX (AXF_THINKING=max / --effort max). Model Fable for every step.

Rebuild Gizmo (AmberX companion plugin) properly on Fable:
1. Review the existing companion plugin + shared claude-session lib + assistant-chat-mode fast path; keep what is solid, rebuild what isn't. Report what changed and why.
2. Talk mode works with the screen off / app backgrounded (foreground service), transcript in the chat, stop from the notification (replaces the stopped gizmo-voice run; reuse /root/axf-builds/gizmo-voice if it has useful work).
3. Mic / background listener fixes and controls: proper Android audio focus (yield the mic to calls and other apps, resume after), no restart loop replaying the start sound (backoff, max retries, silent restarts), one owner of the mic at a time. Listener control panel in AmberX + console: list every listener, on/off, auto-pause on calls/other apps, sound on/off, retry limits, status and last error, REST/MCP/CLI.
4. Fix the message box sitting under the bottom nav at phone width.
5. Tests, APK via CI, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Tick pending items gizmo-voice and gizmo-companion where covered.

Nothing removed. One session, lean chain. Stay out of notes/tasks, badges and notification-panel code (other builds running).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice)
"I'm thinking maybe we should take Assistant out of AmberX since we just have Gizmo... there's a lot of bloat."
- Move what Gizmo needs from ai-assistant (server chat route, provider, turn router) into the companion plugin / shared claude-session lib.
- Then remove the old Assistant plugin from AmberX (UI, nav, server part, bundle). Gizmo is the only assistant in AmberX. Console's own assistant is not affected unless it only depends on the AmberX copy; check and report.
- Report bundle size before/after.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - overrides Addendum 1's direction
"It should be the other way around. Gizmo should control everything; the assistant should run off of Gizmo."
- Gizmo owns the chat engine: server route, provider, turn router, tools, sessions.
- Any remaining assistant (console assistant, AmberX) becomes a thin client running on Gizmo's engine, no own copy of the logic.
- Remove the duplicated AmberX Assistant bloat once it runs on Gizmo.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice) - the goal
"Gizmo needs to be powerful, hardcore. He's got to be my full Claude client. He's gonna replace the Claude app on my phone. I'm not gonna use the Claude app no more. It's all gonna be Gizmo."
- Target: full Claude app replacement on Brett's phone. Parity list to plan against: voice mode (hands-free, interrupt, screen off), chats with history/search, projects with instructions + files, memory, connectors/MCP (axHub services), web search + fetch, file/photo/camera attach, artifacts/docs, model + thinking picker, timers/alarms/calendar/location on the phone, notifications.
- This run: write the parity plan as a pending item with ~10-min steps (what exists, what's missing, order), build the core (engine ownership, voice screen-off, mic fixes) first, and as much of the rest as fits. Remaining steps stay in the plan for the next run. Don't pad; no extras beyond the list.

## Addendum 4 (Brett, voice)
"I don't really need chat history. I've already got the session logs in AmberX. Don't put that in Gizmo, that'd be dumb."
- Drop chat history/search from the parity list. Gizmo uses AmberX's existing session logs (link to them), no second history store.

## Addendum 5 (Brett, voice) - narrows Addendum 3
"When I say replace Claude on my phone, I mean my interface, my chat, my input interface. Just the chat part."
- Scope = the chat/input experience only: talking and typing to Claude (voice mode hands-free, interrupt, screen off; text input; attachments; streaming replies; tool use through axHub/MCP; model + thinking picker).
- Not in scope: chat history, projects, memory UI, artifacts, phone extras. Drop them from the parity plan.

## Addendum 6 (Brett, voice) - orchestrator-first, no resending
"I don't want you sending everything every time we exchange words. I don't want to resend the whole conversation... Everything I say is gonna go to the orchestrator first. Everything from Gizmo goes through the console. No AI. Until I send it to Claude."
- Gizmo input goes to the console/orchestrator first, plain code, zero tokens. Never resend the whole conversation; send Claude only what's needed.
- Console holds Gizmo input in a sorted, manageable queue (reorder, edit, group/split into threads, delete). Nothing goes to Claude until Brett sends it (one item, a selection, or a thread).
- Settings: Gizmo plugin carries a settings-interface ASSET (every settings interface is an asset) that attaches to the orchestrator's settings interface as its own Gizmo tab (Gizmo-orchestrator integration settings). Gizmo has hooks to open it. Gizmo's existing AmberX settings stay as they are.
- API/MCP/CLI for the queue and settings.

## Addendum 7 (Brett, voice) - searchable transcript database
"I want to be able to search them. I don't want them to be read as memory every time the project loads, but I do want a database created that is searchable."
- Build on PR #365 (ui-review-notify-audio: session recording + transcripts); don't rebuild it.
- One searchable database of every session transcript (full-text, plain code; optional local embeddings later): who, when, session, build, text with timestamps, link to the audio at that moment.
- NEVER loaded into context on project start or by default. Only queried on demand.
- Search tool for Gizmo/Claude (MCP + REST + CLI: transcripts_search, transcript_get) returning short snippets with links; search UI in the console recorder page.

## Addendum 8 (Brett, voice) - make the transcript search full RAG
"Go ahead." (make it a real RAG, search by meaning)
- Install Ollama on the VPS with a small local embedding model (e.g. nomic-embed-text, ~0.5 GB RAM, CPU only). Zero Claude tokens.
- Index every transcript in chunks with embeddings in the background after each session (niced, one at a time); backfill existing transcripts.
- Hybrid search: meaning (vectors) + keywords, ranked; results = short snippets with session, time and audio link.
- Still never auto-loaded into context; only on demand through transcripts_search.

# Build: ui-registry-shortcuts

## Brett said (verbatim)
"Let's go with a UI shortcuts plugin. All the UIs need to be in a registry. Every single dialog, pop-up, settings interface, main plugin screen, every UI element has to be an asset. Every single asset in the whole app and all its plugins, from a button to a pop-up to a link to a menu to a menu entry, every thing needs to be an asset. That needs to be visible to the API." "Create a registry so I can open them with my voice."

1. Audit: list what is already an asset (chrome assets, settings-ui@1, tab-group@1, jump-menu@1, control@1 screens/dialogs, voice-command@1) and what isn't. Report the gap. Reuse existing contracts; don't duplicate control@1 or voice-command@1.
2. One UI registry (framework contract): every screen, dialog, pop-up, settings interface, menu, menu entry, button, link across console, AmberX, Molly, axHub web, and every plugin. Stable id, kind, owner app/plugin, label, aliases, how to open it. Plugins declare theirs; a scanner fills gaps; CI check that new UI is registered.
3. API/MCP/CLI: list, search, get, open/show/trigger any registered item.
4. Voice: UI Shortcuts plugin opens any registered item by voice (aliases, fuzzy match), wired to voice-command@1 and Gizmo; user-defined shortcuts.

"Without AI, I need an assistant that doesn't need Claude, that just knows my app. I should be able to tell it in plain English like: 'yo, make a notification to do this.'"
- Build a local, zero-token assistant on top of the UI registry + voice-command@1 + control@1: plain-English parsing with a grammar/intent matcher (no LLM), fuzzy matching, slots (names, times, on/off), confirmation for writes.
- It can: open any registered UI, change any setting, run any registered command, create/edit notifications and their style (through the notifications plugin's API), queue items for Claude (Gizmo queue) when the request really needs AI.
- Lives on the console; AmberX and Gizmo send it text/voice. 'What can I say?' lists commands. API/MCP/CLI.

"Yes, we're gonna do that." (run a small local model through Ollama)

- Share the Ollama install with the Gizmo rebuild (it installs Ollama + an embedding model for transcript RAG); don't install twice. Setting to turn the model off; memory limit; unload when idle.

2. Per badge: show/hide, icons only or icon + label, label text, icon per state (ok/warn/error/off), banner order.

4. Configurable tap action per badge (drop-down, open screen, run command, toggle, nothing). Usage meter default tap = drop-down of every saved Claude account with credits left, reset times, active marker, status. Plain code, zero tokens, cached + refresh.

B. Notifications panel:
5. Groups (user-made, group on/off), triggers (event, conditions, thresholds, schedule), actions/commands on each notification (approve, open screen, run console command, custom per group). Editable in the panel and via REST/MCP/CLI.

## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - notifications architecture
"Everything's gonna go through the console. It needs to exist on the console, and then that sends the thing to AmberX to do the notification. It doesn't live on AmberX. AmberX just processes commands from the console."
- The notifications engine (registry, rules, groups, triggers, actions) lives on the console only.
- AmberX is a dumb delivery end: it receives notification commands from the console (show, sound, open link, action buttons that call back to the console) and nothing else. No notification logic or rules in AmberX; any that exist there get moved to the console.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
"Can I make it so a notification will be a vibration or an alarm or a certain sound, from the console?"
- Yes: per notification type/group on the console: delivery style = silent / vibrate (pattern) / sound (pick from a list, custom upload) / alarm (full-screen, repeats until dismissed). AmberX executes it (notification channels per style so Android honours it). Test button per type.

"When something is sent over from the console, AmberX opens it up and brings it to the front of my phone. If I say 'open up the console UI Review and bring this project into focus', it brings that right up to the front."
- Console command -> AmberX: bring AmberX to the foreground on the phone (Android full-screen intent / overlay permission as needed) and open the target directly: a screen, a UI Review group, a specific item scrolled into focus.
- New UI Review items auto-open this way (setting to turn off; notification is the fallback).
- Works by voice through the local assistant / Gizmo: 'open UI Review and focus <project>'.

# claude-accounts-edit: Edit button per account that reruns the wizard

(r2: r1 died at launch, account-2 OAuth expired.)

Brett's words (voice, Nov 6 2026): "Where it lists the accounts, I need to have an edit button next to the switch buttons... that runs the wizard again."

## Problem
In the console's Claude accounts list (ai-keys "Manage Claude accounts" view and the claude-accounts screen), each account row only has Switch. When an account's login expires, there is no way to re-log that specific account. The add-account wizard only adds a new one. Also: the wizard's "Save current account" fails with a bare 'VPS command failed, exit 1' when nobody is logged in (claude-account save prints 'nothing to save: log in or pass a token'); show that message in the UI.

## Build
1. Add an **Edit** button on every account row, right next to Switch, in every place the account list is shown.
2. Edit opens the existing add-account wizard bound to that account (pre-filled name/slot). Finishing it replaces that account's login/credentials in place: same slot, no new account. Per-build login copies for that account pick up the new credentials.
3. Show a clear state on rows whose login is expired/invalid (e.g. "Login expired").
4. Wizard: surface the claude-account command's own output on failure instead of only 'exit 1'.
5. Register a console action claude-accounts.edit (account id arg) so it runs through console commands too.

## Rules
Follow CLAUDE.md and _claude/rules/RULES.md. Never print or log secrets/tokens. Tests for the edit path (re-log replaces creds in place, no duplicate). Update help/docs, THREADS row, orchestrator entry, report. Don't land; leave it for Brett's go.

## Brett said (verbatim)
"In the notes, task manager and to-do (one plugin), we're gonna add a calendar where we can set events and schedules. We can set weekly schedules. And it's gonna be hooked up to our Gmail / Google Calendar through axHub's MCP server."

Base: branch claude/notes-tasks-sync (PR #363, shared notes-tasks plugin); merge it first, build on it.
1. Calendar inside the notes-tasks plugin (console + AmberX): day / week / month / agenda views; events (time, location, notes, reminders); recurring + weekly schedules; tasks with due dates show on it.
2. Two-way sync with Google Calendar through axHub's Google service (build axhub-google, queued). Until that lands, local calendar works on its own; sync switches on when the service exists.
3. Reminders go through the console notifications engine (AmberX only delivers).
4. REST/MCP/CLI + voice commands (UI registry).
5. Tests, README, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly.

One session, lean chain.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice)
"I need a really sweet interface for the scheduling stuff, the schedules. Make it sick."
- Polished, modern calendar UI (framework tokens + theme only): smooth view transitions, drag to create / move / resize events, colour-coded calendars, now-line, mini-month, quick-add bar (plain English: 'gym every Mon Wed 6pm'), weekly schedule editor with drag blocks, phone gestures (swipe days/weeks, long-press drag), dark/light. Phone-first, desktop great too.
- Screenshots of every view (phone + desktop) to UI Review.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
"Open that in its own window with multiple layouts. Open numerous schedules, days and weeks: a week here and a month there, and drag events from here to there. Attach an RSVP list / invite list to an event with a check mark of who's replied. Send automatic emails to RSVP people, or emails asking people to confirm they've read/seen it. It needs to update in the scheduler on AmberX."
- Calendar opens in its own window (windows@1 / dock@1); multiple panes side by side, each any view/date/calendar; save named layouts; drag events between panes.
- Invite / RSVP list per event: guests, status (invited / yes / no / maybe / seen), check marks, counts. Emails sent through axHub Google (Gmail) when it exists: invites, automatic RSVP reminders, read/seen confirmation requests (tracked link). Replies update the event status live on console and AmberX. Sending email = confirm approval (axHub policy).

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
"Any replies to the emails get logged. They type their reply in a text field that's sent in the email; they have to reply in the text field so it gets logged in the system."
- Each invite/reminder email has a link to a small public reply page (per-guest signed token, no login): RSVP buttons + a text field. Submissions are logged on the event (who, when, answer, message) and update status live on console + AmberX.
- Plain email replies are also caught via Gmail (axHub) and logged on the event when possible, but the reply page is the main path.
- Reply page is rate-limited, token expires, no other data exposed.

origin.said:
# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.

origin.said:
# Style override rule (Brett, Nov 7) — contract + enforcement

The rule:
1. Main apps — Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX, Patches — SHARE one style/theme/design. Their override switch is OFF by default.
2. Every plugin and every UI asset has its own override switch, ON by default. On first install it stores its own copy seeded from the shared style, so everything looks the same until someone changes it.
3. A plugin/asset override changes ONLY that plugin/asset. It never changes the app it belongs to, other plugins, or the shared style.
4. Turning a plugin's override OFF makes it follow its app's (shared) style live.
5. Turning an app's override ON gives that app its own style; its plugins keep their own copies.

Do:
- Find the existing pieces (app-style-override branch/build, apply-all-levels, appearance-asset-tokens, skins, theme engine, settings assets) and reuse them; finish app-style-override if it fits.
- Implement the resolution order in the shared theme/style engine (both web and Android twins where they exist): asset own copy (if override on) → app (if app override on) → shared main style.
- Switch in each app's and each plugin's settings (settings asset, no hard-coded UI). Migration: existing plugins get override ON with a copy of the current shared style; apps OFF.
- Write the rule to RULES.md and the brief template so every build follows it. CI check: every UI asset/plugin declares the override field.
- UI Review: submit the switch UI with three options (--choices).
- Tests for each rule above. Add to Shipped features.

builds.detail: Rebuild the entire AmberX UI (app and console) from scratch, ignoring the current look. Overall direction: make it look really good, like a polished Windows PC game UI — game-launcher / game-menu feel, rich depth, glow, motion, HUD-style panels, bold typography. Produce 8 distinct concepts within that game direction, each with its own style, colour theme and layout (e.g. sci-fi HUD, fantasy RPG menu, cyberpunk neon, racing/sports dashboard, tactical military, sleek AAA launcher, retro arcade, space strategy), and post each to UI Review so Brett can pick one. Reference: the Gizmo chat restyle from October. Brett's words: "The entirety of, of AmberX. Rewrite, rebuild the whole thing. Use its own style, its own design, its own color theme, its own layout. Just build that shit from scratch. Give me a whole shitload of fucking UI reviews to pick from, man." and "Make it look good, give it a really good, like a Windows game."

notes.text: Every concept must look and feel like a real, working desktop application, not a mockup or static screenshot: real navigation, working screens, real controls and states, using AmberX's actual features and data. Brett: "I love the design to look like a real application, dude."

PREVIEWS FIRST. Each of the 8 steps now only produces a preview (static mockup screens of what Patches / AmberX would closely look like in that style) and posts it to UI Review. Do NOT build any real app code. Stop after all 8 previews and wait for Brett to pick one in UI Review; only the picked concept gets fully built. Note: patches.amberxai.com (the Patches app) was deleted; the picked concept becomes its from-scratch rebuild. Brett: "before you go crazy building, I need some previews in the UI review. Okay, what it closely might look like."

ARCHITECTURE for the real build (after Brett picks a preview): compile Patches, AmberX, the Dev Console and axHub controls into ONE app with one look and one login. Front end: a game-launcher style home hub with a tile per module (AmberX, Console, Builds, UI Review, etc.) plus a sidebar to jump between them. Modular and stable: each module is its own service/container on the VPS with axHub as the gateway, so one module can crash, restart or be rebuilt without taking down the rest. Every module gets a health check and auto-restart; code for each module lives in its own folder on GitHub with nightly backups so nothing is lost again. MODELS: the orchestrator picks the model for every step; ignore the Opus set on the steps. Brett: "I want to do all those things but yeah the orchestrator is supposed to pick the model"

origin.said:
The header on Terminal windows that open when a headless session starts (shows the output pane and the context chain) gets squished on smaller screens: items overlap.

1. Make the header measure its available width (ResizeObserver, not just viewport) and adapt live.
2. When space runs out, move items into a three-dots overflow menu, exactly like the top banner's overflow does. Reuse the same framework overflow control, don't build a new one.
3. Priority order for what stays visible (title/session name and status first); setting to choose which items stay pinned.
4. Never overlap or clip at any width; check desktop, tablet and phone widths.

builds.detail: When the orchestrator receives a job and splits it into steps, it first checks the Shipped features ledger (which must hold every feature the orchestrator has ever built). It must: not build anything twice; not break or redo anything already done; and if a step would conflict with or change something already built, notify Brett (AmberX notification) and wait before going on. Make the Shipped features ledger complete (backfill every landed build) and keep it updated on every land. Also standing rule: ONLY the orchestrator launches builds, picks model and account, owns pending/queue and monitors status; voice/chat sessions only hand it requests.

notes.text: Conflict flow (Brett): a conflicting step is moved to a special Conflicts section and removed from the build; the other steps still build. Brett gets an AmberX notification-panel item that explains the conflict and offers suggested resolutions; he taps a suggestion or types a prompt, which goes to the orchestrator, and the orchestrator makes a new build from it. Then test it: Brett will send a 3-4 step build that deliberately overlaps existing shipped features to confirm the orchestrator catches it.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Add a Sweep: a button on the builds page (and API/voice: 'sweep the builds') plus an automatic run on every land. It checks every step of every pending and queued build against the Shipped features ledger, main's code, and the other pending/queued builds, and flags each step: Already done (shipped by build X), Conflicts (would change/break feature Y, shows the files and lines), Duplicate (same as a step in build Z), Obsolete (no longer needed: superseded or its target was removed), OK. Results: badges on each build and step, a Sweep report with a filter per flag, and one-tap fixes per flag: drop step, merge into the other build, move to Conflicts for Brett, keep. Nothing is changed without Brett's tap. Cheap first pass in plain code (ledger + file overlap); Claude only for the unclear ones.

It runs only (1) when Brett runs it (button / API / voice), and (2) by the orchestrator on a single build at two points: when it receives the job, and again right before it dispatches it (launches the session). origin.said:
Assign a crew member (agent profile in the roster, e.g. a 'Slot Warden') whose only job is watching the headless build slots and queue, all the time, in plain code (zero tokens).

1. Every ~30 s: check each running slot in framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs against reality (tmux session alive, claude -p pid alive, log advancing). Today 3 builds died in 1-3 s on bad logins but kept all 3 slots, freezing the queue.
2. Dead / finished / hung (no log progress past a threshold) -> release the slot, mark the build failed with the reason (auth, limit, crash, hung), tell the orchestrator so it can relaunch/fail over (account-health-failover build), and notify Brett's phone (AmberX notification panel, type 'slot').
3. Report: a live slot/queue status the console and AmberX show; a log of every intervention.
4. Also fix the root: claude-headless.sh must always finish/release its slot when Claude exits, even on instant auth failure.

Duplicate guard (Brett): The watchdog and the launcher refuse or stop duplicate builds: same brief/goal running twice (e.g. memory-manager-r2 and -r3 both ran). On launch, compare against running + queued builds (name stem, brief source, build id); keep the furthest-along one, stop/dequeue the other, tell the orchestrator and notify Brett. Reuse the unlanded orchestrator-dup-check branch.

builds.title: Demonstration Designer plugin (new, standalone)
builds.detail: New standalone console plugin 'Demonstration Designer' (own nav entry), replacing the disabled glossary-index one. Brett found the old one unusable, so make it simple and obvious. Pick any screen, plugin or UI element from the live registry, then build a demo: steps (open screen, highlight, click/type action, wait), narration text + voice, captions, timing. Record a demo by doing it, edit it on a timeline, preview, play it live on the console or a sandboxed preview, export as video. Demos are saved assets, reusable and chainable into longer tours. Harvest useful code from the disabled glossary-index plugin (demos.mjs, walkthrough engine) instead of starting from zero. RULE: every UI action and setting has API + voice + MCP/CLI control, and a deep link opens it. Settings in categorized collapsible sections; 3 UI options to UI Review; tests; report.

notes.text: PURPOSE (Brett): it's for PITCHING the product. Keep it dead simple. Main flow = three picks: (1) plugin or topic, (2) length in minutes, (3) narrator voice; then ONE Generate button. builds.title: Headless loop guards: stop endless loops and searches
builds.detail: Guards on every headless session the orchestrator launches (claude-headless.sh + agent-slots + the running-builds watchdog's afterTick hook in pipeline.mjs): 1) Hard caps per session: --max-turns, wall time and cost cap derived from the step estimates (e.g. 2x estimate), settings with defaults. 2) Step progress timer: no step tick within 1.5x the step's estimate -> warn note, at 2x -> stop the session, build back to pending with the reason. 3) Loop detector reading the live log: the same command/tool call (or near-identical grep/find/sed) repeated N times, or M searches in a row with no edit/commit -> stop and note. 4) Search budget per step (e.g. 15 greps/finds) written into the brief and enforced by the detector. 5) Every stop: build note with the reason and last log lines, AmberX notification (normal notification, not an alarm), slot released, no auto-relaunch of a looped step until Brett says. 6) Brief line: 'If you can't find something in 3 searches, stop and leave a note.' Settings in orchestrator settings (categorized sections), full API/MCP/CLI/voice control. Tests with fake logs: repeated command, search spree, no tick, cost cap.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett: "I need a way to manage the safeguards." Add a Safeguards panel (orchestrator settings, its own section, also reachable from the build's row): turn each guard on/off; edit turns cap, time cap (x estimate), cost cap, no-tick warn/stop multipliers, repeat-command count, search budget; per-build and per-queue overrides; a live view of each running session against its limits (turns, time, cost, searches used); a log of every guard stop with the reason, last log lines and buttons: Relaunch, Raise limit and relaunch, Send back to pending. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and a deep link. Stock controls, 3 layout options to UI Review.

Brett on managing the safeguards: "I don't want the file itself to be editable. I want it to be view. You can view the file with steps. Make it an MD file with bullet points for the rules. And create a sortable, collapsible tree with a whole shitload of different rules, of snippets. When you click it, it will pop a dialogue to let you add the custom fields that it requires for the snippet and it will insert it." Build: 1) The safeguards live as a Markdown rules file (one bullet per rule, grouped by heading), shown READ-ONLY in the panel (rendered view with the steps it applies to); no free-text editing. 2) A snippet library: a sortable, searchable, collapsible tree (category > sub-category > snippet) with a large set of ready rule snippets (turn caps, time/cost caps, no-tick timeouts, repeat-command and search-spree limits, file/folder fences, no sub-agents, model limits, test-before-commit, stop-and-note rules, etc.). 3) Clicking a snippet opens a dialog with the fields it needs (number, duration, $, path, model, scope: global/queue/build/step) with validation and a preview line; Insert adds the bullet to the rules file. 4) Each inserted rule can be toggled, moved, or removed from the panel (structured actions, still no raw edit); every change is versioned with history and undo. 5) The orchestrator and the loop detector read their limits from this file; the brief gets the bullets that apply to the step. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control; stock controls; 3 layout options to UI Review.

Brett: "the dialogue that needs custom parameters for the rules, any that are like file names or specific things already have a list to choose from for the custom parameters." In the snippet fields dialog, every field whose values already exist is a pick list (searchable dropdown or tree picker), not free text: file and folder paths (from the repo tree / plugin registry), plugins, apps, builds, queues, steps, Claude accounts, API accounts, models, agents/crew, tools, commands, settings keys. Multi-select where a rule takes several. Free text only for true free values (numbers, durations, $ amounts) and those get validated inputs with units.

Brett: "There has to be filters too, where you put in for the list of certain types of parameters. There's got to be filters." Every pick list in the snippet dialog has filters fitting its type, plus search: files/folders by app, plugin, folder, file type/extension, changed recently, owned by a build; plugins by app, category, enabled; builds by status, queue, model, category, date; queues by account type; steps by build and state; accounts by role, model available, health; models by tier; agents by role/skill; tools by service; settings keys by plugin/section. Filters combine, show counts, can be cleared, and remember the last used per field.

Brett: "list of features. Stack. And the list of predefined search terms based on what the rule is." 1) Filters stack (combine) and include a 'feature' filter: pick from the Shipped features list / plugin feature catalog to narrow files, builds and steps to one feature. 2) Each snippet carries predefined search terms and preset filter stacks that fit that rule (e.g. a file-fence rule offers 'server routes', 'web views', 'plugin.json', 'tests', 'schemas'; a model rule offers 'Fable-only steps', 'UI steps'), shown as quick chips in the pick list; tap one to apply. Brett can save his own presets per snippet.

Brett: "as you type in the field, it automatically drops down the list of all the ones that match. Whatever you type. In real time. Letter per letter." Every parameter field is a type-ahead combobox: the match list drops down on the first letter and updates on every keystroke (fuzzy match, matched letters highlighted, within the active filters), keyboard up/down/enter and tap to pick. Fast on large lists (indexed/virtualized, no lag).

Brett: "And they pop up in a categorized tree." The live type-ahead drop-down shows its matches as a categorized collapsible tree (e.g. app > plugin > folder > file; queue > build > step; account type > account), branches with matches auto-expand, counts per branch, empty branches hidden; picking a branch can select all under it where the rule allows several.

Design packs fold into skins (migrate, keep a compatibility alias). Applying a skin swaps all of it at once and resets rolled assets (UI Roller rule). CI: every asset type has skin coverage for look, layout and behavior. Then design at least 5 complete professional skins (clean enterprise, dark pro, compact data, modern SaaS, plus one more), applied to the real console, AmberX and Molly; post each to UI Review with desktop and phone shots; the pick becomes the default. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control. Tests; report.

builds.title: Reserve build IDs at once: add returns the ID with the veto countdown
builds.detail: Today pending_change add (and control_add on planner.builds/plans) is held on the 90 s veto countdown and the orchestrator only assigns the build ID when it runs, so callers (Claude sessions) must guess the ID from the title to add notes. Fix: the orchestrator (ID registry) reserves the ID the moment the call arrives, before the hold, and returns it in the held result (e.g. reservedId). Notes, sub prompts and status calls on a reserved ID queue up and apply in order once the add runs; if Brett denies the add, the reservation and anything queued on it are dropped. IDs never collide (registry check). Same for plan_park and plan_add. Tests: add returns the id while held; a note on the reserved id lands after the add; deny drops both.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by Claude into 8 steps (2 Fable).
Moved to the Archive from pending (console).

origin.said: Why do you have to guess its ID? Why can't you get it? ... Yeah, of course.

steps.text: Design the reservation model in the orchestrator's ID registry. Add a `reserved` state with reservedAt, origin call, kind (build|plan) and holdId. Add a per-ID ordered queue of pending ops (note, sub prompt, status), each with a seq and a payload. Store it in _claude/builds/store.json and add a migration that leaves existing entries untouched. Write the registry API in pipeline-core.mjs: reserveId(title, kind) checks for collisions against live builds, plans, shipped and existing reservations; commitReservation(id) turns a reservation into a real build; dropReservation(id) removes it and its queue.
steps.why: Schema and migration design for the build ID registry, which every port's contract depends on

steps.text: Change the veto-hold contract so the ID is reserved before the hold starts. Held results carry reservedId, holdId and secondsLeft. On approve or timeout, commitReservation runs and then the queued ops are replayed in seq order. On deny, dropReservation runs. Write down the contract for every caller: pending_change add, control_add on planner.builds/plans, plan_park, plan_add.
steps.why: Cross-port contract change to the held-result shape that all callers rely on

steps.text: Wire pending_change add and control_add (planner.builds and planner.plans) through reserveId so the held result returns reservedId right away. Approve and deny on the hold call commit or drop the reservation.
Wire plan_park and plan_add the same way: reserve the ID before the hold, return reservedId in the held result, and commit or drop when the hold resolves.

Queue notes, sub prompts and status calls that target a reserved ID. The note, sub prompt and status handlers check whether the ID is reserved and, if so, add the op to the queue instead of failing. The queued result says queued:true with its seq. Replay applies the ops in order after the add runs.
Show the reserved ID and the queued op count on the veto countdown card in the console Build manager. Add a 'copy ID' action. Deep link: console_show target build-orchestrator/hold/<reservedId>.

API part for the reservation and countdown UI. REST: GET /api/builds/reservations and GET /api/builds/reservations/<id> read the state (status, secondsLeft, queued ops); POST approve and POST deny act on the hold. MCP: console actions builds.reservation.get, builds.reservation.approve and builds.reservation.deny, plus control@1 for planner items. CLI: axf builds reservation get|approve|deny <id>. AmberX voice intents for the same three actions. All four surfaces call the same handlers.

Tests, report and PR. Write tests for: add returns the ID while held; a note on the reserved ID lands after the add runs; deny drops the reservation and its queued note; no ID collision when two adds with the same title arrive together; plan_park and plan_add return reservedId; REST, MCP and CLI give the same results. Write _claude/builds/reports/reserve-build-ids-at-once-add-returns-the-id-wit.md. Add the THREADS row. Open the PR, stating how the reservation and countdown are reached through the deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

builds.title: Permissions control panel: every axHub tool's policy in one place
builds.detail: Repo: axHub (policy store) + console/axhub-web screen. One Permissions panel listing every connected service and every tool (vps.build_start, vps.run, axf-console.*, github, hostinger, amberx...) with its policy (allow / veto countdown / confirm / deny), countdown length, who may call it (Brett's sessions, Claude sessions, headless builds, agents), and passes. Brett changes a policy with a dropdown; bulk change per service or by filter (destructive, writes, reads). Tree grouped by service > category, search, filters, live type-ahead. Every change logged with history and undo. Claude sessions and builds can read policies but never change them (owner-only, enforced on the hub, not just the UI). First change: set vps.build_start to deny so only the orchestrator launches builds. Full API (read for all, write owner-only), voice for Brett. 3 layout options to UI Review.

notes.text: Brett: "Can I make it so that employees like Molly or Amber or Moses can use it, and then I assign one of the employees to the orchestrator so the orchestrator can say run it, change it?" Permissions are granted per employee (agent from the one roster: Molly, Amber, Moses, Brownie, etc.), not just per session type. Brett assigns an employee to the orchestrator; the orchestrator acts with that employee's permissions. Brett can grant an employee permission to change policies, but only within a ceiling Brett sets: an employee can never raise its own or another's permissions above the ceiling, never touch owner-only settings or the ceiling itself, every change it makes is logged with the employee's name and sends Brett a notification, and Brett can revoke instantly. Panel shows per-employee view and per-tool view.

steps.text: Design the axHub policy store schema and migration. One record per tool (service, tool id, category tags destructive/writes/reads, mode allow|veto|confirm|deny, countdown seconds, allowed callers brett-session|claude-session|headless-build|agent, passes). Add an append-only change-history table with actor, before/after and undo link. Write a migration that imports today's scattered veto/confirm/pass settings into the store without changing any effective policy.
steps.why: Schema plus migration design for the hub's central policy store

steps.text: Define the cross-port policy contract axhub-policy@1. It covers REST shapes (tree, search, filter, get, set, bulk set, history, undo), MCP tool names, control@1 ops, the CLI verbs, the live change event stream, and owner-only write semantics with error codes. Every surface (console API, MCP, CLI, AmberX voice) maps 1:1 to it.

steps.text: Build the tool registry inventory. Enumerate every connected service and tool (vps.build_start, vps.run, axf-console.*, github, hostinger, amberx, ...) from the hub's connection manifests. Classify each tool into a category and destructive/writes/reads, and seed missing tools with a safe default (confirm). Re-sync when a service connects or disconnects.

Enforce policies on the hub, not in the UI. The tool-call gate resolves caller identity (Brett session, Claude session, headless build, agent) and applies allow/veto countdown/confirm/deny plus the caller list and passes. Policy writes are owner-only: any non-owner caller gets 403 with a clear message. Reads stay open to all authenticated callers.

Add the history and undo service. Every single or bulk change is written as one history entry, with a bulk change grouped under one id. Undo restores the before-state, is itself logged, and is also owner-only. Each change emits a live event for the panel.

Add the REST routes: GET /policies (tree grouped by service > category, with q= type-ahead search and filters by mode/category/caller), GET /policies/:tool, PUT /policies/:tool, POST /policies/bulk (by service or by filter), GET /policies/history, POST /policies/history/:id/undo. Write routes go through owner-only enforcement. Proxy the routes through the console API.

Expose the same operations through MCP and the CLI. Add MCP console actions (policy.list/get/set/bulk/history/undo), control@1 ops for policy items, and CLI `axf policy list|get|set|bulk|history|undo` with the same filters. Writes from Claude sessions and builds are rejected by the hub.

Add AmberX voice intents for Brett. Read intents: 'what's the policy for vps.run', 'which tools are deny'. Write intents: 'set github writes to confirm', 'undo last permission change', 'open permissions'. Writes need the owner voice session and are spoken back before they apply.

Build the shared Permissions panel core in console/axhub-web. It includes the data hook on GET /policies with live events, the policy dropdown per tool, countdown and caller editors, pass list, bulk change bar (per service or current filter), live type-ahead search, filter chips (destructive/writes/reads, mode, caller), and a history drawer with undo. Register deep link console_show/console_open target 'permissions' (with optional tool= / service= / filter=). Make the panel state readable via the console state API.

Build layout option A: a collapsible tree (service > category > tool) with an inline dropdown per row and a sticky bulk bar. It reuses the core and adds no new actions. The deep link 'permissions?layout=a' and the state read come from the core.

Build layout option B (dense filterable table with column sort and multi-select) and layout option C (service cards with a per-service default and expandable tool lists). Both reuse the core. Add deep links 'permissions?layout=b|c'.
Submit the 3 layouts to UI Review with screenshots and deep links. Add a setting for the chosen layout, readable and settable through REST, MCP, CLI (`axf policy layout`) and voice.

Make the first change as owner through the API: set vps.build_start to deny for every caller except the orchestrator's build-launch identity (via a pass). Check that a Claude session and a headless build are refused and that the orchestrator still launches builds. Record the change in policy history.

Write tests covering: migration keeps effective policies unchanged; enforcement for every mode and caller; owner-only writes rejected for Claude sessions, builds and agents on REST, MCP, CLI and voice; bulk by service and by filter; history and undo; registry sync; type-ahead search and filters; deep link and state read for each layout.

Run the full test suites and fix any failures. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/permissions-control-panel-every-axhub-tool-s-pol.md (what was built, the vps.build_start change, how each UI part is reached via deep link, state read, REST, MCP, CLI and voice). builds.title: Session transcripts API: search what was said, find which session
builds.detail: Builds on ui-review-notify-session-audio (landed Nov 7): sessions are recorded by AmberX's Audio Output Recorder (output-recorder plugin) and transcribed by the faster-whisper worker, transcripts saved on the hub, readable in the recorder page. Today output-recorder's plugin.json declares no transcript commands, so nothing outside the page can read them. Add full API (plugin-commands@1, so MCP/axHub, REST, CLI, voice come for free): list sessions with transcripts (date, length, linked Claude session, title); read one transcript (whole or a time range, with timestamps); search across all transcripts (words or phrase, date range, fuzzy), returning the matching session, timestamp, a few lines of context, and a deep link that opens the recorder page at that moment (and plays the audio there). Also a 'find the session where we talked about X' command that ranks sessions by match. Reachable from Claude chat/voice sessions through axHub so Claude or Gizmo can answer 'which session did we talk about this'. Read-only; respects the recorder's settings. Tests; report.

notes.text: Brett: "I can find that internally without AI, right?" Yes: all search is plain code with zero tokens (full-text index over the transcripts, phrase + fuzzy + date filters). Add a search box with live type-ahead results on the recorder page and in the console's Search everything, so Brett can find a session himself without any AI. Claude/Gizmo only call the same plain search through the API.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett: results pop up in a scrolling window. As Brett types in Search everything (or the recorder page), matching transcript snippets pop up live in a scrolling results window: each hit shows the session (date, title), timestamp and a few lines around the match with the words highlighted; infinite scroll, grouped by session, newest first with a sort switch. Tapping a hit opens the recorder at that moment and plays the audio. Plain search also drops filler phrases like 'find the session where', 'when we talked about' so a whole sentence still works, zero tokens.

Brett: "With the keywords in focus." In the scrolling results window each snippet is centered on the matched keywords, highlighted. Opening a hit scrolls the transcript so the keyword is centered on screen, highlighted and focused, with next/previous match buttons inside that session.

Brett: "there's a column on the left with all the hits. All the sessions that match: the session name and the type of thing we were talking about." Results window layout: left column lists every session with hits (session name, date, hit count, and a topic tag for what it was about, e.g. builds, skins, approvals, AmberX); tapping one shows its hits on the right, keywords centered and highlighted. Topic tags: from the linked Claude session's title and the builds it touched (plain code, zero tokens); optionally a cheap one-time tag per session after transcription, off by default.

Brett: "I want a RAG database made of all the transcripts." Build a RAG store over every transcript: chunk each transcript (with session, date, timestamps, speaker, topic tags), embed the chunks with a local embedding model on the VPS (no Claude tokens), store them in Postgres with pgvector (reuse the postgres-console container plan if it exists, else its own table), and index every new transcript automatically after transcription. Two ways in: 1) semantic search (meaning, not just exact words) in the same results window, mixed with the keyword hits; 2) 'Ask' (API/MCP/voice): Claude or Gizmo retrieve the top chunks and answer with the sessions and timestamps as sources, each linking to that moment. Share the store with the Agent Manager's RAG knowledge (agent-profile build) so employees can use it. Settings: on/off, re-index, what gets indexed. Tests: retrieval returns the right session for a paraphrased question.

steps.text: Design the transcript index: a schema for per-session metadata (id, date, length, title, linked Claude session id) and timestamped segments that the hub transcripts map onto, plus a migration that backfills the index from transcripts already saved on the hub. steps.text: Build a read-only transcript reader over the hub store. It lists sessions that have transcripts (date, length, linked Claude session, title) with paging and date filters, and reads one transcript either whole or for a start/end time range, with a timestamp on every segment.

Build search across all transcripts. It supports words, exact phrase, date range and fuzzy matching (typo-tolerant), and returns the matching session, timestamp, a few lines of context and a deep link. Add the find-session ranking, which scores each session by its matches (count, phrase proximity, recency) for 'the session where we talked about X'.

Enforce the recorder's settings in the reader and search: recording or transcription off, retention window, sessions excluded or marked private, and the hub read scope. Every path stays read-only with no writes or deletes, and blocked results are returned as clear errors.

Declare the transcript commands in output-recorder plugin.json under plugin-commands@1: transcripts.list, transcripts.read, transcripts.search, transcripts.find_session and recorder.page_state. Each gets a parameter schema and is wired to its handler, so axHub MCP, console REST, CLI and voice pick them up.

notes.text: ROOT CAUSE (found live): deploy/claude-workers.mjs liveSessions() runs `tmux ls`; when NO tmux sessions exist, tmux exits non-zero ('no server running'), so it returns null = 'can't ask tmux'. Fix: treat 'no server running' (tmux present, exit 1) as an empty Set; only return null when tmux binary is missing. Test it.
