builds.title: Split builds pages: Build Manager = Pending + Complete; Orchestrator = Queued + Active
builds.detail: Replaces one-builds-page-pending-queued-built-tabs-remove (mark superseded). Build Manager owns builds before and after the orchestrator: Pending tab (create, edit, prioritize, Send to orchestrator) and Complete tab (finished builds sent back by the orchestrator, with account that actually built it, model, cost, PR, land status). Build orchestrator owns only what it was sent: Queued and Active tabs, with steps, assigned/actual account, model, progress and actions (route, assign account, hold, cancel/return to Pending). builds.title: Saved Claude logins never end up on a spent refresh token
builds.detail: Builds run on a per-build copy of a saved login (claude-login.mjs). Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). Fix: find every path where the rotation is lost (crash, kill, exit 1, sweep timing, two builds refreshing the same login at once), write rotations back atomically with a lock, never let two copies refresh the same login concurrently, and before launch check the saved login is alive; if dead, skip that account, alert the phone, and don't burn runs on it. Tests for each path.

builds.title: Skins as packages of slices: every section its own asset, pick sections on apply, mix creates a new skin via dialog, drag-and-drop Skin Builder
builds.detail: Upgrade the existing skins/appearance system and asset registry; don't build a parallel one. 1) DATA MODEL: a skin is only a package (manifest) referencing section assets. Every section (colours, layouts, design/visual styles, behaviour, and every other category a skin covers) is its own standalone asset with a name, preview, tags and source. Convert every existing skin into this form, with no monolithic skins left. 2) APPLY WITH PICKS: when you apply, enable or change a skin, a dialog lists its sections with checkboxes and previews. Choose which sections to take and which to leave out; left-out sections keep the current skin's. 3) MIX = NEW SKIN: if the result mixes sections from more than one skin, a dialog asks you to save it as a new skin (name, description, thumbnail auto-captured), with Save as new, Apply without saving, or Cancel. 4) SKIN BUILDER: a slice library (searchable, by category, live hover preview) and a pack template with one slot per category. Drag slices into slots, preview the whole console live, see which slots are empty, swap or clear slots, before/after toggle. Save, apply, export or import as a file, duplicate, edit later. 5) Professional polish: snap animations, slot highlights, desktop and phone layouts. 6) Full control via REST, MCP, CLI and voice (list sections, save section, apply with includes/excludes, build skin from sections, export). Screenshots go to UI Review grouped by screen.

builds.title: One VPS plugin: everything VPS in one place (gauges, banner widget with heat-colour icons and dropdown, cleanup, settings, status)
builds.detail: ONE VPS plugin (e.g. 'VPS'), reachable from Maintenance and its own nav entry. 1) CONSOLIDATE: find every VPS-related feature across the console and move it into this plugin as tabs or sections, leaving no duplicates behind. That includes the claude-badge VPS check, agent-slots resource and swap settings and warnings, the VPS settings/orchestrator-only rule plugin (from vps-orchestrator-only-rule-vps-settings-console), Docker/container views, container-access, the Coolify/Hostinger links, VPS terminal shortcuts, ai-keys VPS sync, maintenance cleanup/redundancy scans, the disk alerts, and the running-builds watchdog's resource bits. Old entry points redirect to the new plugin. 2) STATUS tab: live gauges and meters for CPU load (1/5/15 min), RAM, swap, disk per filesystem, plus Docker per-container CPU/RAM and the top processes. Several views (radial, bars, compact strip, history sparklines), switchable and remembered, with adjustable thresholds. 3) BANNER WIDGET: a snappable widget for the banner, toolbars and title bars, with modes icon only, icon plus value, or mini meters. It has its own settings (metrics, mode, thresholds, refresh). 4) ICON-ONLY HEAT COLOUR: each icon's colour follows its level on a smooth scale, white (low) to gray to black to red (high). The stops are editable and the theme can override them. 5) BANNER DROPDOWN: clicking any banner gauge opens a dropdown listing every gauge, one row each: a dot in the same heat colour as that gauge, the name (Load, RAM, Swap, Disk /), the percentage, and the actual values (e.g. 9.4 / 16 GB). Rows update live, the clicked one is highlighted, and the footer has Open VPS plugin and quick cleanup links. 6) CLEANUP tab: docker builder/image/container prune, apt/npm/pip caches, journal vacuum, old build worktrees and logs, /tmp, the Playwright cache, and stale git locks. Each has a size preview and a confirm, shows the space freed and logs to the fix log. Optional auto-cleanup over a threshold (off by default). 7) SETTINGS tab: every VPS setting in one place. Plain code, no AI. Full REST, MCP, CLI and voice control. Desktop and phone screenshots go to UI Review.

origin.said: I need a settings on the approval page to allow all for the next hour or two hours or a custom field that I can enter, or deny all for a custom field. Until a certain time or amount of time. And where's the switch? A setting to control the time of the 90 seconds.

steps.text: Design the approval policy schema and migration: a 'window' record (mode allow|deny, starts_at, ends_at, created_by, source ui|rest|mcp|cli|voice, cancelled_at) and a 'veto_countdown_sec' setting (default 90, bounds 10–3600). Only one active window at a time; a new window replaces the old one. Write the migration so existing installs keep 90 s and have no window. Document the contract in the approvals schema doc.
steps.why: Schema + migration design for persisted approval policy shared by server, MCP, CLI and voice

steps.text: Engine: before an approval is queued, check the active window. In an allow window, auto-approve it; in a deny window, auto-deny it. Log every auto-decision with the window id. Expire windows lazily on read and with a timer so expiry clears without a restart. Replace the hard-coded 90 s veto countdown with the veto_countdown_sec setting, read when each countdown starts.

Policy service: setWindow({mode, duration|until}), cancelWindow(), getPolicy() returning the active window with remaining time, and get/set veto_countdown_sec. REST routes: GET /api/approvals/policy, POST /api/approvals/policy/window ({mode:'allow'|'deny', minutes | until}), DELETE /api/approvals/policy/window, GET/PUT /api/approvals/policy/veto-countdown. Use the existing console auth and audit logging.

origin.said: I don't want to archive. I want to move to another, you know how we set it up from multiple projects. Each one has its own builds, its own notes, all that. Make a new project, remove those from this project and move them to the new project.

steps.text: Design the project contract. Write the project manifest schema covering id, name, created, and the builds, notes and data roots. Define move-build semantics: a build's store entry, journal lines, notes, steps, branches, PR links, reports, shipped records and change entries all move together and keep their ids. Specify the order of operations so a move is atomic (write the target with tmp files, then remove from the source, roll back on failure) and how id collisions are handled. Confirm that a project switch already switches all build data, and write the contract to a doc.
steps.why: Cross-project data contract and schema design that every later step and app depends on

steps.text: Build the createProject core library. Validate the manifest against the schema, scaffold the project's own builds, notes and data folders, register it in the projects registry and the /projects hub sync, and refuse duplicate ids. It is a pure function with no AI. Add unit tests.

Build the moveBuilds core library, following the contract from step 1. Move the selected builds between projects: store entries, journal entries, notes, steps, reports, shipped records and change-entry refs. Git branches and PRs are left untouched, but their references are kept. Writes are atomic with rollback, and a dry-run returns the planned list. Nothing is deleted or archived; the source only loses the moved entries. Add unit tests, including a failure halfway through a move.

Add REST routes for the console API. POST /api/projects creates a project. GET /api/projects and GET /api/projects/:id read state. POST /api/projects/:id/move-builds takes {buildIds|filter:{state,createdBefore}, dryRun} and moves builds. GET /api/projects/:id/builds lists a project's builds. Add route tests.

Expose the same actions through the other three channels, all calling the same library functions with the same arguments. MCP: console actions project.create, project.list, project.get and project.moveBuilds. CLI: axf project create|list|show|move-builds with --dry-run, --state and --created-before. Voice: AmberX intents for 'create project X' and 'move builds to project X'.

Add the UI. A New project dialog in the project picker. In the Build manager, multi-select with a 'Move to project…' action that shows a dry-run preview and asks for confirmation. Add the deep links console_show/console_open targets projects/new, projects/<id> and builds/move?ids=…, register them, and make dialog state readable through the API from step 4.

Run end-to-end tests of create and move on a scratch fixture through REST, MCP and CLI. Check that the results match across channels, that history and notes are intact after a move, that switching to the target project shows the moved builds, and that the source no longer lists them.

Do a dry run against the real data. Using the API, list every build in the current project (amberx-axf) whose state is Pending and that was created before 2026-11-08T00:00. Save the list with ids, titles, created dates and branches. Confirm that builds from 2026-11-08 onward are excluded.

Do the real move. Create the new project through the API (id amberx-axf-backlog unless one is already defined, and record the chosen name). Move the dry-run list into it. Verify the counts before and after, check that every moved build's notes, steps, journal and branch refs are present in the target, and confirm nothing was deleted or archived. Commit the data changes.

Finish the build. Run the full test suite. Write the report to _claude/builds/reports/projects-create-a-new-project-and-move-builds-be.md, including the moved-builds list and how each feature is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Add the THREADS row. Open the PR, with the API access paths listed in its description.

## What to build

A master switch in the main application settings to enable inline edit mode. Same with navigation menus, toolbars, banners, widgets, every single thing. Part of the plugin gives a monster list of everything changed from axHub's inheritance, reset them individually to axHub's. API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

[ ] s1 (~30 min) Define the element-token addressing contract for the GUI framework. Give every framework element a stable token path: app menu items and sub-menus down to the child, navigation menus, toolbars, banners and widgets. Add a resolver that, for any element and each of its parents, lists every settable token (text color, background, border, font, spacing and so on) with its current value and where it was inherited from in axHub. Write the contract doc.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) Design the override schema and its migration. Each override record holds the token path, the scope (single item or parent), the token, the value, the axHub value it replaced, who changed it and when. Build the store module with get, set, unset and list, and migrate existing overrides into the new schema.

When the mode is off it is not attached at all, and it leaves native and app context menus alone.

steps.text: Scaffold the inline-edit plugin. Add the master switch 'Inline edit mode' to the main app settings, persisted, and wire it to attach or detach the capture layer.

Master switch API. Deep link: console_open target settings/inline-edit. State read and on/off/toggle through REST (GET/PUT /api/inline-edit/mode), an MCP console action and plugin command, the CLI (axf inline-edit mode on|off|status) and an AmberX voice intent.

Build the edit dialog shell. It shows the element breadcrumb (child up to the root) and a scope picker for this item or a chosen parent. A visible note says that changes override axHub inheritance under the existing override rules, and each token shows its inherited axHub value.

Add the dialog's three views: tree, classic tree and grid with expandable rows. Add per-token editors (color picker, size, font, text) that write through the overrides store, plus a per-token 'revert to axHub' button. Previews are live.

Edit dialog API. Deep link: console_show/console_open target inline-edit/element?path=<token path>&scope=&view=. State read returns the tokens with their values and sources for any path. Set and unset a token at item or parent scope, and change the view. All of it through REST, MCP (console action plus control@1 for tokens), the CLI (axf inline-edit tokens|set|unset) and voice.

Tests. Unit tests for the store, the resolver and single-item reset. API parity tests showing REST, MCP, CLI and voice behave the same. A UI test for right-click to edit to reset. Then write the report at _claude/builds/reports/inline-element-editing-plugin-right-click-any-el.md, add the THREADS row, and open a PR that lists how each UI is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

origin.said: Fix the top bar of the AmberX app because it's behind my top banner where my call notifications are. It renders the web page too high up for the screen. The top row is hidden. The banner's behind stuff like my camera.

steps.text: Locate the AmberX Android WebView host (activity/fragment, theme, manifest) and the web shell's top-banner CSS; note current edge-to-edge setup (enableEdgeToEdge / setDecorFitsSystemWindows, windowLayoutInDisplayCutoutMode, viewport meta) and record findings in the build notes.

No new settings or actions are added (layout fix only).

Tests: add an instrumented/Robolectric test that dispatches fake WindowInsets (status bar 32dp + top cutout, then landscape side cutout) and asserts the WebView container padding; add a web unit test for the safe-area CSS variables; add an API test for the insets state read across REST/MCP/CLI.

Build the debug APK, install on the paired phone via adb, verify portrait and landscape (with an active call notification) that the top row is fully visible and not under the status bar or camera cutout; capture adb screenshots plus the insets state read output as evidence.

Run the full test suites, write the report (_claude/builds/reports/amberx-android-web-view-top-banner-hidden-behind.md) with before/after screenshots and how the insets state is reached via deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice, add the THREADS row, and open the PR stating the same API reach.

builds.title: Dispatcher: a worktree store write can erase a fresh launch record (double launch, then a stuck build)
builds.detail: Seen on pass-approval-hook-deep-link-amberx-notification, Nov 10 2026 (journal _claude/builds/journal/2026-11-p4.jsonl): 18:11:16 pipeline:launch wrote status running + pipeline.session earl; 18:11:19 the worktree's orchestrator:note ('Claude account: ...', written by claude-headless.sh at start from a store copy taken before the launch) landed with status queued and no pipeline record, and the per-build newer-wins merge kept it; 18:12:11 the next tick launched the same build again (gina), both runs numbered 1. Earl's 's1 done' tick at 18:24:48 erased the second record the same way, so the live build sat in 'running' with no session: checkEnds and reapBuilds both skip a build without pipeline.session / pipeline.account, so the phase end was never handled (set to queued by hand). Fix, in this order: (1) builds-merge-core: merge the pipeline record per field, never let an incoming copy with no pipeline record replace a newer launch record on main (or have orchestrator.mjs act pull main's record before a note/tick write); (2) pipeline-core plan(): never launch a build whose status is running/waiting or that has a running or queued agent slot for its id (agent-slots status lists build per slot); (3) checkEnds/reapBuilds: a build 'running' with no pipeline record and no live slot for it ends by the phase rule (exit 0 + model switch -> queued) instead of being skipped forever; (4) claude-headless.sh: write the 'Claude account' note only after the launch record is published, or through the per-field merge. Add a check in framework/spec/check-builds-live.mjs that replays this journal sequence.

builds.title: Molly gap: axHub allows Molly's origin on /auth/api/* (CORS with credentials) so native screens read the hub session
builds.detail: Found by molly-sign-in-once s1. The orchestrator then sends it to the queue, or he sends it to pending. Yeah, he sends everything to the pending. And I have to send them from pending to queue.

## Addendum (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator doesn't start a headless session right away. If he has slots open, he grabs the next build in the queue and starts the headless session.

## Context found tonight
- The orchestrator (apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator) has NO launch code: nothing in it starts headless sessions. Only deploy/claude-headless.sh enqueues into agent-slots (framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs).
- Pending items are never auto-imported into the orchestrator; 'import' (orchestrator-core.mjs) only copies existing subPrompts, nothing splits.
- HARD RULE in force: no build starts without an orchestrator build ID (launcher enforces it).
- 'Launch builds without asking' (claude-settings) defaults off.
- Profiles were merged into 'all' on Nov 7; queue flagged needsReprocess.

## Do
1. Intake: every new pending item is auto-imported into the orchestrator with a build ID.
2. Split: the orchestrator calls Claude to split into <=30 min steps and pick Fable only where needed, Opus otherwise; write steps to the build.
3. Flow: builds sit in Pending until Brett moves them to Queue (no auto-queue).
4. Dispatcher: a loop in the orchestrator reads VPS accounts (deploy/claude-workers.mjs status, claude-login.mjs accounts): which have Fable, max parallel, free slots. When a slot is free it takes the next Queue build and starts a headless session through the existing launcher (claude-headless.sh / agent-slots), Fable steps to a Fable account, rest to Opus.
5. Progress: steps tick in the progress files per existing rules; the live monitor updates the console in real time.
6. Idle alert: AmberX phone notification when nothing is running while the Queue has work.
7. Tests, report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
When the orchestrator splits a build and sends it to Pending, it also creates a plan in Plan Studio: a note describing the job, with a checklist of the steps, and a sub-note inside it holding Brett's prompt verbatim, with the part this build covers highlighted in a colour set in settings. Sessions are never stopped and rerun per step (saves tokens): instead, the last action of every step is to update the progress file. The orchestrator's listener watches the progress files and, on each change, ticks that step off and crosses it out in the Plan Studio checklist.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator writes each headless session's brief itself, with the least information possible: only the current step(s), the files it touches, and the rules it needs. No history, no full spec.

> No! Every building pending should have its own row that opens, that expands to show everything.

What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"No! Every building pending should have its own row that opens, that expands to show everything."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. steps.text: Design the watchdog@1 contract in framework/core/build-watchdog.mjs. A build counts as stuck when it is marked running or queued-running and has no live session: the pid is gone, the tmux session is missing, the heartbeat (lastSeenAt) is older than staleMin, or an exit code is recorded (143 killed, 137 OOM, 1 failed, usage limit). For each case, define the action: reset the running step, release the slot, requeue, retry on the same or another account, or give up after maxRetries and go back to Pending with a banner item. Also define the recovery record shape { at, buildId, phase, step, cause, exit, action, attempt, account, notified }.
steps.why: New cross-app contract that decides builds@1 status transitions

steps.text: Add the JSON schema framework/schemas/build-watchdog.json and register recovery records on builds@1. This adds an optional `recoveries[]` on a build, which normBuild must keep, plus the journal kind `watchdog-recover`. Old records with no recoveries load unchanged, so no migration is needed. Show this in builds-store verify.
steps.why: Schema + store field design on the one builds store

steps.text: Add golden fixtures for the decision table (killed 143, exit 1, stale heartbeat, live session left alone, retry cap reached, usage limit moves to another account) and a check script. Wire the check into CI.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the new contract

steps.text: Have deploy/claude-headless.sh record each run's end: exit code, signal, account and the time it ended. It writes them to the build's run record through builds-live.mjs (and a run-status file under the slot dir), so killed (143) and failed (1) runs leave evidence the watchdog can read.
Add the liveness probe: framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs `alive <build>` checks pid, tmux session and slot heartbeat and returns JSON. Also free slots whose process is gone (orphan slot reaping).

Add watchdog.mjs `scan` (dry run) to the build-orchestrator plugin. It reads the store, finds every running build, probes liveness, applies the build-watchdog.mjs decisions and prints the stuck builds with cause and planned action (--json).

Add watchdog.mjs `run`, which applies the recoveries. It resets the stuck step to pending, releases the slot, sets the build back to queued through pipeline.mjs, appends a recoveries[] entry under the store lock and pushes it live with builds-live.mjs. It does this idempotently, using a per-build lock and a cooldown.

Retry failed sessions. Crashes and kills are retried up to maxRetries (default 3). A usage limit or account error retries on the next worker through deploy/claude-workers.mjs route. When the cap is hit, the build goes to Pending with a note. The retry count lives on the build, not in memory.

Keep every slot filled. After each recovery, and on every watchdog pass, call pipeline.mjs tick while free slots plus Queue work remain. If slots sit idle while the Queue is non-empty, record that as a recovery cause ('idle-slots') and fix it.

Schedule it: add an `axf-watchdog` cron every minute (with flock) to the plugin's install.mjs and remove it in uninstall.mjs. Mount and add the env in the deploy install script. Make the plugin-lifecycle check pass.

Send a phone FYI for every fix. Declare notify type `watchdog.fix` (FYI, low priority) and `watchdog.gave-up` (alert) in notify.json, and send each through axf.notify@1 to the AmberX app with build, cause, action and attempt. Set `notified` on the recovery record and batch several fixes in one pass into one push.

Add the health@1 check 'Build watchdog' in systems-check. It goes red when the last pass is older than 3 minutes or a build gave up. Its auto-fix reinstalls the cron and runs one pass. A gave-up build becomes a banner item with Fix (requeue).

Add Watchdog settings as a section of Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator (level toolbar applies): on/off, interval, stale heartbeat minutes, max retries, retry on another account, FYI per fix or batched. Stored as plugin settings keys that watchdog.mjs reads.

Add a Watchdog panel in Build orchestrator, built from framework controls and tokens only, in a TabGroup tab. It shows last pass, running builds with liveness, recent fixes (cause → action, attempt, notified) and a Run now toolbar (role=toolbar, aria-label). Each build view shows its recoveries list.
Add the REST API: GET watchdog/status, GET watchdog/scan, POST watchdog/run, GET/PUT watchdog/settings, GET builds/<id>/recoveries on the build-orchestrator server routes.

Add the same API on MCP, the CLI and voice: plugin-commands for the routes (watchdog_status/scan/run/settings), CLI `axf watchdog status|scan|run|set`, the voice/console actions `watchdog.run` and `watchdog.status`, and a console_show / console_open deep link target `build-orchestrator/watchdog` (plus `?build=<id>`).

Write unit tests for watchdog.mjs against a temp store (AXF_DATA_DIR): killed 143 is requeued, exit 1 is retried, a stale heartbeat is reset, a live build is untouched, the cap sends the build to Pending, a usage limit goes to the next account, idle slots trigger a tick, one FYI per fix, and a second pass does nothing.

builds.detail:
Every settings interface (console Settings, plugin settings, chrome settings for tab groups/toolbars/banners/nav/menu bar, and future ones - framework default, enforced by a check) gets a 'Quick settings' pane at the very top:

(3) Override notice: when anything here overrides the skin or console defaults, show 'This is overriding the current skin/defaults' and reuse the existing 'N assets are controlled by their own settings' (chrome.edits) line that expands to list every override, each with reset.
- Any picked asset must have a manifest and pass schema conformance before applying.
- Reachable by REST/MCP/CLI/voice/control@1. Tests, help entries, Shipped features.
Works together with the 'all settings interfaces open in a floating dialog' and per-instance settings-window picker builds.

4. Re-submit stuck shots found in /root/axf-builds and /root/axf-review-shots.
5. Remove the duplicate pending item builds-get-console-token-banner-alert (filed without an id).
6. Tests, Shipped features.

builds.title: Decision dialog: UI Review and other approvals pop up on any screen with approve/deny/pick
builds.detail:
Generalise the approval popup into one 'decision dialog' type used for anything that needs Brett, starting with UI Review.
- Whenever an item is submitted to UI Review, Brett gets a notification AND a dialog pops up on whatever console screen he is on (and on the phone overlay toolbar when built), without navigating away.
- The dialog shows the item (title, build, screenshots/options side by side, desktop + phone), with buttons: pick option N / Approve, Reject, Request changes (with a note), Later, and 'Open in UI Review' (only navigates if tapped).
- Same dialog type reused for other decisions: veto countdowns, confirms, model upgrade approvals, merge clashes, keys needed, passes. Each source registers its buttons; one queue so several waiting items stack with a counter.
- Voice/MCP/API: list waiting decisions, answer one by id ('pick option 2', 'approve it').
- Notification settings to choose which decision types pop up.
- Tests, help entry, Shipped features.

Settings dialogs render through the `settings` asset picked for the kind (`axf.chrome.settings.<type>`; the shared default `settings/chrome-<type>` unless the app's copy `settings/chrome-<type>-<app>` is picked; `extends` folds the chain). Every app in `framework/schemas/shared-assets.json` + Expenses carries its six copies (`node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs check` in CI; `backfill` writes missing ones). A strip that must stay hand-drawn (the Terminal tab strip, the workspace pane strip) carries `data-axf-tab-group="<id>"` + `data-fx-ctx-target="tab-group"`; anything else is a finding in `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`, whose ratchet `framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json` only comes down (`--write-baseline` after a real migration). - UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). It opens each plugin's UI and settings when they exist and lists dependencies in detail (what it needs and whether it's met, who provides it, who needs it, clashes). Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.
- One banner on screen — embed@1 (Oct 21 2026, Brett): an app shown inside another app's frame hides the chrome the host shows, its banner by default. Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. A plugin says when in its web library: `embed: { skipWhen: ['embedded' | 'take:<fn>' | 'hidden:<type>'] }` (`embedSkipReason` in `framework/core/engines/embed.ts`); `installLibraries` skips it, `rt.skippedLibraries` keeps why, the terminal gets one line each plus a summary, Settings → Plugins lists them. Page mode (an app's settings page in the host) never skips. Standalone everything loads. Every new plugin that only draws on chrome a host hides, or does a job a host takes, declares it.

Repo copies, cached copies, local settings, a signed-out session or a read older than two check periods are red. Library: `framework/libs/hubstatus` (`hubLive` in `core.ts`).
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).

No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.

"They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. builds.detail:
Root cause: --fx-opacity-glass / opacityGlass only applies where a component's customization has glass:true (framework/core/engines/customize.ts case 'glass'). Settings dialogs and most panels never set it, so the transparency token does nothing there.
Fix: every dialog, settings interface, panel, popover and floating surface uses a token-driven glass background by default (surface mixed with opacityGlass + blur). Add per-surface-type tokens (glass on/off and opacity per surface type: dialog, settings, panel, menu, toolbar, banner) in tokens.style, editable in Token Control and per instance in Quick settings. Rule: everything visual is driven by a token; add a check that fails on hard-coded backgrounds/opacity. Follows skins. Tests, Shipped features.

To make a surface see-through you lower its value. Per surface type tokens in tokens.style, overridable per instance (Quick settings).

I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). Two enabled editors of one kind are shown as an info-level clash in the Plugin Manager, not an error.

Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.

Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. Settings grey the slot out ("Shown by <host>"). No app hosts others today (Patches, the first host, was retired Nov 3 2026). Engines on both ports, fixture `spec/fixtures/embed.json`.
- One Banners settings (Oct 22 2026, Brett): every banner plugin's settings are one interface (Settings → Plugins → Banners and the right-click Banner settings: a tab per banner with its look, behaviour and own settings). A new banner plugin declares `label`, `icon` and `settingsTab` on its banner so its settings join in.
- Plugins a host makes unneeded aren't loaded (Oct 22 2026, Brett): when an app runs inside a host (any app in a host's tab), plugins that would draw something the host already draws, or that the host makes unnecessary, aren't loaded on that page and are logged at launch. A plugin says when in its web library: `embed: { skipWhen: ['embedded' | 'take:<fn>' | 'hidden:<type>'] }` (`embedSkipReason` in `framework/core/engines/embed.ts`); `installLibraries` skips it, `rt.skippedLibraries` keeps why, the terminal gets one line each plus a summary, Settings → Plugins lists them. Page mode (an app's settings page in the host) never skips. Standalone everything loads. Every new plugin that only draws on chrome a host hides, or does a job a host takes, declares it.

- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.

No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.

Every view root and every plugin root is a `<SkinScope>` (framework/react). builds.title: Console Android app: thin WebView wrapper with overlay, replaces AmberX
builds.detail:
New Android app that replaces AmberX: a thin native shell that runs the AXF console web app in a WebView. Not a native rewrite.
- Native only where Android requires it: draw-over-apps floating toolbar/bubble (port from overlay-toolbar-v2), approvals bar, notifications, mic/recorder, open_url, wake, permissions. Everything else is the web console.
- SAFE AREA (Brett's screenshots, Nov 13): AmberX drew its top bar under the status bar, so the clock, camera cutout, call pill, notification icons and signal sat on top of the title/search/menu. The wrapper must handle WindowInsets (status bar, display cutout, navigation bar, IME), pass them into the WebView as CSS env(safe-area-inset-*) with viewport-fit=cover, and the console must pad every top bar, banner, toolbar and bottom nav with them. Nothing is ever drawn under the clock, camera or notification shade. Test on cutout and punch-hole phones, portrait and landscape.
- The floating toolbar expands to the full-screen console with the toolbar top-left, keeps the app in front, and pops up approvals with a link to the approvals page.
- A JS bridge exposes the native features to the console (window.axfNative), with full API parity: REST/MCP/CLI/voice.
- Auto-updates the web content from the live console. The shell rarely needs a rebuild.
- Migrate AmberX's axHub device service (amberx.open_url, recorder) to the new app.
- Tests, help, Shipped features.

SAFE AREA (Brett's screenshots, Nov 13): AmberX drew its top bar under the status bar, so the clock, camera cutout, call pill, notification icons and signal sat on top of the title/search/menu. The wrapper must handle WindowInsets (status bar, display cutout, navigation bar, IME), pass them into the WebView as CSS env(safe-area-inset-*) with viewport-fit=cover, and the console must pad every top bar, banner, toolbar and bottom nav with them. Nothing is ever drawn under the clock, camera or notification shade. Test on cutout and punch-hole phones, portrait and landscape.
The floating toolbar expands to the full-screen console with the toolbar top-left, keeps the app in front, and pops up approvals with a link to the approvals page.
A JS bridge exposes the native features to the console (window.axfNative), with full API parity: REST/MCP/CLI/voice.
Auto-updates the web content from the live console. The shell rarely needs a rebuild.
Migrate AmberX's axHub device service (amberx.open_url, recorder) to the new app.
Tests, help, Shipped features.
make the console an Android app, just a wrapper for the web app, keep it floating on top; AmberX's banner was behind the camera, the clock and the notification panel

builds.title: Orchestrator settings: collapsible Split section with parallel-split option
builds.detail:
Build Orchestrator settings get a collapsible 'Split' section holding every option for how a request is split into steps and builds.
- Gathers all existing split options (one step per line, step size/estimate, model per step, phases, etc.) into this one section.
- New option: Parallel split. The orchestrator splits a request into independent sub-builds that run at the same time in separate slots. Settings: max parallel slots (default 4), an auto/ask/off mode, and a shared contract or interface step that runs first so the parts don't clash, plus an integration step at the end that merges and tests them together.
- Sub-builds are linked to their parent build (grouped in the builds list, parent shows combined progress, lands together or in order).
- Per-build override when filing ('split into N parallel').
- Full API: REST/MCP/CLI/voice/control@1. Tests, help, Shipped features.

- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.

- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.

- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. - One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.

- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.

- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Done means merged and working (done-means-merged@1, Nov 17 2026, Brett: "We asked you to build it. You should do whatever you have to do to build it, period."): never stop on a failure. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). If you truly cannot go on, write a build note saying what broke and what you tried; the server retries on its ladder (retry, fix, fresh session, another model or account) and escalates to the systems check banner and one phone push only when it runs out. Spec: `framework/spec/DONE-MEANS-MERGED.md`; check `node framework/spec/check-done-means-merged.mjs`.

Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account hulu0241 for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step console-app-part-2-native-floating <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note console-app-part-2-native-floating "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- Android kernel is pure Kotlin (no Android imports). Platform specifics go behind kernel seams. Packages are `ai.amberx.axf.*`, Maven coordinates are `ai.amberx.axf:<module>:<version>`.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Screenshots that aren't for approval go to Screenshots, not the review queue (Nov 1 2026, Brett): a session checking a screen (e.g. the Breakroom), live captures, PR before/after and other ad-hoc pictures are saved with `axf shot <file> --name "…" --app <app> --screen <route> --group "…"` (`node framework/cli/shot.mjs`, or `POST /api/plugins/ui-review/shots`), which lands in UI Review → Screenshots and never waits for approve / reject; Brett can still *Send to review* one. Only planned UI goes through `review.mjs submit`.
- Every tab group, toolbar, banner and nav menu is an asset with an asset settings interface (Nov 4 2026, Brett; shared rule of the same name; build `tab-group-assets`): every tab row in the console, Molly, AmberX web and axHub web is the framework `TabGroup` on the `tab-group` asset (per-row pick `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>.asset`, per-row overrides `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>`); right-click / long-press any tab group, toolbar, banner, nav or menu bar → Settings… / Change… / Move (`framework/react/components/ChromeContext.tsx`, dialogs `axf.chrome.settings` + `axf.chrome.pick`). Settings dialogs render through the `settings` asset picked for the kind (`axf.chrome.settings.<type>`; the shared default `settings/chrome-<type>` unless the app's copy `settings/chrome-<type>-<app>` is picked; `extends` folds the chain). Every app in `framework/schemas/shared-assets.json` + Expenses carries its six copies (`node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs check` in CI; `backfill` writes missing ones). A strip that must stay hand-drawn (the Terminal tab strip, the workspace pane strip) carries `data-axf-tab-group="<id>"` + `data-fx-ctx-target="tab-group"`; anything else is a finding in `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`, whose ratchet `framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json` only comes down (`--write-baseline` after a real migration). Report: `_claude/builds/reports/tab-group-assets.md`.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- All Android work is on hold (Oct 21 2026, Brett): no new Android code anywhere — no Kotlin/Compose features, kernel twins, Android modules or Android app changes (console app, AXHub included). Exceptions: AmberX (`apps/amberx-droid`, its Capacitor shell; Brett, Oct 25 2026); Voice Vault (`apps/voicevault`) may be worked on again (Brett, Oct 21 2026), Voice Vault's own app code only — framework Android code stays on hold. Builds are web/TS/Python only; a cross-port contract gets its Android twin recorded as a deferred gap in `framework/spec/PORTING.md` instead of written. Code already written and merged keeps compiling (CI still builds it, and a build break caused by a web change may be fixed). Brett finishes the Android side himself later.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.
- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A new asset that more than one app could use goes in `framework/assets`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Every banner launches expanded (activity, build manager, codebase changes, approvals, systems check, keys, What's new). Activity still only appears while something runs or just finished.
- Done means merged and working (done-means-merged@1, Nov 17 2026, Brett: "We asked you to build it. You should do whatever you have to do to build it, period."): never stop on a failure. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). builds.title: Console app: wake-word voice listener, voice approvals, every console command by voice
builds.detail:
Voice control for the console Android app (wrapper, parts 1-4), working offline where possible.
- Always-on wake-word listener, with a wake phrase Brett sets in Settings (several allowed). Runs on-device (offline engine, e.g. Vosk/whisper.cpp + a local intent matcher), with a mic-on indicator and an off switch.
- After the wake phrase the app answers out loud ('What's up?') and listens for a command.
- Voice approvals: 'approve' reads pending approvals one at a time (who asked, what it does); Brett says approve, deny, skip or details. 'Approve all pending' and 'deny all' ask for one spoken confirm. Works from the floating overlay and the lock screen.
- Settings by voice, e.g. 'change the veto timer to two hours' (the axHub veto countdown, so he has that long to veto something before it runs/builds), with the value read back.
- Command catalog: every console action, plugin command, control@1 target and pipeline gets a voice entry, built from the API registry so new plugins appear automatically. Multi-field actions run as a spoken wizard that asks for each missing field ('create a new project' -> 'name?' -> 'Gizmo Johnson' -> confirm). Covers projects, builds/pipelines (file, split, prioritise, land, stop), approvals, settings, tokens/skins, notes/tasks, navigation.
- A Voice commands screen lists every command and its phrasings, searchable, with custom phrases Brett adds.
- Destructive commands always need a spoken confirm.
- Full API parity. Tests, help, Shipped features.

Build Orchestrator board gets user-made groups.
- Brett creates, renames, reorders, colours and deletes custom groups/tabs (e.g. 'Console app', 'UI', 'Urgent').

builds.title: Skin from axHub: Override switch, greyed-out editors with notes
builds.detail:
Follow-up to console-skin-axhub-only (the 'Get my skin only from axHub' switch in Settings > Appearance).
- Under that switch add an 'Override' switch, off by default. The two are mutually exclusive: turning Override on turns 'Inherit from axHub only' off right away, and turning axHub-only back on turns Override off.
- While axHub-only is on and Override is off, nothing about the skin or its assets can be edited anywhere: every screen, panel, inline editor, UI Manager row and property/token field that would change the skin or an asset is greyed out (disabled, not hidden).
- Each greyed-out area shows a note: 'This is locked: your skin and assets come from axHub. You can still edit it, but if you do it will no longer refresh or inherit any of its data from axHub.' with a 'Click here to override' link.
- Clicking the link (or the Override switch) asks for one confirm, then turns Override on (axHub-only off) and unlocks editing. Edited assets are marked as overridden.
- Full API: REST/MCP/CLI/voice/control@1. Tests, help, Shipped features.

notes.text: Queued by console.

Brett: reuse the existing overridden-settings dialog (the 'N assets controlled by own settings' notice/dialog), don't build a new one. Next to the Override switch, show a hook/link with the count, e.g. '3 tokens overridden', that opens that dialog listing every overridden token and asset, with reset to axHub per item and reset all.

Brett CHANGED this (overrides the detail): the two switches are NOT mutually exclusive. Both 'Inherit from axHub only' and 'Override' can be on together. With both on, the skin keeps inheriting and refreshing from axHub EXCEPT the tokens Brett has edited: only those overridden tokens stop inheriting, and each is marked 'overridden' with 'reset to axHub'. With axHub-only on and Override off, editors are greyed out with the note and a 'click here to override' link that turns Override on.

I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. - AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.

New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).

No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.

A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. - UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.

Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). Two enabled editors of one kind are shown as an info-level clash in the Plugin Manager, not an error.
- Plugin Manager (Oct 18 2026; Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026): the console's plugin manager is the `plugin-manager` plugin; its model is the cross-port `plugin-inventory@1` engine (`framework/core/engines/plugins.ts` = Kotlin `PluginInventoryEngine` = the plugin's `server/engine.py`, one fixture). Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.

A new banner plugin declares `label`, `icon` and `settingsTab` on its banner so its settings join in.

1. Icon map: a registry of EVERY icon, badge and logo slot in the whole app (every plugin, screen, dialog, menu, toolbar, tab, nav item, banner, widget and button that shows an icon). Each slot gets a stable id, its location and a role (e.g. 'save', 'approve', 'build-running'), and registers through the framework manifest so new plugins appear automatically. Add a CI check that fails on hard-coded icons not in the map.
2. Icon map screen: a searchable, filterable, categorized tree of every slot with a live preview, where you click a slot to change its icon. Ties into the UI Manager.
3. Icon pack template: one pack file maps every role to an icon. Applying a pack changes every icon in the app in one click. Per-slot overrides with Restore previous edit / Restore from axHub.
4. Packs: ship a lot of packs (outline, filled, rounded, duotone, sharp, glyph, emoji-style, plus badge styles and app/plugin logos). Some are themable (follow skin tokens for colour and stroke), others are fixed-colour. Each pack declares whether it's themable. Licences must allow redistribution; prefer open icon sets.
5. Packs are assets: swappable, per-skin defaults, shareable via the hub asset library, importable.
6. Full API: REST/MCP/CLI/voice ('switch to the duotone icon pack'). Tests, help, Shipped features. Use Fable for the registry/schema and asset type.
