builds.title: Own token sets for grids and tab groups
builds.detail:
Today grids only have layout tokens (--fx-grid-areas/cols/rows and the -m mobile variants), and tab groups only have --fx-tab-py/--fx-tab-px padding and --fx-tabs-per-row. Both borrow the general colour tokens (--fx-surface, --fx-border, accent), so hover, selected and active states can't be styled on their own. Add dedicated token families in tokens.style, following skins and editable in Token Control, the UI Manager and per instance.
GRID: header background/text/border/sort arrow/filter chip; row, alternate row, hover, selected, focused, expanded, disabled; grid lines, outer border, cell padding, row height, radius; group header, sticky column shadow, empty state; transparency (default 100%).
TAB GROUP: bar background and border; tab text, background and border for idle, hover, active/selected, pressed, disabled and focus ring; active indicator (underline/pill) colour and thickness; badge on tab; fold/overflow button; gap; radius per style (underline, pills, boxed, segmented, plain, chips); transparency (default 100%).
Wire every grid/table and tab group to read them, and add a CI check against hard-coded colours. Per-instance overrides with Restore previous edit / Restore from axHub. Full API. Tests, help, Shipped features. Fable for the token schema.

notes.text: Queued by console.

Brett: it's not just colours. The style variants (tab styles underline/pills/boxed/segmented/plain/chips, grid styles, and every other component's variants) are hard-coded CSS rules with no tokens of their own. Scope is now EVERY component, not just grids and tab groups. Approach, which is additive with no engine or skin rebuild: (1) audit every component and variant in framework/ui/axf.css and the components engine, and list each hard-coded value (radius, border width/style, shadow, padding, gap, font weight/size, indicator thickness, opacity, colours, transitions); (2) give each component its own token family (--fx-<component>-*), and each style variant its own overrides, whose DEFAULT value points at today's general token (e.g. --fx-tab-radius: var(--fx-radius-sm)), so every existing skin looks identical with zero changes; (3) skins and per-instance settings can then override any of them; (4) a CI check that fails on any literal value in component CSS that isn't a token. Show the new tokens in Token Control, the UI Manager and per-instance settings. Fable for the token schema.

Brett: existing skins do not conform to the new component token set. Add a skin migration as the final phase: (1) bump the skin schema version with the new component token families as optional keys, so old skins still validate and fall back to the general tokens; (2) a skin upgrader (CLI + API + a button in the Skins screen) that walks every skin (built-in, professional skins, hub library, user-made) and writes explicit values for every new component token, derived from that skin's own palette and style so it looks deliberate, not just defaulted; (3) run it on every shipped skin in this build and commit the upgraded skins; (4) a CI check that every shipped skin is on the latest schema and covers every component token; (5) the skin builder/AI skin maker must output the full new token set from now on. Show a 'needs upgrade' badge on any skin not on the latest schema.

Brett: scope is ALL FOUR areas for EVERY element: (1) LAYOUTS: placement, size, gaps, columns/rows, alignment, wrap, density, breakpoints; (2) STYLES: radius, borders, shadows, padding, variants, indicators, typography; (3) COLOUR THEMES: every state (idle, hover, active, selected, pressed, focus, disabled, error) light and dark; (4) BEHAVIOUR: transitions/animation timing and easing, hover/press effects, open/close, collapse, scroll, sticky, motion intensity, and reduced-motion. Every one is a token or asset value. Additive defaults point at today's general tokens, so nothing breaks. Split into parallel sub-builds, one per area (layout, style, colour, behaviour), after a shared Fable schema step, then an integration step and the skin upgrader. The CI gate fails on any literal value in any of the four areas. Treat as top priority.

Brett is worried this breaks things. Safety gate: before any change, capture baseline screenshots of every console screen, plugin, dialog, menu, toolbar and tab group (desktop and phone, light and dark, for each shipped skin). After each sub-build, re-capture and pixel-diff. Any difference fails the step and blocks landing until it's fixed (the token defaults must reproduce today's exact look). The engine change is limited to token resolution, and every engine step runs the full test suite. Land the sub-builds one at a time, each behind its own green visual diff.

Brett: EXHAUSTIVE. Every element gets every possible token: every visual or behavioural property that could ever vary is a token, not just the ones in use today. For style, behaviour, colours, layout, typography, spacing, borders, shadows, effects (blur, glass, gradients, opacity), icons, cursor, motion, sound/haptics where relevant, and every state (idle, hover, focus, active, pressed, selected, disabled, loading, error, empty, dragging) in light and dark. Generate the token families from one schema per element type, so a full set is guaranteed and gaps are caught by CI. Defaults still point at today's values, so nothing looks different.

Brett: the full token set will be overwhelming, so add experience-level views wherever skins/tokens/settings are edited (Token Control, the skin builder/config panel, the UI Manager, per-instance settings, Quick settings, the overrides dialog). BASIC: a handful of friendly controls per element (main colour, accent, roundness, density, transparency, animation on/off), each driving many tokens behind the scenes. PRO: grouped by area (colour, style, layout, behaviour) with the common tokens per state. ADVANCED: every single token, raw, searchable and filterable. Every token in the schema carries a 'level' (basic/pro/advanced) and a plain-English description. There is a global level picker plus a per-screen override, remembered per user; a change made in a higher level shows as 'customised' in lower levels. Full API and voice ('switch to advanced view').

builds.title: Token registry and Skin Editor: live sandbox preview, snapshot history
builds.detail:
Runs after the token schema step of own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups (builds on its schema).
1. TOKEN REGISTRY: one registry listing every token in the system, with element type, area (layout/style/colour/behaviour), state, light/dark, level (basic/pro/advanced), plain-English description, default and source. Every new UI, component or plugin MUST register its tokens through its manifest. A CI check fails any UI whose tokens aren't in the registry, and any registered token that nothing uses. Browsable and searchable, with full API.
2. SKIN EDITOR (plugin and screen): pick any UI from the list (a screen, plugin, dialog, element), or pick it on screen, and it's loaded into a sandbox live-preview window with real components and sample data. Every edit hot-renders the preview in real time. The token list comes from the registry, with Basic/Pro/Advanced views. Inline element and asset editors work inside it.
3. DEFAULT SKIN: there is always a built-in default skin that is locked.
4. SNAPSHOTS: every edit to a skin automatically takes a snapshot (like a disk snapshot). A timeline shows the chain of edits, each with time, who/what made it, and a diff of exactly which tokens changed (old -> new). Click any snapshot to preview it, compare any two, or revert to it (a revert is itself a new snapshot, so nothing is ever lost). No breaking skins into separate style or colour groups: the skin is the only unit.
5. EXPORT: at any point, 'Export current to new skin' saves the current state as a brand-new skin (name, thumbnail, to the hub library).
6. Restore previous edit / Restore from axHub work through the snapshots.
7. Full API: REST/MCP/CLI/voice ('revert the skin to 10 minutes ago', 'export this as a new skin called Midnight'). Tests, help, Shipped features. Fable for the registry and snapshot schema.

builds.title: Dispatcher gate: never launch a build that already has a live session
builds.detail: Bug seen three times on Nov 13 (ui-manager-floating-window-to-select-any: Earl/Gina, Gina/Paulie, Lenny/Paulie): the orchestrator's dispatcher launched the same build phase twice on the same worktree, so two headless sessions wrote the same files at once. Also 'Self-check: marked running with no session' releases builds back to the Queue while a session is still alive. Fix: (1) a dispatch gate that refuses a launch while ANY live tmux/claude session exists for that build id or worktree (check tmux axf-<build>--*, claude -p pids and a lock file in the worktree); (2) the self-check must confirm a session is really dead (pid + tmux) before releasing; (3) a per-build lock file with heartbeat, where stale locks expire; (4) tests that simulate double dispatch. This must land BEFORE parallel split (orchestrator-settings-collapsible-split) goes live, since parallel sub-builds must each get their own worktree and branch and never share one.

builds.detail:
New removable console plugin 'Context menu'.
- Adds one entry, 'Context menu', at the very bottom of EVERY context menu in the app.

builds.title: Auto-land: every finished build lands itself immediately
builds.detail:
Brett is sick of finished builds sitting unlanded until they're thousands of commits behind. Make auto-land the DEFAULT for every build (the per-build switch stays, default ON):
- The moment a build finishes and its tests pass, the server lands it on main (build_land logic: push, merge origin/main, union-merge THREADS/STATUS/decisions, settle orchestrator JSON, check JSON, push).
- Lands go through ONE serial landing queue, so two lands never race (fixes 'cannot lock ref origin/main').
- On a code clash or failing test, the server automatically queues a P0 'merge main and land' fix build for it and keeps retrying until it lands. Brett gets an FYI notification for each attempt, not a question.
- A build that's still running gets main merged into its branch every 30 minutes, so it never falls far behind.
- A sweeper runs every 10 minutes: any finished-but-unlanded build is landed or gets its fix build.
- A banner/badge shows the landing queue and anything stuck for over 30 minutes.
- Full API and voice. Tests, help, Shipped features.

Repo copies, cached copies, local settings, a signed-out session or a read older than two check periods are red. Library: `framework/libs/hubstatus` (`hubLive` in `core.ts`).
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.
- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.

A skin MAY name an icon pack (`iconPack`). Scopes follow the icon-map model: hub-wide (`skin` on the shared appearance document) → app (`skin.use`, `skin.inherit` = follow the hub) → screen (`scopes["ui:<view>"]`) → plugin (`scopes["plugin:<id>"]`), the child overrides the parent (`resolveLookSkin`); apps stay their own by default. Every view root and every plugin root is a `<SkinScope>` (framework/react). Parity: Settings → Appearance (Where / What a skin covers), `node framework/cli/skins.mjs use|off|inherit|follow|global|at|coverage|covers`, the theme-manager routes (MCP by plugin-commands), actions `skin.inherit`, `skin.scope`. Report: `_claude/builds/reports/skins-asset-types.md`.

Hero video (the main selling point): 'Talk an Android app into existence on your way to work.' Story: someone needs a time-tracking app for work, speaks it into AmberX on their phone during the commute, and it's ready when they arrive. Reuse the existing Expenses app if it helps. Label any staged parts as a preview. Also cut a 60-second version.

Third hero video, 'the boss texts': a guy gets a text from his boss: 'We're having an event, I need a public image gallery up right now for all the employees to share their pictures.' He's lying in bed, opens AmberX on his phone and says 'Amber, build me a gallery with user accounts and GPS tagging.' He taps approve on a couple of approval pop-ups, then says 'All right, I'm going to sleep now, get that done, I need it in the morning,' and falls asleep. Then the cat-named agents keep going in the group chat overnight, talking back and forth and joking around ('this guy's asleep and we're up all night working', 'here you go, finish that'), handing work off while they build it. Time-lapse night to morning. He wakes up, yawns, rolls over, and boom: the app is ready. Finished app: login gate with user accounts, employees uploading geotagged photos, a map of where each photo was taken, and a public gallery. Location sharing is opt-in with a clear consent prompt. Keep the banter funny but mostly clean so it works on every platform (an uncut version is fine as an extra). Use real AXF libraries where they exist; label staged parts as a preview. Also cut a 60-second version.

Fourth hero video: someone needs to whip up an internal, private messaging server for their team fast. They describe it by voice in AmberX ('a private chat server for my company, with logins, channels, direct messages and file sharing, only our people can get in'). Show the cat-named agents building it in the group chat, approval pop-ups, AmberX assembling pre-built AXF libraries, deploying on their own VPS so the data stays in-house, then team members logging in and chatting on desktop and the Android app. Label staged parts as a preview. Also cut a 60-second version.

Fifth hero video, 'an app whenever you need one': told over days and weeks, not one sitting. A teen builds an app the moment he needs it: one day a chat with his buddy; the next, a friends-only picture board with a message board; later, a baseball practice schedule with alarms and notifications, built in a rush on his way out the door ('oh, I need this', boom, done in minutes). Every new app plugs straight into his other apps and his data sets on axHub immediately, with no waiting. # Build: group-chat-audio-hear-agents-talk-while

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Build "Group chat audio: hear the agents talk while they build" (group-chat-audio-hear-agents-talk-while) is complete.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account hulu0241 for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step group-chat-audio-hear-agents-talk-while <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note group-chat-audio-hear-agents-talk-while "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- Android kernel is pure Kotlin (no Android imports). Platform specifics go behind kernel seams. Packages are `ai.amberx.axf.*`, Maven coordinates are `ai.amberx.axf:<module>:<version>`.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Screenshots that aren't for approval go to Screenshots, not the review queue (Nov 1 2026, Brett): a session checking a screen (e.g. the Breakroom), live captures, PR before/after and other ad-hoc pictures are saved with `axf shot <file> --name "…" --app <app> --screen <route> --group "…"` (`node framework/cli/shot.mjs`, or `POST /api/plugins/ui-review/shots`), which lands in UI Review → Screenshots and never waits for approve / reject; Brett can still *Send to review* one. Only planned UI goes through `review.mjs submit`.
- Every tab group, toolbar, banner and nav menu is an asset with an asset settings interface (Nov 4 2026, Brett; shared rule of the same name; build `tab-group-assets`): every tab row in the console, Molly, AmberX web and axHub web is the framework `TabGroup` on the `tab-group` asset (per-row pick `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>.asset`, per-row overrides `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>`); right-click / long-press any tab group, toolbar, banner, nav or menu bar → Settings… / Change… / Move (`framework/react/components/ChromeContext.tsx`, dialogs `axf.chrome.settings` + `axf.chrome.pick`). Settings dialogs render through the `settings` asset picked for the kind (`axf.chrome.settings.<type>`; the shared default `settings/chrome-<type>` unless the app's copy `settings/chrome-<type>-<app>` is picked; `extends` folds the chain). Every app in `framework/schemas/shared-assets.json` + Expenses carries its six copies (`node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs check` in CI; `backfill` writes missing ones). A strip that must stay hand-drawn (the Terminal tab strip, the workspace pane strip) carries `data-axf-tab-group="<id>"` + `data-fx-ctx-target="tab-group"`; anything else is a finding in `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`, whose ratchet `framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json` only comes down (`--write-baseline` after a real migration). Report: `_claude/builds/reports/tab-group-assets.md`.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.

I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.

The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- All Android work is on hold (Oct 21 2026, Brett): no new Android code anywhere — no Kotlin/Compose features, kernel twins, Android modules or Android app changes (console app, AXHub included). Exceptions: AmberX (`apps/amberx-droid`, its Capacitor shell; Brett, Oct 25 2026); Voice Vault (`apps/voicevault`) may be worked on again (Brett, Oct 21 2026), Voice Vault's own app code only — framework Android code stays on hold. Builds are web/TS/Python only; a cross-port contract gets its Android twin recorded as a deferred gap in `framework/spec/PORTING.md` instead of written. Code already written and merged keeps compiling (CI still builds it, and a build break caused by a web change may be fixed). Brett finishes the Android side himself later.

builds.detail: Move the entire build orchestrator (queue, pending, splitter, dispatcher/pipeline tick, reconciler, slots, accounts, builds store, notes, steps, landing) out of the console plugin and into axHub (MossesX/axHub), running on the VPS, so builds are managed whether the console is up or not. Staged so nothing breaks mid-flight: (1) Run AFTER auto-lander-controls-in-the-gate-plugin lands (gate + merge queue already in axHub). (2) Stand up the axHub orchestrator service reading the SAME builds store (_claude/builds/*), in shadow mode: it computes what it would launch/land but doesn't act; compare with the console for a while. (3) Cut over: axHub owns the dispatcher, reconciler, splitter and lander; the console's cron/plugin stops acting. (4) Build the full orchestrator UI as axHub screens (all tabs: Pending, Queue, Active, Built, Complete, Errors, Archive, settings, slots, accounts) with every action. (5) axHub tools (orchestrator.*) for Claude, MCP and voice: file a build, note, status, step, approve, land, etc.; today's axf-console.build_orchestrator_pipeline_request and planner.builds callers get equivalent axHub tools. (6) Console keeps only a read-only mirror or a link to the axHub page, then the console plugin is retired. Fix on the way: phase-end builds must never get parked in Pending (reconciler bug), dispatcher alerts link format. No build or data lost; all history migrated. Tests, help, Shipped features.

Private only: no public port, no DNS entry; reachable only on the internal Docker network. axHub is the UI and the door: its screens and its tools (orchestrator.*, gate.*, vps.*) talk to the container internally, behind axHub's existing login and domain. The container needs controlled host access to launch/watch builds (tmux sessions, /root/axf-builds worktrees, git, claude CLI, the builds store): use a narrow host bridge (mounted paths + a small host-side runner/agent), not a wide-open docker socket; document exactly what it can touch. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Plugins: each plugin gets a Plugin Manager entry (info, enable/disable, logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). Two enabled editors of one kind are shown as an info-level clash in the Plugin Manager, not an error.
- Plugin Manager (Oct 18 2026; Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026): the console's plugin manager is the `plugin-manager` plugin; its model is the cross-port `plugin-inventory@1` engine (`framework/core/engines/plugins.ts` = Kotlin `PluginInventoryEngine` = the plugin's `server/engine.py`, one fixture). It opens each plugin's UI and settings when they exist and lists dependencies in detail (what it needs and whether it's met, who provides it, who needs it, clashes). Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.
- One banner on screen — embed@1 (Oct 21 2026, Brett): an app shown inside another app's frame hides the chrome the host shows, its banner by default. Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. Settings grey the slot out ("Shown by <host>"). No app hosts others today (Patches, the first host, was retired Nov 3 2026). Engines on both ports, fixture `spec/fixtures/embed.json`.
- One Banners settings (Oct 22 2026, Brett): every banner plugin's settings are one interface (Settings → Plugins → Banners and the right-click Banner settings: a tab per banner with its look, behaviour and own settings). A new banner plugin declares `label`, `icon` and `settingsTab` on its banner so its settings join in.
- Plugins a host makes unneeded aren't loaded (Oct 22 2026, Brett): when an app runs inside a host (any app in a host's tab), plugins that would draw something the host already draws, or that the host makes unnecessary, aren't loaded on that page and are logged at launch. A plugin says when in its web library: `embed: { skipWhen: ['embedded' | 'take:<fn>' | 'hidden:<type>'] }` (`embedSkipReason` in `framework/core/engines/embed.ts`); `installLibraries` skips it, `rt.skippedLibraries` keeps why, the terminal gets one line each plus a summary, Settings → Plugins lists them. Page mode (an app's settings page in the host) never skips. Standalone everything loads. Every new plugin that only draws on chrome a host hides, or does a job a host takes, declares it.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.

- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Plugins: each plugin gets a Plugin Manager entry (info, enable/disable, logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). Two enabled editors of one kind are shown as an info-level clash in the Plugin Manager, not an error.
- Plugin Manager (Oct 18 2026; Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026): the console's plugin manager is the `plugin-manager` plugin; its model is the cross-port `plugin-inventory@1` engine (`framework/core/engines/plugins.ts` = Kotlin `PluginInventoryEngine` = the plugin's `server/engine.py`, one fixture). It opens each plugin's UI and settings when they exist and lists dependencies in detail (what it needs and whether it's met, who provides it, who needs it, clashes). Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.
- One banner on screen — embed@1 (Oct 21 2026, Brett): an app shown inside another app's frame hides the chrome the host shows, its banner by default. Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. Settings grey the slot out ("Shown by <host>"). No app hosts others today (Patches, the first host, was retired Nov 3 2026). Engines on both ports, fixture `spec/fixtures/embed.json`.
- One Banners settings (Oct 22 2026, Brett): every banner plugin's settings are one interface (Settings → Plugins → Banners and the right-click Banner settings: a tab per banner with its look, behaviour and own settings). A new banner plugin declares `label`, `icon` and `settingsTab` on its banner so its settings join in.
- Plugins a host makes unneeded aren't loaded (Oct 22 2026, Brett): when an app runs inside a host (any app in a host's tab), plugins that would draw something the host already draws, or that the host makes unnecessary, aren't loaded on that page and are logged at launch. A plugin says when in its web library: `embed: { skipWhen: ['embedded' | 'take:<fn>' | 'hidden:<type>'] }` (`embedSkipReason` in `framework/core/engines/embed.ts`); `installLibraries` skips it, `rt.skippedLibraries` keeps why, the terminal gets one line each plus a summary, Settings → Plugins lists them. Page mode (an app's settings page in the host) never skips. Standalone everything loads. Every new plugin that only draws on chrome a host hides, or does a job a host takes, declares it.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.

steps.text: Design the veto-countdown setting and read-only contract: setting key (seconds, 0-120, default 10, clamp/validate), where it is stored with the other approval settings, the readOnly flag on a call and the read-only allow-list format for vps.run (command classifier input/output, what counts as a write: pipes to files, redirection, chained commands, sudo, git push/commit, docker run/rm). Write it as a short spec doc in the axHub repo docs folder and the setting schema entry.
steps.why: Schema + contract design for a hub-wide policy setting and the call classification every caller relies on

steps.text: Find where axHub holds veto calls and the hard-coded 90 s countdown (decision #104); replace the constant with a read of the new setting (clamped 0-120, default 10). 0 s = run at once but still log the notice. Commit.

Migration: existing hubs with no stored value get the default 10 s; keep any saved value. Add unit tests for default, clamp (-5 -> 0, 500 -> 120), 0 s runs at once, and the countdown shown on the notice/page matches the setting.
Approvals settings UI: add a 'Veto countdown (seconds)' slider/number field (0-120, default 10) in the axHub approvals settings, using the framework controls and tokens only. Commit.

API for the countdown setting: REST GET/PUT on the approvals settings (owner session only, validated), MCP tool (axhub.settings get/set for veto countdown), CLI command, and a voice/AmberX action name; deep link that opens the approvals settings with the field highlighted. Tests for each path agreeing.

Read-only classifier for vps.run: allow-list module (inspect, logs, ps, git log/status/fetch/diff/show, cat, head, tail, ls, grep, rg, df, du, free, uptime, docker ps/inspect/logs, systemctl status, journalctl) that rejects writes: output redirection (> >>), tee, chained commands where any part is not read-only, command substitution, sudo, rm/mv/cp/chmod, git push/commit/reset/checkout, docker run/rm/exec/restart. Commit.
Classifier tests: table of read-only commands that pass and lookalikes that must be held (cat x > y, git fetch && git reset, ls; rm, $(…), docker logs | tee f, git log --output=f). Commit.

Wire it into the hold path: a call with an explicit readOnly flag or a vps.run whose command the classifier passes skips the veto countdown and runs at once (still logged with 'read-only, not held'); tools whose policy is read-only by definition skip it too. A readOnly flag on a command the classifier rejects is ignored and the call is held. Anything changing keeps the countdown; confirm/irreversible tools keep their approval regardless. Commit.

Integration tests: read-only vps.run runs immediately, mutating vps.run is held for the setting's countdown, readOnly flag on a write is still held, confirm-policy tool still needs approval at 0 s, destructive tools never skip. Commit.

Surface it: approvals log/page shows 'read-only, ran at once' for skipped calls; API exposes the read-only allow list (REST GET + MCP read) so callers can check a command first. Update the MCP server instructions text (90 seconds -> the setting) and the veto docs. Commit.

Help entries for the countdown setting and the read-only rule, Shipped features entry, and a decision record in axHub's decisions (replacing the fixed 90 s of #104, with Brett's verbatim words). Commit.

Run the full axHub test suite (pnpm test), fix failures, write report _claude/builds/reports/axhub-veto-countdown-setting-read-only.md (what changed, before/after: 90 s fixed -> 10 s setting; read-only calls run at once; how each part is reached via REST/MCP/CLI/voice/deep link), add the THREADS row, push the branch and open the PR on MossesX/axHub stating the API paths.

- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.

Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.

- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.

New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.

New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).

Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.

- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Screenshots that aren't for approval go to Screenshots, not the review queue (Nov 1 2026, Brett): a session checking a screen (e.g. the Breakroom), live captures, PR before/after and other ad-hoc pictures are saved with `axf shot <file> --name "…" --app <app> --screen <route> --group "…"` (`node framework/cli/shot.mjs`, or `POST /api/plugins/ui-review/shots`), which lands in UI Review → Screenshots and never waits for approve / reject; Brett can still *Send to review* one. Only planned UI goes through `review.mjs submit`.
- Every tab group, toolbar, banner and nav menu is an asset with an asset settings interface (Nov 4 2026, Brett; shared rule of the same name; build `tab-group-assets`): every tab row in the console, Molly, AmberX web and axHub web is the framework `TabGroup` on the `tab-group` asset (per-row pick `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>.asset`, per-row overrides `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>`); right-click / long-press any tab group, toolbar, banner, nav or menu bar → Settings… / Change… / Move (`framework/react/components/ChromeContext.tsx`, dialogs `axf.chrome.settings` + `axf.chrome.pick`). Settings dialogs render through the `settings` asset picked for the kind (`axf.chrome.settings.<type>`; the shared default `settings/chrome-<type>` unless the app's copy `settings/chrome-<type>-<app>` is picked; `extends` folds the chain). Every app in `framework/schemas/shared-assets.json` + Expenses carries its six copies (`node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs check` in CI; `backfill` writes missing ones). A strip that must stay hand-drawn (the Terminal tab strip, the workspace pane strip) carries `data-axf-tab-group="<id>"` + `data-fx-ctx-target="tab-group"`; anything else is a finding in `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`, whose ratchet `framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json` only comes down (`--write-baseline` after a real migration). Report: `_claude/builds/reports/tab-group-assets.md`.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Plugins: each plugin gets a Plugin Manager entry (info, enable/disable, logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). Two enabled editors of one kind are shown as an info-level clash in the Plugin Manager, not an error.
- Plugin Manager (Oct 18 2026; Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026): the console's plugin manager is the `plugin-manager` plugin; its model is the cross-port `plugin-inventory@1` engine (`framework/core/engines/plugins.ts` = Kotlin `PluginInventoryEngine` = the plugin's `server/engine.py`, one fixture). It opens each plugin's UI and settings when they exist and lists dependencies in detail (what it needs and whether it's met, who provides it, who needs it, clashes). Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.
- Every rebuild ends with a differences report (Oct 20 2026): after any rebuild (Fable rebuilds and every future one, any model), write `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/<pending-id>.md` comparing the new build with the version it replaced: what was removed, kept, changed and added; contract/API/asset/fixture changes; migrations and compatibility notes for apps already using it; tests before vs after; known gaps. Then show Brett the differences and improvements in chat (phone-readable summary, link to the report).
- One banner on screen — embed@1 (Oct 21 2026, Brett): an app shown inside another app's frame hides the chrome the host shows, its banner by default. Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. Settings grey the slot out ("Shown by <host>"). No app hosts others today (Patches, the first host, was retired Nov 3 2026). Engines on both ports, fixture `spec/fixtures/embed.json`.
- One Banners settings (Oct 22 2026, Brett): every banner plugin's settings are one interface (Settings → Plugins → Banners and the right-click Banner settings: a tab per banner with its look, behaviour and own settings). A new banner plugin declares `label`, `icon` and `settingsTab` on its banner so its settings join in.
- Plugins a host makes unneeded aren't loaded (Oct 22 2026, Brett): when an app runs inside a host (any app in a host's tab), plugins that would draw something the host already draws, or that the host makes unnecessary, aren't loaded on that page and are logged at launch. A plugin says when in its web library: `embed: { skipWhen: ['embedded' | 'take:<fn>' | 'hidden:<type>'] }` (`embedSkipReason` in `framework/core/engines/embed.ts`); `installLibraries` skips it, `rt.skippedLibraries` keeps why, the terminal gets one line each plus a summary, Settings → Plugins lists them. Page mode (an app's settings page in the host) never skips. Standalone everything loads. Every new plugin that only draws on chrome a host hides, or does a job a host takes, declares it.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.
- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A new asset that more than one app could use goes in `framework/assets`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Every banner launches expanded (activity, build manager, codebase changes, approvals, systems check, keys, What's new). Activity still only appears while something runs or just finished.

steps.text: Read the current todo-manager plugin (plugin.json, server, web UI, data files, commands) and the superseded build to-do-manager-fully-voice-mcp-controlled; write the design notes (current data shape, every entry point, the old build's notes folded in) into the report draft

steps.text: Tree engine part 2: operations create inside, rename, edit, move (cycle-safe: never into itself or a descendant), reorder, duplicate subtree with new ids, complete/uncomplete (cascade rule), delete subtree to a trash with undo token, collapse/expand
steps.why: Engine internals: move and duplicate invariants on an unlimited-depth tree

steps.text: Tree engine part 3: export of any subtree (markdown checklist and JSON), and an op log so every change is journalled and undoable
steps.why: Engine internals: undo/journal contract used by every surface

steps.text: Engine tests: depth 50 nesting, every kind inside every kind, move cycles refused, duplicate, delete + undo, path resolution, export
steps.why: Conformance for the new engine contract

steps.why: Schema migration design for live user data

- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. - Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.
- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step.
