steps.text: Declare the notify type: add apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/notify.json (notify-types@1) with type `pipeline.build-started` (label 'Queue build started', default on, channel AmberX push, not guarded). Check that notify-control's registry picks it up.

Add a setting to turn it off: `pipeline.notifyOnStart` (default on) in the build-orchestrator plugin settings, shown as a switch under Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator, with a lifecycle marker and a control@1 / console-control target.

Write the sender in apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/queue-notify.mjs. It builds the message (build title + id, step/phase, model, Claude account, queue position left) and a deep link to row:<build>. It sends through axf.notify@1 via the console's notify route, using the container token, and does nothing when the setting or the notify type is off. It sends once per build run (keyed on build id + run number).

Hook the sender into the dispatcher: in pipeline.mjs tick, call queue-notify only after claude-headless.sh --account has actually started the run. Never call it on a refused launch (no slot, model gate exit 3, no account). A notify failure only gets a log line and never blocks the launch.

Make the notification also go out when a build starts outside the tick (relaunch after a crash, 'Launch builds without asking' auto-queue). Put the call where those starts happen, reuse the same once-per-run key, and leave a note on the build record.

API for the setting and a test send. REST: GET/POST /api/plugins/build-orchestrator/pipeline/notify (state: on/off, last sent) and POST .../notify/test. CLI: `pipeline.mjs notify status|on|off|test`. MCP: through plugin-commands (static route descriptions). Voice: console action `pipeline.notify` (AmberX). All four do the same thing.

Deep links: tapping the notification opens the console on that build's row (console_show target row:<build>). The setting has its own address (setting:pipeline.notifyOnStart), so check-console-control.mjs passes.

Tests in apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/test/queue-notify.test.mjs. Use a fake notify endpoint to check: it sends on launch, skips a refused launch, does nothing when the setting is off, does nothing when the type is off in notify-control, sends once per run, and the message names the build, model and account.

Docs and checks: update the build-orchestrator README and help (the notification, the setting, the API). Run python apps/console-web/plugins/notify-control/test.py, plugin-lifecycle check build-orchestrator, check-console-control.mjs and glossary catalog --check, and fix any findings.

Final step: run the tests again, write the report _claude/builds/reports/notify-phone-when-queue-starts-building.md (what was added, how each part is reached by REST, MCP, CLI and voice, and a test send to the phone if one is available), add the THREADS row, push the branch and open the PR, link it with builds-live.mjs link, and add it to the merge queue.

builds.title: Live build status: real-time grids, 15-second VPS liveness check, animated running rows, red alert + dialog when a build breaks
builds.detail: 1) Live updates: the console updates in real time whenever a build changes (push over the console's live channel, no refresh), on every grid and tab (Active, Queue, Pending, Incomplete, etc.). 2) The VPS checks every 15 seconds that each running job is really alive (session, pid, heartbeat) and pushes the result to the console. 3) Every running/building row in any grid shows an animated indicator: a spinning/animated icon next to it, and the row itself slowly flashes or pulses. Configurable in settings: animation type (flash, pulse, glow, other), colors, speed, as a hot-swappable asset with tokens only. 4) When a running job stops or breaks: the animation stops, the row turns red/pink, a pop-up alert says it broke, and a dialog shows what happened (cause, exit code, last step, what the watchdog is doing about it), with a link to the build. 5) Full API: deep link, state read, REST, MCP, CLI, voice for the settings and the alert. Coordinate with both watchdogs (#772 recovery, #780 stale-row) instead of duplicating their checks.

# Build: live-build-status-real-time-grids-15

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-17T19:30:44.328Z
> Every time something happens, I want the console to be updated in real time. The VPS checks every 15 seconds to make sure the jobs are running and updates the console. Every running job in any grid has a spinning or animated icon, and building rows flash slowly; configure the animation, flash, pulse, colors. When it stops it goes red, a pink background with a pop-up alert that says broke, and a dialog shows what happened.

## What to build
Continue build "Live build status: real-time grids, 15-second VPS liveness check, animated running rows, red alert + dialog when a build breaks" (live-build-status-real-time-grids-15) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-17 19:30):
"Every time something happens, I want the console to be updated in real time. The VPS checks every 15 seconds to make sure the jobs are running and updates the console. Every running job in any grid has a spinning or animated icon, and building rows flash slowly; configure the animation, flash, pulse, colors. When it stops it goes red, a pink background with a pop-up alert that says broke, and a dialog shows what happened."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (4 left, ~40 min):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Design the build-live@1 event contract: the build change and liveness events pushed over the console live channel (build id, status, step, alive/stale/dead, cause, exit code, last step, what the watchdog is doing, at). - The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Every notification is in the one registry (Nov 6 2026, Brett: "I need to control all the notifications."): every notification goes through the console's alert hub or asks capability `axf.notify@1` before it sends; a plugin that sends one declares it in its own `notify.json` (`notify-types@1`), and the Notifications panel controls it (Plugins → Notifications; `axf notify-control …`, MCP `notify-control_*`). Approvals and veto notices are guarded: only Brett's own click turns them down, never a session or agent. `python apps/console-web/plugins/notify-control/test.py` fails on an alert source no registry names.

- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.

- Every banner launches expanded (activity, build manager, codebase changes, approvals, systems check, keys, What's new). Activity still only appears while something runs or just finished.
- Done means merged and working (done-means-merged@1, Nov 17 2026, Brett: "We asked you to build it. You should do whatever you have to do to build it, period."): never stop on a failure. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). If you truly cannot go on, write a build note saying what broke and what you tried; the server retries on its ladder (retry, fix, fresh session, another model or account) and escalates to the systems check banner and one phone push only when it runs out. steps.text: Add the run-indicator and row-state styles to framework/ui/axf.css: running rows get the keyframe pulse, flash or glow and a spinning icon, broke rows get a red/pink background and stop animating, and prefers-reduced-motion is respected. Tokens only.

Add a framework React piece, <RunIndicator> plus a useRowRunState(buildId) hook, that DataGrid rows use through a row-state prop (data-axf-run=running|stale|broke). Register its control@1 targets at the end of the list.

Server side: publish a build-live@1 event on the console live channel for every builds store write (status, step, note, branch, PR) by hooking the store-change path. The UI then needs no polling and no refresh.

VPS liveness tick: a 15-second loop that checks every running build (session, pid, heartbeat) by reading the #772 recovery and #780 stale-row watchdog state instead of re-checking. Push a liveness event only when the state changes, plus a heartbeat summary.
Run the liveness tick: add a cron or systemd timer entry next to axf-pipeline (15 s, under the agent-slots rules, light) and a health@1 check that goes red when the tick stops.

Web client: a live builds store (framework/react or console src) that subscribes to build-live@1 on the live channel, applies events through the engine and reconnects with a resync on reconnect or focus.
Wire the Active, Queue and Pending grids to the live store: rows update in place and running rows get the row-state and RunIndicator.
Wire Incomplete, Build manager, Pipeline and every other grid that lists builds (search for build-row grids) to the live store and row-state.
Broke alert: when a build goes running → broke, send one alert through the alert hub (declared in the plugin's notify.json) and show a pop-up toast in the console that says it broke.

Broke dialog: a framework Dialog (dialog asset) showing the cause, exit code, last step, what the watchdog is doing (from #772 and #780) and a link to the build. It opens from the toast and from the broke row.

Settings: a Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator → Live status sub-tab, with the level toolbar, for the run-indicator asset pick, the animation type, the colour token picks, speed, alerts on/off and the dialog on/off. Values are saved as per-key settings and asset token overrides.
UI Review: build three run-indicator options (pulse, flash, glow) as real assets in plugins/build-orchestrator/assets/run-indicator/ with a choices JSON for the submit step.
REST API: GET /api/plugins/build-orchestrator/live (state of all running builds, liveness, last tick), GET/PUT live/settings, GET live/broke/<id> (dialog data), POST live/broke/<id>/ack.

MCP + CLI: plugin commands for live-status, live-settings get/set and broke-show/ack (MCP through plugin-commands), plus `axf builds live|live-settings|broke <id>`. Add a console-control address for the settings tab, the broke dialog (dialog:build-broke/<id>) and grid rows so console_show and console_open can deep link them.

Voice: AmberX console actions builds.live.status, builds.live.animation (set type, colour, speed) and builds.broke.show, so they match the REST, MCP and CLI parts, and register them with console-control.

Tests: engine fixture checks, a Python test for the liveness tick (alive → stale → broke, no duplicate alerts, reads the watchdog state), a route test, and a client test that an event updates a row without a refresh.

Run CI checks: check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, check-console-control, check-skin-coverage, glossary catalog --check, tracker --check and plugin-lifecycle check. Re-bake the console src/axf and fix what fails.

Take desktop and phone shots of a running row, a broke row, the dialog and the settings tab, and submit them to UI Review with the 3 choices. Then write the report _claude/builds/reports/live-build-status-real-time-grids-15.md (API reach for each feature, watchdog coordination), add the THREADS row, push the branch and open the PR, saying in it how each feature is reached and that it waits in UI Review.

builds.title: Guided live demo test: watch the orchestrator do everything in real time, with an overlay, focus and Next/Pause
builds.detail: A guided live demo test of the orchestrator that Brett watches in real time, run on throwaway test builds (never real ones). Before it starts, an overlay with Continue and Pause buttons and a 'Pause between steps' switch. The test walks through everything the orchestrator can do, one thing at a time: queue, launch, steps ticking off/crossed out as they finish, running animation, a deliberate crash, the watchdog catching it, retry, red CI, auto-fix, merge-main, landing, a build dying and showing what failed (red row + alert dialog), stale-row cleanup, phone notifications. For each one: bring the console to focus on the exact grid/row/dialog to watch (console_open / focus), show a caption of what is about to happen, run it live, then wait. With pause on, wait until Brett clicks Next, then wait at least 30 seconds before the next one; with pause off, at least 30 seconds between each. A summary at the end of what passed/failed. Deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice to start/pause/next/stop it. Depends on the live build status build (real-time grids, animated rows, break alerts).

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). steps.text: Design the demo-run@1 record and its state machine (idle → overlay → focusing → captioned → running → waiting-next → cooldown → done / stopped), pause flag, min-gap (≥30 s, never lower), per-act result (pass/fail/skipped + evidence), and the demo-act@1 entry shape (id, title, caption, focus target, run, expect, cleanup). steps.why: Engine internals that every driver shares; the fixture is the contract

steps.text: Add the test-build sandbox rule to the builds store: a `demo: true` tag on throwaway builds (id prefix `demo-`). Projections, dispatcher, lander, alerts and builds-live mark them as demo-only, and a guard refuses any demo action on a build without the tag. Add a migration note.

Write the act catalog part 1 as demo-act@1 entries: queue a demo build, launch it, tick steps one at a time (crossed out in the grid), and the running animation. Each entry has a caption, a focus target (row:<build>/step:sN, view:builds/tab:pipeline) and an expect check.

Build the runner on the core: drives acts in order, focuses the console before each act (console_open / focus with highlight), shows the caption, runs the act, records the result, and keeps the waits. Persists demo-run@1 so a console restart picks the run back up.
Add the runner's stop and cleanup path: Stop stops the run at once, removes every demo-* build, branch and alert, and the summary (passed/failed/skipped per act) is written to the run record.
Add the server routes: GET state, POST start {pause}, pause, resume, next, stop, set pause-between-steps, GET summary. Register them with plugin-commands so the MCP tools come from them.
Build the start overlay UI: a framework Dialog with what the demo will do, Continue and Pause buttons, a 'Pause between steps' Switch, and a toolbar (role=toolbar, aria-label). Tokens only.
Build the live caption bar UI: a floating caption above the focused target showing what is about to happen, the act number (n/N), a countdown to the next act, and Next / Pause / Stop on a toolbar.
Build the summary dialog at the end: a DataGrid of acts with pass/fail, evidence links (row, alert, PR) and a Run again button.

Wire the web library: register the overlay, caption bar and summary; console-control targets (view:orchestrator-demo, dialog ids, buttons via data-axf-target); a deep link `?axf-open=orchestrator-demo` and console_show target; and a settings sub-tab under Plugins (min gap shown, can't go below 30 s, default pause).

Add console actions + voice: demo.start, demo.pause, demo.resume, demo.next, demo.stop, demo.state, with AmberX voice phrases ('start the orchestrator demo', 'next', 'pause the demo', 'stop the demo').
Add the CLI: `axf demo orchestrator start [--pause] | pause | resume | next | stop | state | summary`, calling the same REST routes.
Add the dependency check: refuse to start (with a plain reason) when the live build status build's real-time grids and break alerts aren't there; list what's missing in the overlay.
Write unit tests: core vs fixture, ≥30 s gap in both modes, Next then 30 s, the sandbox guard refuses real builds, and stop cleans up everything. Write a Python route test.
Run a dry run end to end with a shortened gap override (test-only env), the fake runner and the dry-run lander; check every act passes and no non-demo build changed (builds-store verify).

Run the CI checks: check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-console-control, check-chrome-assets, plugin-lifecycle check --after-uninstall, the help ratchet and the glossary catalog --check; fix any findings.
Take desktop and phone shots of the overlay, caption bar and summary, with 3 option assets for the overlay (ui-choices@1), and submit to UI Review with --choices.

Finish: run all tests, write the report _claude/builds/reports/guided-live-demo-test-watch-orchestrator.md (acts, how each is reached by deep link / REST / MCP / CLI / voice, results), add the THREADS row, push the branch, open the PR stating the UI Review hold and the API paths, and link it with builds-live.

REST: GET /api/plugins/console-terminal/build-session/<build> (state read) and POST .../build-session/<build>/open (focuses the existing tab in the open console via the console-control channel; 409 with the reason when there is no live session). Register them so plugin-commands exposes them as MCP tools.

Console-control address + deep link: register target 'view:terminal/session:<sessionId>' and alias 'row:<build>/session' so console_show / console_open / Ctrl+K open the terminal focused on that tab; append the new targets at the end of the control@1 registry (append-only).
Terminal front end: handle the focus request: open (or pop open) the terminal panel and select the existing session tab by id, never spawning a new session; show a short toast when the tab is gone.

Context menu item: add 'Open session' to the dynamic section of the build-grid context menus (Build manager, orchestrator, pipeline/queue grids, Live list) as a runtime contribution (rt.addContextItems), enabled only for builds with a live session, disabled with the reason as its hint otherwise; it calls the open route.

Live state for the menu item: cache build→session liveness per grid (one batched GET for visible running rows, refreshed on build-store events) so the menu opens instantly and the disabled reason is current.
CLI: 'axf console session <build>' (prints live/reason) and 'axf console session <build> --open' through the same REST routes; help text in the CLI header.

Voice: console action 'build.session.open' with phrases ('show me the <build> session', 'open the <build> session') resolving a spoken build name to an id by fuzzy title/id match, then the open route; ambiguous names ask back with the top matches.

Plugin docs + notify/lifecycle bookkeeping: README section (UI, REST, MCP, CLI, voice), plugin.json command descriptions for the glossary, lifecycle markers on any line outside the plugin folder, help stub.

Web smoke test: render a build grid with one running build (mocked live session) and one finished build, right-click both, assert enabled/disabled + reason, click Open session and assert the terminal focuses the existing tab and no new session is created.

Run the checks (check-console-control, check-controls, check-theme, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, plugin-lifecycle check, glossary catalog --check, plugin tests), finish the report _claude/builds/reports/right-click-running-build-pop-open.md, THREADS row, push branch and open the PR stating how each piece is reached (deep link, REST, MCP, CLI, voice) and that UI Review is waiting.

Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. Server event bus: add an in-memory ring buffer (default 2000 events, set from the plugin's settings) plus a JSONL tail under the plugin's dataDir, written through data_store (data-store@1, namespace plugins/console-terminal). Add an append(event) function that redacts tokens and keys. Include unit tests for the ring and the redaction

REST: GET /api/plugins/console-terminal/claude-link (snapshot, with since, kind, q and limit filters), GET .../claude-link/stream (SSE live feed with heartbeat and Last-Event-ID resume), POST .../claude-link/clear (clears the view marker, not the log), GET .../claude-link/state (connected, last event, counts per kind). Add route tests

Hook the console server's own Claude and axHub traffic into the bus: outgoing axHub /mcp calls (tool name, held/veto/result state, timing, errors), connect and disconnect, and auth failures, through a small wrapper at the existing call sites. Register it as capability axf.claude-link@1 in plugin_services so no other plugin imports it by folder

Hook the headless launches: deploy/claude-headless.sh and claude-workers.mjs route send launch, account-pick, limit-handoff, exit-code and stderr-error events to the bus. When the console can't be reached they POST to an ingest route (POST .../claude-link/ingest, console token) and append to the JSONL on failure. Add the ingest route and a test with a fake launch

Hook the agent-slot and MCP events: agent-slots.mjs take, queue and release, and the console's own /mcp server tool calls from Claude sessions (session, tool, ok/error), sent to the bus through the same ingest helper (framework-side helper takes the URL from env, never names the plugin folder)

Web UI: a pinned main tab 'Claude link' (first in the Terminal's TabGroup, can't be closed) with a read-only live log view on framework controls and tokens only. EventSource with reconnect and a connected/disconnected chip; each row shows time, a kind chip, source, account/model and summary, and expands to show the detail

UI controls on a role=toolbar Toolbars-plugin toolbar (aria-label, settings id): auto-scroll with Pause/Resume (pauses by itself when scrolled up, shows a 'N new' jump button), a kind filter (multi-select), a text filter, and Clear. Register every control with data-axf-target / control@1 addresses (view:terminal/tab:claude-link, its actions and filters)

Settings: add a sub-tab in Settings → Plugins → Terminal for buffer size, the default kind filter, auto-scroll on/off and showing detail by default, with a level for each setting in the level toolbar. Persist them through the settings registry

API parity: add console actions and plugin commands for open (console_show target view:terminal/tab:claude-link), state, tail (with filters), pause/resume, filter set and clear. Expose them as MCP tools (console-terminal_claude_link_*), the CLI (axf claude-link tail|state|clear|open [--follow] [--kind] [--q]) and voice phrases for AmberX ('show the Claude link', 'what's Claude doing'). Add a deep link ?view=terminal&tab=claude-link

Lifecycle and registries: update install.mjs/uninstall.mjs so the dataDir and JSONL are removed, add axf-plugin:console-terminal markers on lines outside the plugin, add help and README sections, give glossary descriptions to the new commands and CLI, and add a notify.json entry for disconnect/error alerts (off by default)

UI Review: capture desktop and phone shots of the tab (live, paused, filtered, empty) through a vite preview with mocked SSE. Ship 3 layout options as assets in plugins/console-terminal/assets/ (dense rows / cards / split detail) and submit them with review.mjs --choices

# Build: toolbars-1-5-build-orchestrator-incl

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-17T20:39:55.233Z
> Split the toolbar build into multiple builds, about three plugins each, so they run on multiple slots. Land the foundation first.

## What to build
Continue build "Toolbars 1/5: Build orchestrator (incl. merge queue), Gate & rules, Terminal" (toolbars-1-5-build-orchestrator-incl) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-17 20:39):
"Split the toolbar build into multiple builds, about three plugins each, so they run on multiple slots. Land the foundation first."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (4 left, ~36 min):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Merge main so the page-toolbar foundation from rebuild-every-toolbar-page-specific is in (stop if it hasn't landed). Then add page toolbar assets for the Build orchestrator's Pipeline, Pending and Queue pages. Each button is bound to an existing action: split now, queue, unqueue, move, set priority and open the build. Fold the merge-queue buttons (list, add, remove, move) into the Queue page's toolbar. Mount the toolbars on those pages through the foundation's page-toolbar host, each with role=toolbar and a settings id. Register their console-control targets, using the deep link view:builds/tab:pipeline|pending|queue plus toolbar:<id>/button:<id>, so every button can be pressed through REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Commit.
[ ] s2 (~8 min) Add a page toolbar asset for Builds → Gate & rules. Bind its buttons to existing gate actions: open a build rule, run the gate check, toggle a rule and refresh the verdicts. Mount it with the foundation host and register its control@1 / console-control targets (deep link view:builds/tab:gate, readable state, presses through REST, MCP, CLI and voice). Commit.
[ ] s3 (~8 min) Add page toolbar assets for the Terminal and its sessions nav. Bind the buttons to existing terminal actions: new session, jump in, clear, copy, kill or close the session, and filter My sessions. Mount the toolbars with the foundation host, each with role=toolbar and a settings id, and register their console-control targets (deep link view:terminal, readable state, presses through REST, MCP, CLI and voice). Commit.
[ ] s4 (~10 min) Add one test that resolves each new toolbar asset, checks every button is bound to a registered action, and presses one button per page through the console-control API. Then run check-toolbars.mjs, check-console-control.mjs, check-theme.mjs, check-controls.mjs, check-chrome-assets.mjs and the console typecheck and build. Take shots: axf shot for Screenshots, or a UI Review submit with 3 options if the gate requires it. Write _claude/builds/reports/toolbars-1-5-build-orchestrator-incl.md and the THREADS row. Open the PR, with a section on how each toolbar is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice, and put it in the merge queue to land.

Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review �� Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account hulu0241 for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step toolbars-1-5-build-orchestrator-incl <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note toolbars-1-5-build-orchestrator-incl "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.

- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Screenshots that aren't for approval go to Screenshots, not the review queue (Nov 1 2026, Brett): a session checking a screen (e.g. the Breakroom), live captures, PR before/after and other ad-hoc pictures are saved with `axf shot <file> --name "…" --app <app> --screen <route> --group "…"` (`node framework/cli/shot.mjs`, or `POST /api/plugins/ui-review/shots`), which lands in UI Review → Screenshots and never waits for approve / reject; Brett can still *Send to review* one. Only planned UI goes through `review.mjs submit`.
- Every tab group, toolbar, banner and nav menu is an asset with an asset settings interface (Nov 4 2026, Brett; shared rule of the same name; build `tab-group-assets`): every tab row in the console, Molly, AmberX web and axHub web is the framework `TabGroup` on the `tab-group` asset (per-row pick `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>.asset`, per-row overrides `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>`); right-click / long-press any tab group, toolbar, banner, nav or menu bar → Settings… / Change… / Move (`framework/react/components/ChromeContext.tsx`, dialogs `axf.chrome.settings` + `axf.chrome.pick`). Settings dialogs render through the `settings` asset picked for the kind (`axf.chrome.settings.<type>`; the shared default `settings/chrome-<type>` unless the app's copy `settings/chrome-<type>-<app>` is picked; `extends` folds the chain). Every app in `framework/schemas/shared-assets.json` + Expenses carries its six copies (`node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs check` in CI; `backfill` writes missing ones). A strip that must stay hand-drawn (the Terminal tab strip, the workspace pane strip) carries `data-axf-tab-group="<id>"` + `data-fx-ctx-target="tab-group"`; anything else is a finding in `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`, whose ratchet `framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json` only comes down (`--write-baseline` after a real migration). Report: `_claude/builds/reports/tab-group-assets.md`.

- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.

The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Every rebuild ends with a differences report (Oct 20 2026): after any rebuild (Fable rebuilds and every future one, any model), write `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/<pending-id>.md` comparing the new build with the version it replaced: what was removed, kept, changed and added; contract/API/asset/fixture changes; migrations and compatibility notes for apps already using it; tests before vs after; known gaps. Then show Brett the differences and improvements in chat (phone-readable summary, link to the report).
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- The axHub badge is red unless settings come live from axHub (Oct 24 2026, Brett): any axHub status badge or indicator starts red and turns green only while the app is reading its settings live from axHub right now (a fresh read of the hub's settings document succeeded, and a developer app's own hub source is ready). Repo copies, cached copies, local settings, a signed-out session or a read older than two check periods are red. Library: `framework/libs/hubstatus` (`hubLive` in `core.ts`).
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.
- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A new asset that more than one app could use goes in `framework/assets`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Every banner launches expanded (activity, build manager, codebase changes, approvals, systems check, keys, What's new). Activity still only appears while something runs or just finished.
- Done means merged and working (done-means-merged@1, Nov 17 2026, Brett: "We asked you to build it. You should do whatever you have to do to build it, period."): never stop on a failure. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). If you truly cannot go on, write a build note saying what broke and what you tried; the server retries on its ladder (retry, fix, fresh session, another model or account) and escalates to the systems check banner and one phone push only when it runs out. Spec: `framework/spec/DONE-MEANS-MERGED.md`; check `node framework/spec/check-done-means-merged.mjs`.

Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.

A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. split.note: Split by Claude into 27 steps (10 Fable).

steps.text: Plan it in Plan Studio first: park plan 'Flagship professional skin' (plans.mjs add … --status parked --category "Appearance > Skins") listing every skin@1 slot, every registered asset type from asset-types.json, the gaps the skin format can't express yet (context/app/nav menu behaviour, animations, behaviour, hooks, grids, settings interfaces, banner widgets), and the target apps (console, axHub web, AmberX); link the plan id on the build
steps.why: Designs the skin format extension and coverage across apps before any code

steps.text: Audit coverage: run skin-coverage over asset-types.json and write the gap table (type → by slot|parts|reference|bundle|none, what's missing for a full skin) into the build report draft
steps.why: Engine-level read of skin-coverage@1 to decide new slots

steps.text: Schema: add skin@1 slots for motion (animation durations, easings, enter/exit presets, reduced-motion) and behaviour (tap-confirm, hover/press feedback, menu open/close, focus rings) to the skin schema in asset-types.json; regenerate JSON Schemas (axf schemas)
steps.why: Changes the cross-app skin@1 contract

steps.text: Schema: add skin@1 slots for menus (context-menu, app-menu, nav-menu), tab-group, toolbar, banner + banner widget parts, grid, dialog and settings-interface looks, plus a 'hooks' slot (hook@1 refs the skin attaches, default-deny, validated ids); keep old skins valid (all new slots optional, inherit)
steps.why: Contract + migration design for skin@1

steps.text: Engine: teach the skin resolver (resolveLookSkin / skin engine) to apply the new motion and behaviour slots as --fx-motion-* / behaviour tokens and settings keys, child-overrides-parent at hub/app/screen/plugin scope
steps.why: Reference engine internals

steps.text: Engine: apply the menu, tab-group, toolbar, banner/widget, grid, dialog and settings slots through their style targets in schemas/customize.json and the chrome-settings picks; apply the hooks slot through hook@1 registration with an allow-list
steps.why: Engine internals; changes how chrome GUIs are styled in every app

steps.text: Coverage: update skin-coverage@1 declarations so every registered type is reached by the new slots; check-skin-coverage.mjs fails on a type the flagship can't reach
steps.why: Coverage contract

steps.text: Fixtures: add golden cases for the new slots (motion, behaviour, menus, grids, hooks, scope inheritance, an old skin with no new slots) and regenerate with gen-fixtures.mts; record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android on hold)
steps.why: Cross-port conformance fixtures

steps.why: New cross-app read contract

steps.why: Contract fixture for skin-map@1

Flagship skin: fill context-menu, app-menu and nav-menu slots, shipping the menu assets it references

Flagship skin: fill hooks slot (allow-listed hook@1 refs only) and every remaining slot the coverage check reports; skin-coverage shows 100%

## Rules for this job

- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.

- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.

The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.

- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). - Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.
- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A new asset that more than one app could use goes in `framework/assets`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Every notification is in the one registry (Nov 6 2026, Brett: "I need to control all the notifications."): every notification goes through the console's alert hub or asks capability `axf.notify@1` before it sends; a plugin that sends one declares it in its own `notify.json` (`notify-types@1`), and the Notifications panel controls it (Plugins → Notifications; `axf notify-control …`, MCP `notify-control_*`). Approvals and veto notices are guarded: only Brett's own click turns them down, never a session or agent. `python apps/console-web/plugins/notify-control/test.py` fails on an alert source no registry names.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Every banner launches expanded (activity, build manager, codebase changes, approvals, systems check, keys, What's new). Activity still only appears while something runs or just finished.
- Done means merged and working (done-means-merged@1, Nov 17 2026, Brett: "We asked you to build it. You should do whatever you have to do to build it, period."): never stop on a failure. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). If you truly cannot go on, write a build note saying what broke and what you tried; the server retries on its ladder (retry, fix, fresh session, another model or account) and escalates to the systems check banner and one phone push only when it runs out. Spec: `framework/spec/DONE-MEANS-MERGED.md`; check `node framework/spec/check-done-means-merged.mjs`.
