origin.brief:
# Build: settings-fix-part-2-blank-toolbars

## Brett said (verbatim)
> Make every toolbar blank and just all it has is a settings hook. A little gear with a settings hook. That's it. Every toolbar, we'll edit them later. Don't even allow editing or changing the fucking settings layout.

## What to build
Continue build "Settings fix part 2: blank toolbars, locked settings layout" (settings-fix-part-2-blank-toolbars) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"Make every toolbar blank and just all it has is a settings hook. A little gear with a settings hook. That's it. Every toolbar, we'll edit them later. Don't even allow editing or changing the fucking settings layout."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~30 min):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Skins must not restyle toolbars: in the skin-coverage registry, declare the toolbar asset type as not reached by skins (skin by:none, with why), so resolveLookSkin and SkinScope leave toolbar tokens alone; update the coverage check and its fixture
[ ] s2 (~10 min) Settings windows are locked to one interface: the chrome-settings rules always resolve the Gizmo X AI Studio settings interface for every kind and ignore per-app picks (axf.chrome.settings.<type>); old stored picks are read and ignored, never deleted; regenerate the fixtures
[ ] s3 (~10 min) Toolbar override contract: add per-toolbar override (axf.toolbar.<id>.override, off by default). Off means the toolbar uses the shared defaults and counts as not edited. On makes it editable. Turning it off resets that toolbar's keys to defaults. Write the pure helper (isEdited, reset on off) and its unit test
Read first: framework/schemas/asset-types.json, framework/core/engines/skin-coverage.mjs, framework/spec/check-skin-coverage.mjs, framework/spec/fixtures/, framework/core/engines/chrome-settings-rules.mjs, framework/spec/check-chrome-settings.mts, framework/core/engines/tapconfirm.ts, framework/core/engines/toolbar-override.ts, framework/spec/check-toolbar-override.mts
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step settings-fix-part-2-blank-toolbars <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). The VPS opens the PR and links it (Build rules → builds-live).
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account hulu0241 for the Fable phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step settings-fix-part-2-blank-toolbars <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note settings-fix-part-2-blank-toolbars "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Screenshots that aren't for approval go to Screenshots, not the review queue (Nov 1 2026, Brett): a session checking a screen (e.g. the Breakroom), live captures, PR before/after and other ad-hoc pictures are saved with `axf shot <file> --name "…" --app <app> --screen <route> --group "…"` (`node framework/cli/shot.mjs`, or `POST /api/plugins/ui-review/shots`), which lands in UI Review → Screenshots and never waits for approve / reject; Brett can still *Send to review* one. Only planned UI goes through `review.mjs submit`.
- Every tab group, toolbar, banner and nav menu is an asset with an asset settings interface (Nov 4 2026, Brett; shared rule of the same name; build `tab-group-assets`): every tab row in the console, Molly, AmberX web and axHub web is the framework `TabGroup` on the `tab-group` asset (per-row pick `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>.asset`, per-row overrides `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>`); right-click / long-press any tab group, toolbar, banner, nav or menu bar → Settings… / Change… / Move (`framework/react/components/ChromeContext.tsx`, dialogs `axf.chrome.settings` + `axf.chrome.pick`). Settings dialogs render through the `settings` asset picked for the kind (`axf.chrome.settings.<type>`; the shared default `settings/chrome-<type>` unless the app's copy `settings/chrome-<type>-<app>` is picked; `extends` folds the chain). Every app in `framework/schemas/shared-assets.json` + Expenses carries its six copies (`node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs check` in CI; `backfill` writes missing ones). A strip that must stay hand-drawn (the Terminal tab strip, the workspace pane strip) carries `data-axf-tab-group="<id>"` + `data-fx-ctx-target="tab-group"`; anything else is a finding in `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`, whose ratchet `framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json` only comes down (`--write-baseline` after a real migration). Report: `_claude/builds/reports/tab-group-assets.md`.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- The axHub badge is red unless settings come live from axHub (Oct 24 2026, Brett): any axHub status badge or indicator starts red and turns green only while the app is reading its settings live from axHub right now (a fresh read of the hub's settings document succeeded, and a developer app's own hub source is ready). Repo copies, cached copies, local settings, a signed-out session or a read older than two check periods are red. Library: `framework/libs/hubstatus` (`hubLive` in `core.ts`).
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.
- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A new asset that more than one app could use goes in `framework/assets`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins cover every asset type, at any scope (Nov 7 2026, Brett: "Upgrade the skins system so it styles EVERY asset type now in the registry … Skins apply at any scope: global/app/UI/plugin, with child-overrides-parent inheritance … A skin is a design pack; it MAY reference an icon pack … no hardcoded list; add a CI check that fails if a registered asset type has no skin coverage."; build `skins-asset-types`, Fable): how a skin reaches each asset type is worked out from `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` itself (skin-coverage@1, `framework/core/engines/skin-coverage.mjs`): every type is a slot unless excluded; widgets and attachables are styled through their style target in `schemas/customize.json` (`parts` on the skin: box / text / icon / items); the few types with no look or that are bundles declare `"skin": { "by": slot | parts | reference | bundle | none, via?, why? }` on their registry entry. A new type with none of these fails CI (`node framework/spec/check-skin-coverage.mjs`), so a build that adds an asset type gives it a style target or a declaration. A skin MAY name an icon pack (`iconPack`). Scopes follow the icon-map model: hub-wide (`skin` on the shared appearance document) → app (`skin.use`, `skin.inherit` = follow the hub) → screen (`scopes["ui:<view>"]`) → plugin (`scopes["plugin:<id>"]`), the child overrides the parent (`resolveLookSkin`); apps stay their own by default. Every view root and every plugin root is a `<SkinScope>` (framework/react). Parity: Settings → Appearance (Where / What a skin covers), `node framework/cli/skins.mjs use|off|inherit|follow|global|at|coverage|covers`, the theme-manager routes (MCP by plugin-commands), actions `skin.inherit`, `skin.scope`. Report: `_claude/builds/reports/skins-asset-types.md`.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Every banner launches expanded (activity, build manager, codebase changes, approvals, systems check, keys, What's new). Activity still only appears while something runs or just finished.
- Done means merged and working (done-means-merged@1, Nov 17 2026, Brett: "We asked you to build it. You should do whatever you have to do to build it, period."): never stop on a failure. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). If you truly cannot go on, write a build note saying what broke and what you tried; the server retries on its ladder (retry, fix, fresh session, another model or account) and escalates to the systems check banner and one phone push only when it runs out. Spec: `framework/spec/DONE-MEANS-MERGED.md`; check `node framework/spec/check-done-means-merged.mjs`.

# Build: move-everything-axhub-web-console

## Brett said (verbatim)
> I really need to get this axHub and AmberX over the console. I really need that done. With the phone app.

## What to build
Continue build "Move everything from axHub web into the console" (move-everything-axhub-web-console) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"I really need to get this axHub and AmberX over the console. I really need that done. With the phone app."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (155 left, ~23 h):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Inventory every axHub web page, option and setting (approvals, approval log, passes, veto/countdown, users, account, apps/connectors, services, handoff, auth admin, each settings page) and the axHub REST/MCP endpoint behind each one; write the parity map as a hub-console@1 spec draft and save the whole migration as a parked Plan Studio plan
[ ] s2 (~10 min) Define the hub-console@1 contract: one console address per hub screen (view:hub/…), the state shape each screen reads, the action list per screen with personOnly flags (approve/deny/shelve/grant pass stay person-only), and how the console reads them through the hub (proxy, own session, never the console token for decisions); add the schema and a fixture
[ ] s3 (~10 min) Write the hub-console@1 validator and route table (framework/core/hub-console.mjs) with a spec check that holds it to the fixture, and record the deferred Android twin in PORTING.md
[ ] s4 (~10 min) Design the migration of axHub web's saved UI settings (per-user page prefs, approval view options, connector display options) into console settings keys, and write the one-shot migration script with a dry-run mode
[ ] s5 (~8 min) Scaffold the hub-admin console plugin: plugin.json (builtWith, lifecycle dataDir, settings tab under Plugins), install.mjs and uninstall.mjs, and an empty Hub view group registered on the console nav
[ ] s6 (~10 min) Server side of the plugin: a FastAPI router that proxies the hub-console@1 reads to axHub with retries and a clear unavailable state, plus its unit tests
[ ] s7 (~10 min) Approvals screen: live list of held/confirm calls with countdown, title-first reason, collapsible code, and Approve / Deny / Shelve through the approvals-banner relay (Brett's own hub session, personOnly), on framework controls and the tab-group asset
[ ] s8 (~8 min) Approvals API part: deep link view:hub/tab:approvals, state read REST + MCP tool hub_approvals_list, CLI `axf hub approvals`, voice action hub.approvals; decide actions registered personOnly so no session can run them
[ ] s9 (~8 min) Approval log screen: searchable history of decided/expired/denied calls with filters (service, tool, who, outcome) as a DataGrid
[ ] s10 (~6 min) Approval log API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_approval_log, CLI `axf hub approval-log`, voice hub.approvalLog
[ ] s11 (~10 min) Passes and veto settings screen: active passes with revoke, grant pass form (service, tools/scope, minutes), veto countdown length and No-wait status shown read-only where owner-only
[ ] s12 (~8 min) Passes/veto API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_passes_list / hub_pass_revoke / hub_pass_request (grant stays Brett's click), CLI `axf hub passes`, voice hub.passes; countdown setting through control@1
[ ] s13 (~10 min) Users screen: list, invite, roles, disable, with destructive actions behind confirm
[ ] s14 (~8 min) Users API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_users_*, CLI `axf hub users`, voice hub.users; role changes and disable need confirm
[ ] s15 (~8 min) Account screen: profile, sessions/devices with sign-out, linked phone, notification prefs
[ ] s16 (~6 min) Account API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_account_*, CLI `axf hub account`, voice hub.account
[ ] s17 (~10 min) Apps/connectors screen: connected services with status, policies per tool (allow/veto/confirm), add/reconnect/remove connector, token health shown as systems-check items
[ ] s18 (~10 min) Services detail screen: one service's tools, schemas, policy editor and recent calls
[ ] s19 (~10 min) Connectors/services API: deep links (view:hub/tab:connectors, row:<service>), REST + MCP hub_services_list / hub_service_get / hub_policy_set / hub_connector_remove (confirm), CLI `axf hub services`, voice hub.services; register a health@1 check for dead connector keys
[ ] s20 (~8 min) Handoff screen: open handoffs between devices/sessions, send, accept, clear
[ ] s21 (~6 min) Handoff API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_handoff_*, CLI `axf hub handoff`, voice hub.handoff
[ ] s22 (~10 min) Auth admin screen: OAuth clients, API tokens (create shows once, revoke with confirm), sign-in methods; no secret ever stored in the console
[ ] s23 (~8 min) Auth admin API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_auth_*, CLI `axf hub auth`, voice hub.auth; token create/revoke personOnly or confirm per the contract

steps.text: Inventory every axHub web page, option and setting (approvals, approval log, passes, veto/countdown, users, account, apps/connectors, services, handoff, auth admin, each settings page) and the axHub REST/MCP endpoint behind each one; write the parity map as a hub-console@1 spec draft and save the whole migration as a parked Plan Studio plan

Define the hub-console@1 contract: one console address per hub screen (view:hub/…), the state shape each screen reads, the action list per screen with personOnly flags (approve/deny/shelve/grant pass stay person-only), and how the console reads them through the hub (proxy, own session, never the console token for decisions); add the schema and a fixture
Write the hub-console@1 validator and route table (framework/core/hub-console.mjs) with a spec check that holds it to the fixture, and record the deferred Android twin in PORTING.md

Design the migration of axHub web's saved UI settings (per-user page prefs, approval view options, connector display options) into console settings keys, and write the one-shot migration script with a dry-run mode
Scaffold the hub-admin console plugin: plugin.json (builtWith, lifecycle dataDir, settings tab under Plugins), install.mjs and uninstall.mjs, and an empty Hub view group registered on the console nav
Server side of the plugin: a FastAPI router that proxies the hub-console@1 reads to axHub with retries and a clear unavailable state, plus its unit tests

Approvals screen: live list of held/confirm calls with countdown, title-first reason, collapsible code, and Approve / Deny / Shelve through the approvals-banner relay (Brett's own hub session, personOnly), on framework controls and the tab-group asset

Approvals API part: deep link view:hub/tab:approvals, state read REST + MCP tool hub_approvals_list, CLI `axf hub approvals`, voice action hub.approvals; decide actions registered personOnly so no session can run them
Approval log screen: searchable history of decided/expired/denied calls with filters (service, tool, who, outcome) as a DataGrid
Approval log API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_approval_log, CLI `axf hub approval-log`, voice hub.approvalLog
Passes and veto settings screen: active passes with revoke, grant pass form (service, tools/scope, minutes), veto countdown length and No-wait status shown read-only where owner-only
Passes/veto API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_passes_list / hub_pass_revoke / hub_pass_request (grant stays Brett's click), CLI `axf hub passes`, voice hub.passes; countdown setting through control@1
Users screen: list, invite, roles, disable, with destructive actions behind confirm
Users API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_users_*, CLI `axf hub users`, voice hub.users; role changes and disable need confirm
Account screen: profile, sessions/devices with sign-out, linked phone, notification prefs
Account API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_account_*, CLI `axf hub account`, voice hub.account
Apps/connectors screen: connected services with status, policies per tool (allow/veto/confirm), add/reconnect/remove connector, token health shown as systems-check items
Services detail screen: one service's tools, schemas, policy editor and recent calls

Connectors/services API: deep links (view:hub/tab:connectors, row:<service>), REST + MCP hub_services_list / hub_service_get / hub_policy_set / hub_connector_remove (confirm), CLI `axf hub services`, voice hub.services; register a health@1 check for dead connector keys
Handoff screen: open handoffs between devices/sessions, send, accept, clear
Handoff API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_handoff_*, CLI `axf hub handoff`, voice hub.handoff
Auth admin screen: OAuth clients, API tokens (create shows once, revoke with confirm), sign-in methods; no secret ever stored in the console
Auth admin API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_auth_*, CLI `axf hub auth`, voice hub.auth; token create/revoke personOnly or confirm per the contract

Hub settings: one Settings → Plugins → Hub sub-tab with the level toolbar, every former axHub web setting as a registered setting; run the settings migration from step 4 against a copy and wire it into install.mjs

Console-control registration: every hub screen, tab, row and action gets its control address (data-axf-target), toolbars role=toolbar + settings ids, tab rows through TabGroup; make check-console-control, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, check-theme and check-controls pass

Phone Connect tie-in: hub approval and veto notices open the console's Approvals screen through Phone Connect deep links instead of the AmberX app; note the overlap with builds phone-connect and remove-amberx-app-code-once-phone on those builds

Parity check: a script that walks the hub-console@1 route table and fails when any axHub web page/action has no console screen, deep link, REST route, MCP tool, CLI command or voice action; add it to CI

Retire the axHub web UI from this repo's side: apps/axhub-web marked retired in its manifest, axhub.amberxai.com UI paths redirect to the console's Hub screens (deploy config), shared-assets list updated; open the matching axHub-repo change as a follow-up item (server stays backend/MCP only)
Docs and help: plugin README, help entries, glossary descriptions, decision line in memory/decisions.md, rule line that the console is the only hub UI
UI Review: desktop + phone shots of each hub screen with 3 options per screen as assets, submitted with --choices

Run all checks (hub-console spec check, plugin tests, parity, theme/controls/toolbars/console-control, lifecycle --after-uninstall, console typecheck + build), write _claude/builds/reports/move-everything-axhub-web-console.md with how each screen is reached by deep link/REST/MCP/CLI/voice, update the THREADS row, push the branch and open the PR

# Build: auto-lander-never-wait-missing-ui-review

## Brett said (verbatim)
> If it recorded the test of the pipeline and didn't merge it on its own, then the test failed. It should have tested itself before it did the demo.

## What to build
Continue build "Auto-lander: never wait on a missing UI Review, and test the real lander" (auto-lander-never-wait-missing-ui-review) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"If it recorded the test of the pipeline and didn't merge it on its own, then the test failed. It should have tested itself before it did the demo."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Branch: claude/auto-lander-never-wait-missing-ui-review
Steps in this phase (17 left, ~2.5 h):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) gate-rules@1 verdict contract: a UI Review hold applies only when the review item exists in the console. A missing or unposted review gives the verdict 'land, review flagged' (new verdict reason ui-review-missing) instead of 'hold'. Update the spec and the default rule set.
[ ] s2 (~10 min) lander-state@1 schema: add heldSince, holdReason and reviewFlag (missing|unposted|waiting) to each PR record. Migration: existing held records get heldSince = their last-seen time. Regenerate the fixture with check-gate-rules.mjs --write.
[ ] s3 (~8 min) Add check-gate-rules cases: review item missing → land; review unposted → land with a flag; review waiting or changes asked → hold; review rejected → hold; the held-age field is filled in.
[ ] s4 (~10 min) Lander: before holding a PR on UI Review, look the item up in the live console (review.mjs state --pr N --console / GET ui-review state). Not found → land when CI is green and record reviewFlag. Never treat a failed lookup as a hold.
[ ] s5 (~10 min) Merge queue / landing line: use the new verdict, so a stack entry whose review is missing goes ahead and is not parked. Write heldSince and holdReason to lander-state when an entry is truly held.
[ ] s6 (~8 min) Flagged reviews: when a PR lands with a missing or unposted review, file a UI Review notice (Screenshots group '<build id> - missing review') and add a build note, so the review is flagged separately and nothing blocks.
[ ] s7 (~8 min) Gate plugin setting 'Held PR alert after' (minutes, default 60) in Settings → Plugins → Gate, saved through the gate settings store. Add the API: REST setting route, MCP plugin command, `axf gate settings set heldAlertMin`, and a voice action.
[ ] s8 (~10 min) Systems check health@1 check 'held-prs': lists every lander-held PR older than the setting, with the PR, its build, the reason and how long it has been held. It turns red past the limit and is pushed once to the AmberX app.
[ ] s9 (~10 min) 'Land now' fix on the held-prs banner item: puts the PR into the merge queue at the front with an override note (never a direct merge). It is a destructive press, so it needs confirm. API: REST POST /api/plugins/gate/land-now, an MCP command, `axf gate land-now <pr>`, a voice action, and a console_show deep link to the item (row:held-prs/pr:<n>).
[ ] s10 (~6 min) Register the banner item and the Land now button as console-control targets (data-axf-target). Add the state read (GET held PRs with reasons). Pass check-console-control.mjs.
[ ] s11 (~8 min) Builds that ship UI Review items must post them to the live console. review.mjs submit --console exits non-zero when the console doesn't confirm the item id, and the build step that submits fails instead of carrying on.
[ ] s12 (~8 min) Build rule 'ui-review-posted' in the build-rules store: when a build records UI Review choices, the VPS checks that each item exists in the console before the step is ticked, and otherwise marks the step failed with the reason.
[ ] s13 (~10 min) Orchestrator demo self-test: before the demo runs its landing act, run the real lander path on a throwaway PR state through the real gate verdict, the real review lookup and the queue add in check mode. If the self-test fails, the demo stops and files a systems check item instead of recording.
[ ] s14 (~10 min) Demo landing act runs for real (not only a dry run): it confirms the demo PR reaches the merge queue and merges. If it doesn't merge, the demo is marked failed. Add the API: REST demo self-test route, an MCP command, `axf demo selftest`, and a voice action.
[ ] s15 (~10 min) Regression test that replays PR #816: CI green, review item absent from the console → the lander lands it. Also: held > limit → the held-prs check is red with Land now; a submit that can't post → the step fails.
[ ] s16 (~6 min) Help and docs: gate plugin README, ui-review README (must post, fails otherwise), systems-check README (held-prs) and the decisions.md line, with the API paths for each feature.
[ ] s17 (~10 min) Run the checks: check-gate-rules, check-landing-line, check-console-control, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, and the plugin tests. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/auto-lander-never-wait-missing-ui-review.md (before/after, the #816 replay, and how each feature is reached by REST/MCP/CLI/voice). Add the THREADS row, open the PR and add it to the merge queue so it lands when green.
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step auto-lander-never-wait-missing-ui-review <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). The VPS opens the PR and links it (Build rules → builds-live).
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account hulu0241 for the Fable phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step auto-lander-never-wait-missing-ui-review <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note auto-lander-never-wait-missing-ui-review "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Screenshots that aren't for approval go to Screenshots, not the review queue (Nov 1 2026, Brett): a session checking a screen (e.g. the Breakroom), live captures, PR before/after and other ad-hoc pictures are saved with `axf shot <file> --name "…" --app <app> --screen <route> --group "…"` (`node framework/cli/shot.mjs`, or `POST /api/plugins/ui-review/shots`), which lands in UI Review → Screenshots and never waits for approve / reject; Brett can still *Send to review* one. Only planned UI goes through `review.mjs submit`.
- Every tab group, toolbar, banner and nav menu is an asset with an asset settings interface (Nov 4 2026, Brett; shared rule of the same name; build `tab-group-assets`): every tab row in the console, Molly, AmberX web and axHub web is the framework `TabGroup` on the `tab-group` asset (per-row pick `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>.asset`, per-row overrides `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>`); right-click / long-press any tab group, toolbar, banner, nav or menu bar → Settings… / Change… / Move (`framework/react/components/ChromeContext.tsx`, dialogs `axf.chrome.settings` + `axf.chrome.pick`). Settings dialogs render through the `settings` asset picked for the kind (`axf.chrome.settings.<type>`; the shared default `settings/chrome-<type>` unless the app's copy `settings/chrome-<type>-<app>` is picked; `extends` folds the chain). Every app in `framework/schemas/shared-assets.json` + Expenses carries its six copies (`node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs check` in CI; `backfill` writes missing ones). A strip that must stay hand-drawn (the Terminal tab strip, the workspace pane strip) carries `data-axf-tab-group="<id>"` + `data-fx-ctx-target="tab-group"`; anything else is a finding in `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`, whose ratchet `framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json` only comes down (`--write-baseline` after a real migration). Report: `_claude/builds/reports/tab-group-assets.md`.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). - Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.
- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A new asset that more than one app could use goes in `framework/assets`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Every banner launches expanded (activity, build manager, codebase changes, approvals, systems check, keys, What's new). Activity still only appears while something runs or just finished.
- Done means merged and working (done-means-merged@1, Nov 17 2026, Brett: "We asked you to build it. You should do whatever you have to do to build it, period."): never stop on a failure. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). If you truly cannot go on, write a build note saying what broke and what you tried; the server retries on its ladder (retry, fix, fresh session, another model or account) and escalates to the systems check banner and one phone push only when it runs out. Regression test that replays PR #816: CI green, review item absent from the console → the lander lands it. Also: held > limit → the held-prs check is red with Land now; a submit that can't post → the step fails.
Help and docs: gate plugin README, ui-review README (must post, fails otherwise), systems-check README (held-prs) and the decisions.md line, with the API paths for each feature.

gate-rules@1 verdict contract: a UI Review hold applies only when the review item exists in the console. A missing or unposted review gives the verdict 'land, review flagged' (new verdict reason ui-review-missing) instead of 'hold'. Update the spec and the default rule set.

lander-state@1 schema: add heldSince, holdReason and reviewFlag (missing|unposted|waiting) to each PR record. Migration: existing held records get heldSince = their last-seen time. Regenerate the fixture with check-gate-rules.mjs --write.
Add check-gate-rules cases: review item missing → land; review unposted → land with a flag; review waiting or changes asked → hold; review rejected → hold; the held-age field is filled in.

Lander: before holding a PR on UI Review, look the item up in the live console (review.mjs state --pr N --console / GET ui-review state). Not found → land when CI is green and record reviewFlag. Never treat a failed lookup as a hold.

Flagged reviews: when a PR lands with a missing or unposted review, file a UI Review notice (Screenshots group '<build id> - missing review') and add a build note, so the review is flagged separately and nothing blocks.

Orchestrator demo self-test: before the demo runs its landing act, run the real lander path on a throwaway PR state through the real gate verdict, the real review lookup and the queue add in check mode. If the self-test fails, the demo stops and files a systems check item instead of recording.

Demo landing act runs for real (not only a dry run): it confirms the demo PR reaches the merge queue and merges. If it doesn't merge, the demo is marked failed. Add the API: REST demo self-test route, an MCP command, `axf demo selftest`, and a voice action.

Regression test that replays PR #816: CI green, review item absent from the console → the lander lands it. Also: held > limit → the held-prs check is red with Land now; a submit that can't post → the step fails.
Help and docs: gate plugin README, ui-review README (must post, fails otherwise), systems-check README (held-prs) and the decisions.md line, with the API paths for each feature.

gate-rules@1 verdict contract: a UI Review hold applies only when the review item exists in the console. A missing or unposted review gives the verdict 'land, review flagged' (new verdict reason ui-review-missing) instead of 'hold'. Update the spec and the default rule set.
