origin.brief:
# Build: one-true-source-for-every-setting

## Brett said (verbatim)
> All settings need one true fucking source.

## What to build
Continue build "One true source for every setting" (one-true-source-for-every-setting) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"All settings need one true fucking source."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (20 left, ~3.3 h):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Design the settings-source@1 contract: a registry file framework/schemas/settings-sources.json mapping every setting key (or key prefix) to exactly one owning store (data-store namespace + path + owner plugin/module), with readers/writers lists and a 'mirrors' field that must be empty; write the spec framework/spec/SETTINGS-SOURCES.md (one owner per key, readers resolve through the owner, no copies, how a migration moves a key from one store to another)
[ ] s2 (~10 min) Write the resolver core framework/core/settings-source.mjs: load the registry, ownerOf(key), readSetting(key) / writeSetting(key, value) routed through data-files.mjs to the owning store only, refuse writes to a non-owner path; plus a fixture framework/spec/fixtures/settings-sources.json with golden owner lookups (exact keys, prefixes, unknown keys)
[ ] s3 (~10 min) Design the migration helper framework/cli/settings-migrate.mjs: for a duplicated key, read every store that holds it, pick the owner's value (newest-wins when the owner is unset, recorded), write it to the owner, strip the key from the other stores, journal before/after in _claude/builds/reports/one-true-source-for-every-setting/migrations.json; --dry-run lists what would move
[ ] s4 (~10 min) Audit pass 1, console server + plugins: scan apps/console-web/server and apps/console-web/plugins/*/ for settings files and keys (settings.json, *.json under dataDir, SettingsRegistry keys, data_store writes); write the raw inventory to _claude/builds/reports/one-true-source-for-every-setting/audit-console.json (key, store, file, writer, editor UI)
[ ] s5 (~10 min) Audit pass 2, orchestrator + pipeline + agent stores: build-orchestrator (pipeline accounts.json, orchestrator settings), claude-accounts (workers.json), agent-slots, claude-settings, gate/lander settings, push-banner settings; add to the inventory as audit-builds.json
[ ] s6 (~10 min) Audit pass 3, framework + axHub side: framework/core settings (SettingsRegistry keys, appearance@1 / app-look@1 / skins, tapconfirm, chrome settings), framework/libs/settings, lib-hub, axhub-adapter-axf plugin and hub settings documents under /projects/_shared/_data; add audit-framework.json
[ ] s7 (~10 min) Collate the three inventories into the duplicate list: every key held or editable in more than one store or with more than one editing UI/API; for each pick the true owner with a one-line reason; write duplicates.md and fill framework/schemas/settings-sources.json with every audited key and its owner
[ ] s8 (~10 min) Fix duplicate 1, Claude account on/off: make claude-accounts workers.json the one owner of account enabled/worker state; build-orchestrator pipeline reads it through settings-source.mjs (no accounts.json copy of on/off); run settings-migrate for those keys so Moses X's real state is kept
[ ] s9 (~10 min) Remove the duplicate account on/off control and API from the orchestrator (pipeline accounts UI toggle, its REST route and MCP command) and point them at the claude-accounts ones (deep link view:builds/tab:claude-accounts, same REST/MCP/CLI/voice action); update plugin-commands routes and console-control targets
[ ] s10 (~10 min) Fix the next duplicates from duplicates.md in the build stores (e.g. agent caps, lander/auto-merge switches, model defaults between claude-settings and orchestrator): one owner each, readers through settings-source.mjs, migrate values, delete the copies
[ ] s11 (~10 min) Remove the duplicate controls/APIs for the build-store duplicates just fixed: the non-owner settings fields become a read-only line with a 'Change in <owner>' link (console_show deep link); drop their write routes and MCP/CLI/voice aliases, keeping one action per setting
[ ] s12 (~10 min) Fix the console server + plugin duplicates from duplicates.md (settings kept both in a plugin dataDir and the console settings registry or local storage): one owner, migrate, readers resolve through server/data_store.py owner lookup
[ ] s13 (~10 min) Python twin of the resolver: server/settings_source.py reads framework/schemas/settings-sources.json and refuses a write to a non-owner path; wire data_store.py writes through it; unit test in server tests
[ ] s14 (~10 min) Fix the framework/axHub duplicates from duplicates.md (e.g. look values held in both appearance@1 and app-look@1 or local SettingsRegistry copies, hub vs repo settings snapshots): one owner, migrate, remove local copies; record any Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md
[ ] s15 (~10 min) Run settings-migrate.mjs for every remaining duplicate on the real hub data (dry-run first, then apply), commit the migration journal, verify each owner holds the expected value and the old stores no longer carry the key
[ ] s16 (~10 min) API for the registry: REST GET /api/settings-sources (list, owner of key, duplicates found by a live scan), MCP console tools settings_source_owner / settings_source_check, CLI `axf settings-source owner|list|check`, voice action settings.source, deep link view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=sources
[ ] s17 (~10 min) Small read-only Settings → Sources view listing each setting key, its one owner and a jump to the owner's control (framework DataGrid + TabGroup, tokens only, data-axf-target registered); submit 3 UI Review options per the ui-choices rule
[ ] s18 (~10 min) CI check framework/cli/check-settings-sources.mjs: static scan of every store writer (data-files writeData, data_store.py writes, SettingsRegistry.set, json writes under plugin dataDirs) and every settings asset; fails when a key is defined or written in two stores, when a written key has no registry owner, or when a non-owner writes it; add a fixture test and wire into .github/workflows
[ ] s19 (~10 min) Write the rule into the shared build rules store: build-rules@1 rule 'one-setting-source' (every setting has exactly one true source in settings-sources.json; new settings register an owner; no copies; CI check name) via `axf gate build-rules`, plus a line in _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md and memory/decisions.md with Brett's verbatim words
[ ] s20 (~10 min) Tests, report, THREADS row and PR: run check-settings-sources, settings-source fixture test, plugin and server tests, check-console-control, check-theme, tracker --check; write _claude/builds/reports/one-true-source-for-every-setting.md listing every duplicate found, owner picked, values migrated, controls/APIs removed, and how each new feature is reached (REST, MCP, CLI, voice, deep link); add THREADS row; open the PR
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step one-true-source-for-every-setting <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). The VPS opens the PR and links it (Build rules → builds-live).
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Fable phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step one-true-source-for-every-setting <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note one-true-source-for-every-setting "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Plugins: each plugin gets a Plugin Manager entry (info, enable/disable, logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). Two enabled editors of one kind are shown as an info-level clash in the Plugin Manager, not an error.
- Plugin Manager (Oct 18 2026; Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026): the console's plugin manager is the `plugin-manager` plugin; its model is the cross-port `plugin-inventory@1` engine (`framework/core/engines/plugins.ts` = Kotlin `PluginInventoryEngine` = the plugin's `server/engine.py`, one fixture). It opens each plugin's UI and settings when they exist and lists dependencies in detail (what it needs and whether it's met, who provides it, who needs it, clashes). Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.
- One banner on screen — embed@1 (Oct 21 2026, Brett): an app shown inside another app's frame hides the chrome the host shows, its banner by default. Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. Settings grey the slot out ("Shown by <host>"). No app hosts others today (Patches, the first host, was retired Nov 3 2026). Engines on both ports, fixture `spec/fixtures/embed.json`.
- One Banners settings (Oct 22 2026, Brett): every banner plugin's settings are one interface (Settings → Plugins → Banners and the right-click Banner settings: a tab per banner with its look, behaviour and own settings). A new banner plugin declares `label`, `icon` and `settingsTab` on its banner so its settings join in.
- Plugins a host makes unneeded aren't loaded (Oct 22 2026, Brett): when an app runs inside a host (any app in a host's tab), plugins that would draw something the host already draws, or that the host makes unnecessary, aren't loaded on that page and are logged at launch. A plugin says when in its web library: `embed: { skipWhen: ['embedded' | 'take:<fn>' | 'hidden:<type>'] }` (`embedSkipReason` in `framework/core/engines/embed.ts`); `installLibraries` skips it, `rt.skippedLibraries` keeps why, the terminal gets one line each plus a summary, Settings → Plugins lists them. Page mode (an app's settings page in the host) never skips. Standalone everything loads. Every new plugin that only draws on chrome a host hides, or does a job a host takes, declares it.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- The axHub badge is red unless settings come live from axHub (Oct 24 2026, Brett): any axHub status badge or indicator starts red and turns green only while the app is reading its settings live from axHub right now (a fresh read of the hub's settings document succeeded, and a developer app's own hub source is ready). Repo copies, cached copies, local settings, a signed-out session or a read older than two check periods are red. Library: `framework/libs/hubstatus` (`hubLive` in `core.ts`).
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Done means merged and working (done-means-merged@1, Nov 17 2026, Brett: "We asked you to build it. You should do whatever you have to do to build it, period."): never stop on a failure. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). If you truly cannot go on, write a build note saying what broke and what you tried; the server retries on its ladder (retry, fix, fresh session, another model or account) and escalates to the systems check banner and one phone push only when it runs out. Spec: `framework/spec/DONE-MEANS-MERGED.md`; check `node framework/spec/check-done-means-merged.mjs`.

builds.title: VPS sets every build status in the manifest; orchestrator files tabs from it
builds.detail: Rule from Brett: the VPS is the only thing that sets a build's status. Status lives in the build manifest the VPS owns. As soon as a build starts on the VPS, its manifest status becomes building. When the VPS hands a build back to the orchestrator (stopped, killed, crashed, paused, kicked out) and its status is building or on hold, the orchestrator files it straight into the Hold tab: never Pending, never auto-relaunched. The orchestrator never computes status itself; it only reads the manifest status and puts the build in the matching tab. Hold must work on running builds too (stop the session on the VPS, keep the branch and ticked steps, file to Hold). Today hold only works on queued builds, and a paused build (flagship-professional-skin-covering-2) got relaunched on its own. Add tests: started build returned => Hold; held build never relaunched by the dispatcher. Part of the everything-on-the-VPS rule; coordinate with move-server-side-console-parts-onto-vps.

"That failed. Shouldn't the VPS be doing this on its own? Nothing should be sitting there."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.

Add a stop core to the orchestrator CLI: `orchestrator.mjs stop <id> [--reason]` finds the build's running tmux session, kills it on the VPS host (the same host-exec path the launcher uses), frees its agent slot, sets the build to Hold (status hold, with a note naming who stopped it and why), and records a no-relaunch flag the dispatcher must honour. It is idempotent: a build with no live session is still set to Hold. Commit.

Make the dispatcher and the crash/requeue path honour the stop: pipeline.mjs tick and the 'session stopped with steps left → back to Queue' logic must skip builds on Hold or carrying the stopped flag, so a stopped build is never relaunched until Brett re-queues it. Commit.

Unit tests for stop: a running build gets its session killed (fake tmux / host exec), its slot freed, its status set to Hold with a note; a build with no session still gets Hold; the dispatcher skips a stopped build and the requeue path never puts it back in the Queue. Commit.

API part, REST: add POST /api/plugins/build-orchestrator/builds/<id>/stop (needs confirm, destructive) calling the stop core, plus GET of each running build's session state (tmux session, host, started, stoppable) on the Active list route. Route tests. Commit.

API part, MCP + CLI + voice: list the stop route in plugin-commands (MCP `build-orchestrator_stop`, needs confirm), add `axf orchestrator stop <id>` through the CLI, and add the AmberX voice action `build.stop` with its description and confirm. Commit.

UI: add a Stop button on every running row of the Active tab using the framework Button (tokens only, destructive confirm string, tap-to-confirm in its row toolbar with role=toolbar + aria-label). builds.title: Fix CI red on main: watchdog test vs done-means-merged guard, alerts engine job
builds.detail:
CI on main has been red since at least 2026-11-17 19:19 (runs 44171482751, 44186908843) on two jobs, and every PR inherits it (seen on #827):
1. builds.title: axHub repo: JSON routes for connectors, handoff and auth admin; redirect old pages to the console
builds.detail:
The console is the only hub UI now (build move-everything-axhub-web-console, hub-console@1). axHub keeps serving JSON pages for approvals, log, passes, go pass, users, account, handoff, apps and the policy table; the console shows these hub parts as "the hub has no route for this yet" (hub_missing) until the axHub repo grows the routes:
- POST /auth/api/services {namespace, type, config}  (connectors/add: axHub configures services in its own CLI (axhub services add); no JSON route yet.; today: axhub services add <namespace> --type <type>)
- POST /auth/api/services/{namespace}/reconnect  (connectors/reconnect: No reconnect route on the hub yet.; today: axhub services refresh <namespace>)
- DELETE /auth/api/services/{namespace}  (connectors/remove: No remove route on the hub yet.; today: axhub services remove <namespace>)
- POST /auth/api/handoff/{id}/accept {device}  (handoff/accept: Device-to-device handoff waits on the hub protocol (AXPP).)
- DELETE /auth/api/handoff/{id}  (handoff/clear: No delete route for a handoff run yet.)
- POST /auth/api/auth/tokens {label, scopes[], expiresInDays}  (auth/token-create: No token admin route on the hub yet; the secret is shown once and never stored in the console.)
- DELETE /auth/api/auth/tokens/{id}  (auth/token-revoke: No token admin route on the hub yet.)
- POST /auth/api/auth/clients {name, redirectUris[]}  (auth/client-add: OAuth clients are configured on the hub itself today.)
- DELETE /auth/api/auth/clients/{id}  (auth/client-remove: OAuth clients are configured on the hub itself today.)

Also on the axHub side: redirect the old HTML pages (/auth/admin/approvals, /auth/account, /auth/admin/users, …) straight to https://console.amberxai.com/?axf-open=hub.open:<screen>[:<id>] instead of the retired web app, keep /auth/api/* and /mcp as they are, and drop the axhub-web static site from the deploy once the console redirect has run for a while. Repo: MossesX/axHub (packages/server/src/*-web.ts).

steps.text: Read framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs, apps/console-web/plugins/agent-slots/ and pipeline.mjs tick. Write down in _claude/builds/reports/vps-frees-stale-build-slots-every-minute.md how slot entries are stored: running and heavy entries, pid, session name, startedAt, queue. Include the three stale cases Brett hit (3-day-old rhonda-ci-fix job, finished tmux sessions, builds-store verify heavy processes) and the liveness rule for each.

Add a pure liveness core, framework/core/slot-liveness.mjs. Given one slot entry, a process-table snapshot (pid, ppid, cmd, etime) and a list of tmux sessions with pane_dead and pane_current_command, it returns a verdict: alive, dead (no pid / no claude process), finished (tmux session there but claude exited or pane dead), hung-heavy (heavy step past its max runtime), or orphan-session. Every verdict comes with a plain reason. It has no side effects.

Add settings defaults for the reaper to the agent-slots settings: reaper.enabled (on), reaper.heavyMaxMin (30), reaper.graceSec (90, so a just-launched slot is never reaped), reaper.closeFinishedSessions (on) and reaper.launchNext (on). Read them through the existing settings loader in agent-slots.mjs.

Add an `agent-slots.mjs reap [--dry-run] [--json]` subcommand. It takes the slots lock, snapshots ps and `tmux list-sessions/list-panes`, runs slot-liveness on every running and heavy entry, and frees the dead and finished entries under the same lock. Entries inside the grace window are skipped.

Make reap act on what it frees: SIGTERM then SIGKILL the process group of a hung-heavy step, `tmux kill-session` a finished axf-* session (only sessions the slots table owns, never the shared human tmux session), and drop orphan queue entries whose build is no longer queued.

Log every freed slot through data-store@1 (framework/core/data-files.mjs), namespace plugins/agent-slots/reaped/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl. Each line records at, slot id, build/session, verdict, reason, age, pid, action taken (freed/killed/closed) and host. Register the path in framework/schemas/data-store-paths.json.

After freeing at least one slot, reap calls the pipeline dispatcher (`pipeline.mjs tick`, in-process or as a child) so the next queued build starts at once. The tick result goes in the reap summary. --no-launch skips it.

Add the every-minute VPS timer. deploy/slot-reaper.sh wraps `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs reap --json` with flock so runs never overlap. Install a cron line `axf-slot-reaper` (* * * * *) the same way the axf-pipeline cron is installed (install/uninstall in the agent-slots plugin's install.mjs/uninstall.mjs, and in framework/deploy/axf-deploy.sh where the pipeline cron is set). Write a last-run heartbeat file.

Add a systems-check health@1 check, agent-slots.reaper: red when the reaper heartbeat is older than 3 minutes or the cron line is missing. Its auto-fix reinstalls the cron and runs one reap. Also report a freed-slot count over the last hour in the check detail.

Add the API for the reaper in the agent-slots plugin server. GET /api/plugins/agent-slots/reaper (settings, last run, heartbeat), GET /reaper/log?limit=, POST /reaper/run {dryRun}, PUT /reaper/settings. Add them to the plugin's commands so MCP plugin-commands exposes agent-slots_reaper_* tools, add the CLI `axf slots reap|reaper-log`, and add voice actions slots.reap / slots.reaper-log.

UI in Settings → Plugins → Agent cap: a Reaper section built from framework controls and tokens (Switch for enabled/close sessions/launch next, number fields for heavy max and grace, a Run now Button, a DataGrid of freed slots from /reaper/log). Each control registers its target through the framework controls (console-control address view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins … agent-slots.reaper) so console_show / console_open deep-link to it.

Add fixtures and a CI check. framework/spec/fixtures/slot-liveness.json holds cases: rhonda-ci-fix 3 days old with no pid, finished tmux pane, builds-store verify heavy past its cap, a fresh slot in grace, a live claude. framework/spec/check-slot-reaper.mjs runs slot-liveness against them and runs `reap --dry-run` on a temp slots file with a faked ps/tmux (AXF_SLOTS_PS / AXF_SLOTS_TMUX env hooks). It also asserts the cron line is installed by install.mjs. Wire it into .github/workflows/android.yml next to the other spec checks.

Docs. Run plugin-lifecycle check agent-slots --after-uninstall, check-theme, check-controls and check-console-control.

Tests, report, THREADS row and PR. Run check-slot-reaper.mjs, the agent-slots plugin tests, `agent-slots.mjs reap --dry-run` on the live VPS table (paste the verdicts for the stale entries into the report), then one real reap and the freed-slot log lines. Add the THREADS.md row, push branch claude/vps-frees-stale-build-slots-every-minute, open the PR, link it with builds-live.mjs link, and send the Reaper settings section to UI Review.

Rule from Brett: before every build launch and whenever anything jams, check for stale slots, ghost processes and dead sessions and clear them first. The VPS and the console both run this check and back each other up: if one misses it, the other catches it.

builds.title: One landing line: pull in main and merge one build at a time
builds.detail: Landing must be one strict line on the VPS: finished builds wait in a single ordered landing line; only one lands at a time. For each: fetch main, merge main into the branch, resolve clashes (automatic fix session if needed), run checks against that fresh main, merge to main, then the next one starts from the new main. Nothing else may push to main while one is landing. A build that finishes building goes straight into the line. Lives in the Watchdog plugin with its settings and order. CI check.

origin.said: We have to put everything in a line, pull in main and merge one at a time.

split.note: Split by Claude into 20 steps (5 Fable).

steps.text: Read the existing landing-line@1 engine, its fixture and spec (framework/core/landing-line.mjs, framework/spec/check-landing-line.mjs, framework/spec/fixtures/landing-line*.json), the merge-queue lander (land.mjs) and the Watchdog plugin. Write the gap list in _claude/builds/reports/one-landing-line-pull-main-merge-one.md: which parts already land one at a time, which still batch, and every place that pushes to main.

Extend the landing-line@1 contract to a strict single line: one ordered list, at most one entry 'landing', per-entry phases (waiting → fetch-main → merge-main → resolving → checks → merging → landed | failed), the main SHA it was checked against, and a recorded main-lock holder. Update the JSON Schema and the spec doc. Migrate old merge-queue stack records into line entries without losing any.

Engine state machine in framework/core/landing-line.mjs: pure functions next(), advance(entry, event), and the rule that the next entry starts only once the one before it is landed or failed, always from the new main SHA. Stacks and batches get flattened into the line.

Main lock in the engine: acquireMainLock / releaseMainLock / mainLockHolder with a stale-lock timeout, plus a guard function that refuses any main push not made by the current lock holder. The builds-live [skip ci] status commits are the only exemption and wait for the lock window.

Regenerate the landing-line fixture with node framework/spec/check-landing-line.mjs --write, and add cases for one at a time, starts from new main, red → fix session, clash → resolve, lock refusal and the migration. Make the check pass.

Watchdog runner: apps/console-web/plugins/watchdog/landing-line.mjs tick takes the line's head and runs the fetch-main and merge-main phases in a scratch worktree (git fetch origin main; git merge origin/main into the branch), recording each phase on the entry through data-store@1.

Clash phase: on merge conflicts, first auto-resolve the generated files (store, THREADS, tracker, fixtures by regenerating them). If conflicts remain, launch one automatic fix session through deploy/claude-headless.sh (agent-slots, agent-job 'land' owner) with the conflict list, and mark the entry 'resolving'. If the fix fails, the entry fails and the line moves on.

Checks phase: push the merged branch, wait for CI on that exact head (dispatch android.yml once if no pull_request run starts) and record the main SHA it was tested against. If main moved, go back to fetch-main. If CI is red, file a fix build and move on.

Merge phase: take the main lock, merge the PR to main (fast-forward or merge commit, head pinned), release the lock, mark the entry landed, link it with builds-live.mjs link and set the build to complete. Then the next entry starts from the new main.

Enforce the main lock in every writer that can push or merge to main (land.mjs, push-banner auto-merge, builds-live.mjs, pipeline lander, gate auto-lander): each one calls the guard and backs off while another build is landing. builds-live queues its status commits until the lock is free.
Retire the batching paths: the merge-queue stacks and the Landin' Lenny batch job now add entries to the line one by one. Keep the old land.mjs queue commands as aliases onto the line.

Built → line hook: when a build reaches 'built' (all steps done, PR open), a build-hook@1 listener adds it to the end of the line straight away, without duplicates. The order follows priority tags, and manual moves win.

Cron and service: register the watchdog landing-line tick (every minute, a single-run lock so two ticks never overlap) on the VPS next to axf-pipeline, and add a health@1 check that turns red with an Auto fix when the line is stuck, the lock is stale or main moved without the lock.

Watchdog settings: add the line's settings (on/off, stale-lock minutes, max fix-session tries, CI wait timeout, auto-add built builds) to plugin.json settings, shown as a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins → Watchdog with the level toolbar, framework controls and tokens only.

Watchdog Landing line view: an ordered DataGrid of the entries with the phase, the main SHA and the lock holder, the landing one highlighted, and actions to move up or down, remove, retry and pause the line. TabGroup and Toolbars-plugin toolbar (role=toolbar), console-control targets registered with data-axf-target.

API parity: REST routes /api/plugins/watchdog/line (GET state, POST add/move/remove/retry/pause/resume, GET/PUT settings), MCP through plugin-commands, the CLI 'axf land line list|add|move|remove|retry|pause|resume|lock', voice actions 'landing.line.*', a console_show deep link view:watchdog/tab:landing-line, and control@1 targets appended last.

CI check: framework/spec/check-landing-line.mjs also scans the repo statically for any main push or merge path that skips the main-lock guard, and verifies the one-landing-at-a-time invariant on the live line export. Wire it into .github/workflows/android.yml.
Tests: unit tests for the watchdog runner phases using a fake git remote (clash, red CI, main moved, lock refusal), python tests for the routes, and the plugin-lifecycle check --after-uninstall.

UI Review: shoot the Landing line view and its settings tab on desktop and phone with 3 option assets (ui-choices@1) under apps/console-web/plugins/watchdog/assets/, and submit them with review.mjs submit --choices. Update the help stub and docs at _claude/memory/docs/landing-line.md.

Run the full checks (check-landing-line, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-console-control, check-chrome-assets, builds-store verify, tracker --check). Finish the report at _claude/builds/reports/one-landing-line-pull-main-merge-one.md with the API reach list, add the THREADS row, open the PR stating how each feature is reached (REST/MCP/CLI/voice/deep link) and that UI Review is waiting, and link it with builds-live.mjs link.

# Build: vps-never-gives-up-fix-land-every-build

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "VPS never gives up: fix and land every build until all options are exhausted" (vps-never-gives-up-fix-land-every-build) — Phase 1, model Opus.
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Page mode (an app's settings page in the host) never skips. Standalone everything loads. Every new plugin that only draws on chrome a host hides, or does a job a host takes, declares it.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.
- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A new asset that more than one app could use goes in `framework/assets`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Every banner launches expanded (activity, build manager, codebase changes, approvals, systems check, keys, What's new). Activity still only appears while something runs or just finished.
- Done means merged and working (done-means-merged@1, Nov 17 2026, Brett: "We asked you to build it. You should do whatever you have to do to build it, period."): never stop on a failure. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). If you truly cannot go on, write a build note saying what broke and what you tried; the server retries on its ladder (retry, fix, fresh session, another model or account) and escalates to the systems check banner and one phone push only when it runs out. Spec: `framework/spec/DONE-MEANS-MERGED.md`; check `node framework/spec/check-done-means-merged.mjs`.

# Build: one-build-time-always-split-to-fill

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "One build at a time, always split to fill every slot: split-ID gate, Splitting status, expandable queue row with live per-part badges" (one-build-time-always-split-to-fill) — Phase 2, model Opus.
This phase downgrades Fable → Opus: fine, no approval needed (it is recorded when you tick its first step).
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Branch: claude/one-build-time-always-split-to-fill · PR #846
Steps in this phase (8 left, ~1.2 h):
[x] s6 (~10 min) Write the spec tests for split, state machine and one-at-a-time in framework/spec/check-build-split.mjs: no file overlap, every slot filled, roll-up, all-or-nothing, migration loses nothing.
[x] s7 (~10 min) Auto-split on intake in pipeline.mjs. A pending build is set to 'splitting' at once, the splitter runs with the current free-slot count, and the split plan and splitId are written to the store, after which the build is ready for the Queue. The old orchestrator-auto-split-tab path is removed.
[x] s8 (~10 min) Dispatcher tick: when the Queue gets a split build and no other run is active, lock main, then create one branch per part from the locked sha and start each part in its own agent slot with --account routing.
[x] s9 (~10 min) Report part status. The headless part runner writes waiting, building, testing, rebuilding, failed and done to the store through builds-live, using the part id and splitId from env, and records a slot heartbeat.
[x] s10 (~10 min) Combine step. When all parts are done, merge the part branches into one combine branch and set the status to 'combining'. A clash or any failed part marks the run failed, nothing lands, and main is unlocked.
[x] s11 (~10 min) Landing hand-off. The combine branch becomes one PR in the landing line with one CI run. The run status follows ci, merging, merged, live (deploy seen) and finished, and main unlocks at finished or failed.
[x] s12 (~8 min) Server gate rule 'require-split-id' (on by default). Add it to the default gate rule set and record that it coordinates with the server-gate build's rule instead of duplicating it.
[x] s13 (~10 min) Enforce the gate at the launcher. deploy/claude-headless.sh and model-gate.mjs launch refuse any build start that has no orchestrator build id or no valid splitId in the store (exit 3 with the reason).
[x] s14 (~8 min) Send rejected starts to the orchestrator Failed tab: write a rejection record (who, when, the reason, what was missing) to the store as failed with gateReason, journalled.
[x] s15 (~8 min) Show the rule on Gate & rules with its description and on/off switch, and make sure the Failed tab shows the gate reason on rejected rows.

builds.title: Out-of-credits account failover: flag the dead account and move every slot to the backup
builds.detail:
Brett's words: "So Moses X just ran out of credits. So when it runs out of credits, it needs to note that and stop using it. It needs to switch everything over to Hulu."

When a Claude account (e.g. MossesX) runs out of credits, the orchestrator records it on the account (out of credits + timestamp + which build/step hit it), stops handing that account any new slots or steps, and moves every running and queued slot over to the backup account ("Hulu" (name from voice transcription, confirm)). In-flight steps on the dead account get handed off on the same branch, not restarted. Show the account switch in the banner and the builds journal.

origin.brief:
# Build: stop-push-storm-builds-live-pushes-build

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "Stop the push storm: builds-live pushes at build end only, Expenses rebuilds only on its own changes" (stop-push-storm-builds-live-pushes-build) [orchestrator] — Phase 1, model Opus.
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (2 left, ~35 min):
[ ] s1 (~20 min) builds-live.mjs: stop pushing to main on every store write; push once when a build ends (built, landed, failed, cancelled). Keep the local store and journal writes. Update the CLAUDE.md 'Builds go live to main' line and _claude/builds/README.md
[ ] s2 (~15 min) apps/expenses/deploy/install.sh: rebuild only when apps/expenses (or the framework files it bakes) changed since the running image's commit; skip status-only commits
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step stop-push-storm-builds-live-pushes-build <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). The VPS opens the PR and links it (Build rules → builds-live).
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account hulu0241 for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step stop-push-storm-builds-live-pushes-build <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note stop-push-storm-builds-live-pushes-build "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- VPS: Hostinger, runs Coolify; its Traefik proxy owns 80/443, so web apps go behind it as Coolify apps (no separate nginx). Domain `amberxai.com`.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Every rebuild ends with a differences report (Oct 20 2026): after any rebuild (Fable rebuilds and every future one, any model), write `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/<pending-id>.md` comparing the new build with the version it replaced: what was removed, kept, changed and added; contract/API/asset/fixture changes; migrations and compatibility notes for apps already using it; tests before vs after; known gaps. Then show Brett the differences and improvements in chat (phone-readable summary, link to the report).
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Every notification is in the one registry (Nov 6 2026, Brett: "I need to control all the notifications."): every notification goes through the console's alert hub or asks capability `axf.notify@1` before it sends; a plugin that sends one declares it in its own `notify.json` (`notify-types@1`), and the Notifications panel controls it (Plugins → Notifications; `axf notify-control …`, MCP `notify-control_*`). Approvals and veto notices are guarded: only Brett's own click turns them down, never a session or agent. `python apps/console-web/plugins/notify-control/test.py` fails on an alert source no registry names.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Done means merged and working (done-means-merged@1, Nov 17 2026, Brett: "We asked you to build it. You should do whatever you have to do to build it, period."): never stop on a failure. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). If you truly cannot go on, write a build note saying what broke and what you tried; the server retries on its ladder (retry, fix, fresh session, another model or account) and escalates to the systems check banner and one phone push only when it runs out. Spec: `framework/spec/DONE-MEANS-MERGED.md`; check `node framework/spec/check-done-means-merged.mjs`.

builds.title: URGENT — All data to Postgres: builds store first, then every JSON data file
builds.detail:
Priority: Urgent (Brett).

Brett's words: "I don't want any data stored in JSON period. Everything needs to be a Postgres table. Everything, dude. Not a single piece of data should be stored in JSON."

Found Nov 18 2026: _claude/builds/store.json (2 MB+) is still a file with a lockfile (/axf/_claude/builds/store.json.lock); console writes fail with 'builds store is locked'. data-store-paths.json maps builds/* but the namespace was never cut over. axf-data-db (postgres:16) is running.

Goal: every piece of runtime data (builds store + journal, pending, queue, plans, notes, settings, plugin data dirs, agent-slots, worker accounts...) lives in real Postgres tables through axf-data, not JSON blobs or files. Builds first (biggest, most contended). Repo code/config that is source (asset@1 assets, schemas, plugin.json manifests) stays in the repo. Any JSON in the repo that is data becomes a read-only export or goes away. Update CLAUDE.md and the data-store doc to the new rule.

notes.text:
Brett, Nov 18 2026 (voice), correction to the earlier write-only note: "We're going to move the build store over to a Postgres table. We're going to still allow the orchestrator to check it in case it's going to build a feature that's going to break an already built feature, or in case that feature has already gone live through another build. We want to keep the orchestrator able to make sure we're not going to break something."

So: the builds history table is NOT write-only. Before launching a build, the orchestrator queries it (indexed search by feature, files, plugin, title words) for (a) the same feature already shipped by another build and (b) built features the new build could break. It pulls only matching rows, never the whole history. The pipeline's routine tick still reads only the live/active builds.

- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Plugins: each plugin gets a Plugin Manager entry (info, enable/disable, logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). Two enabled editors of one kind are shown as an info-level clash in the Plugin Manager, not an error.
- Plugin Manager (Oct 18 2026; Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026): the console's plugin manager is the `plugin-manager` plugin; its model is the cross-port `plugin-inventory@1` engine (`framework/core/engines/plugins.ts` = Kotlin `PluginInventoryEngine` = the plugin's `server/engine.py`, one fixture). It opens each plugin's UI and settings when they exist and lists dependencies in detail (what it needs and whether it's met, who provides it, who needs it, clashes). Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.
- One banner on screen — embed@1 (Oct 21 2026, Brett): an app shown inside another app's frame hides the chrome the host shows, its banner by default. Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. Settings grey the slot out ("Shown by <host>"). No app hosts others today (Patches, the first host, was retired Nov 3 2026). Engines on both ports, fixture `spec/fixtures/embed.json`.
- One Banners settings (Oct 22 2026, Brett): every banner plugin's settings are one interface (Settings → Plugins → Banners and the right-click Banner settings: a tab per banner with its look, behaviour and own settings). A new banner plugin declares `label`, `icon` and `settingsTab` on its banner so its settings join in.
- Plugins a host makes unneeded aren't loaded (Oct 22 2026, Brett): when an app runs inside a host (any app in a host's tab), plugins that would draw something the host already draws, or that the host makes unnecessary, aren't loaded on that page and are logged at launch. A plugin says when in its web library: `embed: { skipWhen: ['embedded' | 'take:<fn>' | 'hidden:<type>'] }` (`embedSkipReason` in `framework/core/engines/embed.ts`); `installLibraries` skips it, `rt.skippedLibraries` keeps why, the terminal gets one line each plus a summary, Settings → Plugins lists them. Page mode (an app's settings page in the host) never skips. Standalone everything loads. Every new plugin that only draws on chrome a host hides, or does a job a host takes, declares it.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Done means merged and working (done-means-merged@1, Nov 17 2026, Brett: "We asked you to build it. You should do whatever you have to do to build it, period."): never stop on a failure. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). If you truly cannot go on, write a build note saying what broke and what you tried; the server retries on its ladder (retry, fix, fresh session, another model or account) and escalates to the systems check banner and one phone push only when it runs out. Spec: `framework/spec/DONE-MEANS-MERGED.md`; check `node framework/spec/check-done-means-merged.mjs`.
