# Build: postgres-part-c-console-state-settings

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "Postgres part C: console state, settings, alerts and plugin data dirs to tables" (postgres-part-c-console-state-settings) [data] — Phase 1, model Opus.
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (4 left, ~1.8 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) s4.4: console state.json + small console files, deploys log, alerts, settings (hub-settings becomes the source), notifications, home cards, token log, notes, control inventory, amberx notes, app catalog rows → console_state, console_deploys, alerts, alerts_seen, settings, notifications, home_cards, token_log, notes, control_targets/tabs, app_catalog; backfill, verify, cut over
[ ] s2 (~30 min) s4.5a: large plugin data first: chat-viewer SQLite → chats (+ tts blobs), shipped-features SQLite → ledger_* as source, push-banner, agent-swarm, ui-review; backfill, verify, cut over
[ ] s3 (~30 min) s4.5b: remaining plugin data dirs per the inventory table (agent-manager, ai-assistant, activity, systems-check, claude-accounts, handoff, terminal, phone-connect, todo-manager...) plus plugin_settings and plugin_audit for small config and audit files; backfill, verify, cut over
[ ] s4 (~15 min) Tests, report and PR: per-namespace count checks, report _claude/builds/reports/postgres-part-c.md, PR through CI and the merge queue
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step postgres-part-c-console-state-settings <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). The VPS opens the PR and links it (Build rules → builds-live).
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account hulu0241 for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step postgres-part-c-console-state-settings <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note postgres-part-c-console-state-settings "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Plugins: each plugin gets a Plugin Manager entry (info, enable/disable, logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). builds.detail:
Brett (voice, Nov 19 2026): "There needs to be something on the VPS to detect it when things are in the queue and not running … and then fix it. On its own, without AI. Or with, if the switch is on. Default off." Also: "put some chatter in the group chat asking people to do different things and give them response."

Seen today: three Postgres builds queued, 0 of 4 slots running and 0 waiting while the pipeline cron was on; earlier launches failed on a broken worktree and on the dispatcher running claude-headless.sh from an old build folder (axf-molly-container-orchestrator-gate, HOME unbound); the reconciler kept bouncing a build back to the Queue every 20-30 min without launching it.

What to build:
1. Detector on the VPS (server side, no AI, no console needed): every tick, if any build is queued and free slots exist but nothing launched within N minutes, it is a stall. Record why (dispatcher not ticking, lock held, launch failed, worktree broken, wrong launcher path, account limit, slot state stale).
2. Auto-fix ladder without AI: restart the dispatcher tick, clear a stale lock or slot row, rebuild the worktree, use the launcher from /opt/axf only, try the next account; re-check after each.
3. AI fix switch: setting axf.pipeline.stall.aiFix, default OFF. When on and the no-AI ladder is used up, start one headless Claude session to diagnose and fix.
4. Group chat chatter: post each stall, each fix attempt and its result in the crew group chat, assigning the steps to named agents (who checks the lock, who rebuilds the worktree, who retries the launch) with their replies, so Brett can follow it.
5. Banner + one phone push when it can't fix it (systems check health@1 item with Auto fix).
Extend the existing stale-row watchdog / server watchdog (orchestrator-stale-row-watchdog-vps, server-watchdog-orchestrator-auto-recovers-stuck) instead of adding another cron; check for overlap first. Full API control (REST, MCP, CLI, voice) for its status, settings and the switch.

steps.text: Brett (voice, Nov 19 2026): "There needs to be something on the VPS to detect it when things are in the queue and not running … and then fix it. On its own, without AI. Or with, if the switch is on. Default off." Also: "put some chatter in the group chat asking people to do different things and give them response."

Seen today: three Postgres builds queued, 0 of 4 slots running and 0 waiting while the pipeline cron was on; earlier launches failed on a broken worktree and on the dispatcher running claude-headless.sh from an old build folder (axf-molly-container-orchestrator-gate, HOME unbound); the reconciler kept bouncing a build back to the Queue every 20-30 min without launching it.
What to build:

Detector on the VPS (server side, no AI, no console needed): every tick, if any build is queued and free slots exist but nothing launched within N minutes, it is a stall. Record why (dispatcher not ticking, lock held, launch failed, worktree broken, wrong launcher path, account limit, slot state stale).
Auto-fix ladder without AI: restart the dispatcher tick, clear a stale lock or slot row, rebuild the worktree, use the launcher from /opt/axf only, try the next account; re-check after each.
AI fix switch: setting axf.pipeline.stall.aiFix, default OFF. When on and the no-AI ladder is used up, start one headless Claude session to diagnose and fix.

Group chat chatter: post each stall, each fix attempt and its result in the crew group chat, assigning the steps to named agents (who checks the lock, who rebuilds the worktree, who retries the launch) with their replies, so Brett can follow it.
Banner + one phone push when it can't fix it (systems check health@1 item with Auto fix).

Extend the existing stale-row watchdog / server watchdog (orchestrator-stale-row-watchdog-vps, server-watchdog-orchestrator-auto-recovers-stuck) instead of adding another cron; check for overlap first. Full API control (REST, MCP, CLI, voice) for its status, settings and the switch.
Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/queue-stall-detector-vps-spots-queued.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR

builds.title: Load spike alarm: VPS detects CPU/load spikes, rings the phone, flashing banner alert that pops open
builds.detail:
Brett (voice, Nov 19 2026): "I need the VPS to detect spikes like that and get an audible alarm to the phone. And an alert in one of the banners that pops open automatically to show the flashing alert."

Seen today: load average 60 this morning, then 13-22 on an 8-core KVM 8 (srv1837178) several times; cause each time was something different (builds-live push storm, cron-spawned node scripts piling up, Coolify at 400% CPU). Everything timed out while it lasted.

What to build:
1. Detector on the VPS, server side, no console or AI needed: samples load average, CPU per container and top processes every 30-60 s. A spike = load above a threshold relative to core count (default: over 1.5x cores for 2 minutes; settings for threshold, duration, cool-down). Records the top offenders (process, container, cron that started it).
2. Audible alarm on the phone through Phone Connect (AmberX app is retired): a loud alarm-type notification that plays sound even on silent/DND where Android allows it, with the cause in the text and a tap that opens the console alert.
3. Banner alert: the systems check banner (or alerts banner) gets a flashing, high-priority item, and the banner pops open on its own to show it. The item says what spiked, how high, since when and the top offenders, with Fix actions (kill the offending process, pause the cron, restart the container) that need a confirm.
4. Clears itself and says so when load is back to normal.
5. Uses the systems check health@1 registry; flashing look comes from asset tokens. Full API control (REST, MCP, CLI, voice) for status, settings, test alarm and acknowledge.
Check overlap with the Maintenance plugin (already reads os.getloadavg) and the queue stall detector build; reuse, don't duplicate.

builds.title: Server safe mode: one emergency button that instantly sheds load on the VPS
builds.detail:
Brett (voice, Nov 19 2026): "I need an emergency button … like a safe mode button. I hit it, boom, and immediately the server shuts a whole bunch of shit down."

Seen today: load 60 this morning, 13-42 several times tonight (push storm, cron pile-ups, builds-store verify jobs re-reading the 14 MB store, Coolify at 400%). Everything timed out, including the console and the phone app.

What to build:
1. One Safe mode switch, reachable from a big button in the console banner, the phone (Phone Connect / console app, works even when the console is slow because it talks to a tiny always-on endpoint), voice and the CLI/MCP. Confirm once.
2. On: moves the non-essential crons aside (console-nightly, doctor, maintenance, watchdogs, auto-land, updaters), holds the pipeline (no new launches), pauses heavy steps (builds-store verify, model-gate audit, typechecks, vite/esbuild), optionally pauses running build sessions, and stops non-essential containers. Configurable list of what goes down and what stays.
3. Always stays up: axHub, the console server, axf-data / Postgres, Phone Connect link, SSH.
4. Off: puts back exactly what it took down, in order, and reports.
5. Shows the live picture while on: load, CPU per container, memory, swap, disk, what it stopped.
6. Hooks into the load spike alarm build: optional auto safe mode when load passes a set level.
Full API control (REST, MCP, CLI, voice).
